title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
嘉靖四年陝西鄉試巡按御
史鄭〔氣〕睠茲令典夙夜在公
先是貢院歲久弗葺乃申飭
藩司周視荒度翼而新之而
增廠美尤務脩明品式表樹
風聲士氣勃勃乎其興矣及
===
期教授林〔同〕學正范〔維恭〕以
考試官至而同考試官則教
諭許〔選〕陳〔英〕周〔謐〕路〔子泰〕冀
進〔方〕〔邦望〕以禮授館分經置
局御史鄭〔氣〕寔臨其事凜于
日監惟公惟恪合提學副使
唐〔龍〕所選士凡一千九百有
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序

嘉靖四年，陝西鄉試，巡按御史鄭〔氣〕睠茲令典，夙夜在公。先是，貢院歲久弗葺，乃申飭藩司，周視荒度，翼而新之，而增廠美，尤務脩明品式，表樹風聲，士氣勃勃乎其興矣。及期，教授林〔同〕、學正范〔維恭〕以考試官至，而同考試官則教諭許〔選〕、陳〔英〕、周〔謐〕、路〔子泰〕、冀進〔方〕〔邦望〕。以禮授館，分經置局。御史鄭〔氣〕寔臨其事，凜于日監，惟公惟恪。合提學副使唐〔龍〕所選士，凡一千九百有
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the fourth year of Jiajing [1525], for the Shaanxi Provincial Examination, Regional Inspector Zheng Qi attended to this worthy institution, devoting himself to public duty day and night. Previously, the examination compound had gone unrepaired for many years. He therefore directed the Provincial Administration Commission to inspect it thoroughly, survey and plan the work, and renovate it, making it more spacious and handsome [?]. Above all, he sought to clarify and uphold the prescribed standards and procedures and to establish an exemplary reputation. The spirits of the candidates rose with flourishing vigor.

When the appointed time arrived, Prefectural School Instructor Lin Tong and Subprefectural School Instructor Fan Weigong came to serve as Examiners. The Associate Examiners were County School Instructors Xu Xuan, Chen Ying, Zhou Mi, Lu Zitai, Ji Fang, and Jin Bangwang [the last two names are uncertain in the transcription]. They were ceremonially provided with quarters, and examining offices were established according to the individual Classics. Censor Zheng Qi personally supervised the proceedings, mindful with awe of daily scrutiny and acting with impartiality and diligence. The candidates selected by Education Intendant Tang Long, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, numbered altogether one thousand nine hundred and …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
奇明試其文槩其德行而得
六十五人蔚然三秦之良也
古昔選士或十拔五或十取
一抑以爲異矣茲乃不啻三
十取一不亦尤異乎哉〔同作〕
而颺言曰舉明揚之典者建
揆序之功崇推讓之節者廣
===
無斁之教古之人事君以人
類如此今日大者亦惟以人
已矣昔孔子語哀公曰人有
五儀有庸人有士人有君子
有賢人有聖人甚矣哉人之
不同也況厲于色或荏于內
言于靜而恒庸之違抑亦有
punctuated: 奇，明試其文，槩其德行，而得六十五人，蔚然三秦之良也。古昔選士，或十拔五，或十取一，抑以爲異矣。茲乃不啻三十取一，不亦尤異乎哉？〔同作〕而颺言曰：「舉明揚之典者，建揆序之功；崇推讓之節者，廣無斁之教。古之人事君以人，類如此。今日大者，亦惟以人已矣。昔孔子語哀公曰：『人有五儀：有庸人，有士人，有君子，有賢人，有聖人。』甚矣哉，人之不同也！況厲于色，或荏于內；言于靜，而恒庸之違，抑亦有
translation_en:
…and more. They carefully examined the candidates’ compositions and assessed their moral conduct, selecting sixty-five men—an impressive gathering of the finest talents of the Three Qin regions of Shaanxi. In antiquity, when men were selected, sometimes five were chosen out of ten, sometimes one out of ten; these were already considered exceptional selections. Now, however, fewer than one in thirty were chosen. Was this not still more exceptional?
〔Tong rose〕 and proclaimed: “Those who uphold the established practice of bringing worthy men to light accomplish the work of ordering affairs; those who honor the principle of yielding precedence to others extend tireless instruction. Such, in general, was how the ancients served their rulers by recommending men. The great task today, too, consists simply in finding the right men. Confucius once told Duke Ai: ‘There are five categories of men: ordinary men, men of learning, gentlemen, worthies, and sages.’ How profound are the differences among men! Moreover, some are stern in countenance yet perhaps weak within; some speak in tranquil circumstances yet depart from their words in everyday conduct [?]. Might there also be…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
難知者乎慎始者辨志正極
者定分考成者廣業子多士
峩然而冠也褎然而衣也不
可謂之非士人矣由是而君
子履忠信之實始仁義之美
廣通明之用油然如可企也
由是而賢人亮節砥行脩辭
===
廣業興道建治至不難矣由
是而聖人宣明德敦敬典窮
萬事協庶品撫五辰經國家
和上下亦或其庶乎乃若見
小闇大名實紛錯俛然而爲
庸人是則可憂也已夫聖人
踔乎不可及已曰君子曰賢
punctuated: 難知者乎？慎始者辨志，正極者定分，考成者廣業。子多士，峩然而冠也，褎然而衣也，不可謂之非士人矣。由是而君子，履忠信之實，始仁義之美，廣通明之用，油然如可企也。由是而賢人，亮節砥行，脩辭廣業，興道建治，至不難矣。由是而聖人，宣明德，敦敬典，窮萬事，協庶品，撫五辰，經國家，和上下，亦或其庶乎？乃若見小闇大，名實紛錯，俛然而爲庸人，是則可憂也已。夫聖人，踔乎不可及已。曰君子，曰賢
translation_en:
…those who are difficult to know? Those who take care at the outset distinguish aspirations; those who set the standard aright establish proper distinctions; those who assess accomplishments broaden undertakings. You, the many scholars, wear lofty caps and ample robes: one cannot say that you are not men of learning. From this point, to become gentlemen—to put loyalty and trustworthiness into practice, initiate the beauty of benevolence and righteousness [?], and extend the application of clear understanding—seems naturally within reach. From this point, to become worthy men—to display integrity, temper your conduct, cultivate your words and broaden your undertakings, promote the Way and establish good government—is by no means difficult to attain. From this point, to become sages—to manifest illustrious virtue, give earnest attention to the observances requiring reverence, comprehend the myriad affairs, bring all categories of things into harmony, regulate the five celestial cycles, order the state, and harmonize those above and below—might this too perhaps be approached?
But if you perceive small matters while remaining blind to great ones, confuse names and realities, and bow your heads to become ordinary men, this indeed is cause for concern. Now, sages soar beyond our reach. As for those called gentlemen and those called worthy…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人實邦之紀民之望也子多
士均之乎若人則固以君子
賢人事吾
君吾責塞矣雖然聖人亦可爲也
子多士奮而求之則名世之
德格天之業如詩書所稱者
罔獲專厥美矣又孰有大如
===
吾事
君者乎
廟堂之上庶幾曰舉能其官惟
爾之能榮之至也不幸而有
庸人厠乎内又將尤之稱匪
其人惟爾不任則何以逭厥
咎乎而子多士亦重有責矣
punctuated:
人，實邦之紀、民之望也。子多士均之乎若人，則固以君子賢人事吾君，吾責塞矣。雖然，聖人亦可爲也。子多士奮而求之，則名世之德、格天之業，如詩書所稱者，罔獲專厥美矣。又孰有大如吾事君者乎？
廟堂之上，庶幾曰：「舉能其官，惟爾之能。」榮之至也。不幸而有庸人厠乎内，又將尤之，稱：「匪其人，惟爾不任。」則何以逭厥咎乎？而子多士亦重有責矣。
translation_en:
…worthy men are truly the guiding framework of the state and the hope of the people. If you scholars measure up to such men, then I shall indeed have provided gentlemen and worthy men to serve our sovereign, and my responsibility will have been discharged. Nevertheless, sagehood too can be attained. If you scholars exert yourselves in its pursuit, then those praised in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents for virtue renowned in their age and achievements that moved Heaven will no longer possess that glory alone. What undertaking could be greater than this service of mine to the sovereign?
At court, they may then say: “Those you recommended are capable of fulfilling their offices; this is due to your ability.” That would be the highest honor. But if, unfortunately, mediocre men are found among them, the court will instead reproach me, saying: “These are not the right men; you have failed in your responsibility.” How, then, could I escape the blame? You scholars, too, thus bear a weighty responsibility.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
昔趙宣子言韓獻子於晉以
爲司馬河曲之役克不隱焉
宣子觴諸大夫曰吾舉厥也
而中乃吾今知免於罪矣子
多士毋爲庸人而及我等於
罪哉時提督邊務少傅兼太
子太傅兵部尚書楊〔一清〕昔
===
甞董學于斯遺澤動鼓篋之
化文事兼憲邦之則鎮守太
監晏〔宏〕則於斯文雅尚焉巡
撫都御史王〔藎〕廣厲儒術懋
勤風訓林〔琦〕張〔縉〕冦〔天敘〕都
督僉事鄭〔卿〕繹同聲教而不
遐遺巡按御史胡〔體乾〕吉〔棠〕
punctuated:
昔趙宣子言韓獻子於晉，以爲司馬。河曲之役，克不隱焉。宣子觴諸大夫曰：「吾舉厥也而中，乃吾今知免於罪矣。」子多士毋爲庸人而及我等於罪哉！
時提督邊務少傅兼太子太傅兵部尚書楊〔一清〕，昔甞董學于斯，遺澤動鼓篋之化，文事兼憲邦之則。鎮守太監晏〔宏〕則於斯文雅尚焉。巡撫都御史王〔藎〕廣厲儒術，懋勤風訓；林〔琦〕、張〔縉〕、冦〔天敘〕、都督僉事鄭〔卿〕，繹同聲教而不遐遺。巡按御史胡〔體乾〕、吉〔棠〕
translation_en:
Formerly, Zhao Xuanzi recommended Han Xianzi in Jin, and he was appointed Commander of the Horse. At the battle of Hequ, he proved capable and concealed nothing [?]. Xuanzi offered wine to the grandees and said: “I recommended him, and my choice was sound. Only now do I know that I am free from blame.” You scholars must not become mediocrities and thereby implicate us in blame!
At this time, Yang Yiqing, Superintendent of Frontier Affairs, Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of War, had formerly supervised education here. His enduring beneficence fostered the transforming influence of learning, and his literary undertakings also provided a model for the realm. The Regional Command Eunuch, Yan Hong, held this literary culture in refined esteem. Wang Jin, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief, vigorously promoted Confucian learning and diligently encouraged moral instruction. Lin Qi, Zhang Jin, Kou Tianxu, and Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Zheng Qing continued to extend the same civilizing instruction, neglecting no distant place. The Regional Inspectors Hu Tiqian and Ji Tang …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
王〔鼎〕協恭同德聿相厥成給
事中曹〔懷〕劉〔棋〕監察御史監
〔田〕任〔佃〕郎中林〔文〕婁〔沛〕〔志德〕
主事周〔詔〕胥將使事于境上
式覲賓興共敦嘉樂提調則
叅政楊〔叔通〕叅議李〔綽〕綜理
惟勤監試則副使趙〔載〕僉事
===
桑〔溥〕周防惟密布政使宋〔晃〕
孫〔禎〕叅政成〔文〕韓〔士奇〕副使
陳〔鼎〕高〔公韶〕翟〔鵬〕張〔宏〕叅議
王〔汝舟〕周〔鎬〕僉事姚〔文清〕周
〔汝〕勤鍾〔鍚〕李〔孟旭〕王〔鈞〕宋〔璉〕
郭〔鳳翱〕都指揮張〔鎬〕賴〔銘〕翼
襄成有力焉布政使劉〔思賢〕
punctuated: 王〔鼎〕協恭同德，聿相厥成。給事中曹〔懷〕、劉〔棋〕，監察御史監〔田〕、任〔佃〕，郎中林〔文〕、婁〔沛〕、〔志德〕，主事周〔詔〕，胥將使事于境上，式覲賓興，共敦嘉樂。提調則叅政楊〔叔通〕、叅議李〔綽〕，綜理惟勤；監試則副使趙〔載〕、僉事桑〔溥〕，周防惟密。布政使宋〔晃〕、孫〔禎〕，叅政成〔文〕、韓〔士奇〕，副使陳〔鼎〕、高〔公韶〕、翟〔鵬〕、張〔宏〕，叅議王〔汝舟〕、周〔鎬〕，僉事姚〔文清〕、周〔汝〕勤、鍾〔鍚〕、李〔孟旭〕、王〔鈞〕、宋〔璉〕、郭〔鳳翱〕，都指揮張〔鎬〕、賴〔銘〕，翼襄成，有力焉。布政使劉〔思賢〕
translation_en:
…Wang Ding, acting with them in respectful cooperation and shared purpose, helped bring the undertaking to completion. Supervising Secretaries Cao Huai and Liu Qi; Investigating Censors Jian Tian [?] and Ren Dian; Bureau Directors Lin Wen, Lou Pei, and Zhide [?; surname missing]; and Secretary Zhou Zhao were all carrying out official missions within the province. They witnessed the ceremonial selection and presentation of worthy men and together contributed to the joyful occasion.

Serving as Proctors, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Shutong and Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Li Chuo diligently managed the arrangements. Overseeing the examination, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhao Zai and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Sang Pu maintained meticulous safeguards.

Provincial Administration Commissioners Song Huang and Sun Zhen; Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Cheng Wen and Han Shiqi; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Ding, Gao Gongshao, Zhai Peng, and Zhang Hong; Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners Wang Ruzhou and Zhou Gao; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Yao Wenqing, Zhou Ruqin [?], Zhong Yang, Li Mengxu, Wang Jun, Song Lian, and Guo Feng’ao; and Regional Military Commissioners Zhang Gao and Lai Ming all contributed substantial assistance toward its successful completion. Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Sixian…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
郭〔韶〕按察使袁〔擯〕叅政潘〔埴〕
嘗效厥勞旣而遷秩行矣其
餘百執事罔不愼選以畀而
知府趙〔仲〕楊〔應奎〕則先之也
夫庶正雍雍雖秩之不同事
之與弗與要之以人事君之
心孰不皇皇如乎子多士尚
===
克念焉可也
浙江金華府儒學教授林〔同〕
謹序
punctuated:
郭〔韶〕、按察使袁〔擯〕、叅政潘〔埴〕，嘗效厥勞，旣而遷秩行矣。其餘百執事，罔不愼選以畀，而知府趙〔仲〕、楊〔應奎〕則先之也。夫庶正雍雍，雖秩之不同，事之與弗與，要之以人事君之心，孰不皇皇如乎？子多士尚克念焉可也。
浙江金華府儒學教授林〔同〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Guo Shao, Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Bin, and Administration Vice Commissioner Pan Zhi had likewise contributed their efforts, but subsequently received promotions and departed. All the other functionaries were carefully selected before being entrusted with their duties, with Prefects Zhao Zhong and Yang Yingkui taking the lead.
The various officials worked together harmoniously. Although their ranks differed, and some participated in this undertaking while others did not, whose heart was not deeply concerned with serving the sovereign by securing worthy men? You, the assembled scholars, should bear this in mind.
Preface respectfully composed by Lin Tong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四年陝西鄉試
監臨官
巡按陝西監察御史鄭氣〔浩然直隸靜海縣人　甲戌進士〕
提調官
陝西等處承宣布政使司右叅政楊鐍〔靜修浙江鄞縣人　戊辰進士〕
陝西等處承宣布政使司左叅議李緋〔廷章河南固始縣人　乙丑進士〕
監試官
陝西等處提刑按察司副使趙載〔文載山西垣曲縣人　辛未進士〕
陝西等處提刑按察司僉事桑溥〔汝公山東濮州人　甲戌進士〕
===
考試官
浙江金華府儒學教授林同〔宜正福建晉江縣人　辛酉貢士〕
湖廣岳州府澧州儒學學正詭維恭〔以莊福建長樂縣人　丙子貢士〕
同考試官
江西廣信府上饒縣儒學教諭許選〔舜徵福建漳浦縣人　庚午貢士〕
山東兗州府滋陽縣儒學教諭陳英〔碩夫福建龍溪縣人　癸酉貢士〕
山東登州府萊陽縣儒學教諭周謚〔世寧河南鈞州人　丙子貢士〕
湖廣岳州府臨湘縣儒學教諭曁泰〔巖夫江西安福縣人　壬午貢士〕
河南汝寧府光州固始縣儒學教諭龔進〔以正直隸唐山縣人　癸酉貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖四年陝西鄉試

監臨官
巡按陝西監察御史鄭氣〔浩然，直隸靜海縣人，甲戌進士〕。

提調官
陝西等處承宣布政使司右叅政楊鐍〔靜修，浙江鄞縣人，戊辰進士〕。
陝西等處承宣布政使司左叅議李緋〔廷章，河南固始縣人，乙丑進士〕。

監試官
陝西等處提刑按察司副使趙載〔文載，山西垣曲縣人，辛未進士〕。
陝西等處提刑按察司僉事桑溥〔汝公，山東濮州人，甲戌進士〕。

考試官
浙江金華府儒學教授林同〔宜正，福建晉江縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
湖廣岳州府澧州儒學學正詭維恭〔以莊，福建長樂縣人，丙子貢士〕。

同考試官
江西廣信府上饒縣儒學教諭許選〔舜徵，福建漳浦縣人，庚午貢士〕。
山東兗州府滋陽縣儒學教諭陳英〔碩夫，福建龍溪縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
山東登州府萊陽縣儒學教諭周謚〔世寧，河南鈞州人，丙子貢士〕。
湖廣岳州府臨湘縣儒學教諭曁泰〔巖夫，江西安福縣人，壬午貢士〕。
河南汝寧府光州固始縣儒學教諭龔進〔以正，直隸唐山縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shaanxi Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Jiajing (1525)

Supervising Official
Zheng Qi, Regional Inspector of Shaanxi and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Haoran and was from Jinghai County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiaxu year.

Proctors
Yang Jue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Jingxiu and was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Li Fei, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Tingzhang and was from Gushi County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Examination Inspectors
Zhao Zai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Wenzai and was from Yuanqu County, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
回也非助我者也於吾言無所不說
徵則悠遠悠遠則博厚博厚則高明
老吾老以及人之老幼吾幼以及人之幼
天下可運於掌詩云刑于寡妻至于兄
弟以御于家邦言舉斯心加諸彼而已
故推恩足以保四海
易
===
初筮告以剛中也
女正位乎內男正位乎外男女正天地之
大義也
顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂
盛德大業至矣哉
爻有等故曰物物相雜故曰文
書
地平天成六府三事允治萬世永賴時乃
功
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

回也非助我者也，於吾言無所不說。

徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。

老吾老，以及人之老；幼吾幼，以及人之幼。天下可運於掌。詩云：「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦。」言舉斯心加諸彼而已。故推恩足以保四海。

易

初筮告，以剛中也。

女正位乎內，男正位乎外。男女正，天地之大義也。

顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂，盛德大業至矣哉！

爻有等，故曰物；物相雜，故曰文。

書

地平天成，六府三事允治，萬世永賴，時乃功。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Hui is no help to me: there is nothing I say that does not please him.”

“Manifest in evidence, it becomes enduring and far-reaching; enduring and far-reaching, it becomes broad and substantial; broad and substantial, it becomes lofty and luminous.”

“Honor your own elders and extend that honor to the elders of others; care for your own young and extend that care to the young of others. Then all under Heaven can be turned in the palm of your hand. The Book of Odes says: ‘Set an example for your wife, extend it to your brothers, and thereby govern your household and state.’ This means simply taking this heart and applying it to others. Thus, extending kindness is sufficient to protect all within the Four Seas.”

Book of Changes

“‘At the first divination, an answer is given’: this is because the firm line occupies the central position.”

“The woman occupies her proper position within; the man occupies his proper position without. That man and woman should each be in their proper position is the great principle of Heaven and Earth.”

“It manifests itself in benevolence and conceals itself in its workings. It stirs the myriad things into activity without sharing the sage’s anxieties. How consummate are its abundant virtue and great undertaking!”

“The lines have ranks, and so are called ‘things’; the things intermingle, and so are called ‘patterns.’”

Book of Documents

“Earth has been brought into order, and Heaven’s work accomplished. The Six Resources and Three Affairs are truly well managed, and countless generations will forever benefit. This is your achievement.”

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
若虞機張往省括于度則釋
百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用平康
萬年厭于乃德殷乃引考王伻殷乃承敘
萬年
詩
被之僮僮夙夜在公被之祁祁薄言還歸
既見君子德音孔膠
伴奐爾游矣優游爾休矣豈弟君子俾爾
彌爾性似先公酋矣爾土宇昄章亦孔
===
之厚矣豈弟君子俾爾彌爾性百神爾
主矣爾受命長矣茀祿爾康矣豈弟君
子俾爾彌爾性純嘏爾常矣
駿發爾私終三十里亦服爾耕十千維耦
春秋
九月考仲子之宮〔隱公五年〕
六月雨〔僖公三年〕齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
楚子伐鄭〔宣公四年〕楚子伐鄭〔宣公九年〕
punctuated:
若虞機張，往省括于度，則釋。百穀用成，乂用明，俊民用章，家用平康。萬年厭于乃德，殷乃引考。王伻殷乃承敘，萬年。
詩
被之僮僮，夙夜在公；被之祁祁，薄言還歸。既見君子，德音孔膠。伴奐爾游矣，優游爾休矣。豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性。似先公酋矣，爾土宇昄章，亦孔之厚矣。豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性。百神爾主矣，爾受命長矣。茀祿爾康矣，豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性。純嘏爾常矣。駿發爾私，終三十里。亦服爾耕，十千維耦。
春秋
九月，考仲子之宮〔隱公五年〕。六月，雨〔僖公三年〕。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田〔定公十年〕。楚子伐鄭〔宣公四年〕。楚子伐鄭〔宣公九年〕。
translation_en:
As when a gamekeeper has drawn his bow: he examines whether the arrow’s nock is properly aligned, and only then releases it. Thus the hundred grains ripen, government becomes enlightened, worthy men gain recognition, and households enjoy peace and well-being. For ten thousand years may you be satisfied with your virtue and greatly prolong your life. May the king enable Yin to continue in its proper order for ten thousand years.

Book of Odes
Her headdress is stately; morning and night she attends to public duties. Her headdress sways gracefully as she returns home. Having seen the noble man, I find his virtuous words deeply binding.
At ease you wander; leisurely you rest. Gracious and kindly noble man, may you fully realize your nature. Continue the work of your former lords to its completion. Your territory is broad and illustrious, and its resources are most abundant. Gracious and kindly noble man, may you fully realize your nature. You preside over the sacrifices to the hundred spirits; long may you hold the mandate. May abundant blessings bring you peace. Gracious and kindly noble man, may you fully realize your nature. May great blessings remain yours forever.
Vigorously break up your private fields, throughout the whole thirty li. Attend also to your plowing, ten thousand working in pairs.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In the ninth month, the ancestral shrine of Zhongzi was completed and consecrated. 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin.〕
In the sixth month, it rained. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕 Men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xuan.〕 The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan.〕

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
三月取鄆〔昭公元年〕叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公〕
〔二十四年〕有鸜鵒來巢　秋七月上
辛大雩　季辛又雩〔俱昭公二十五〕
〔年〕
禮記
凡君召以三節二節以走一節以趨
禮樂刑政其極一也所以同民心而出治
道也
盡其道端其義而教生焉是故君子之事
===
君也必身行之
古之制禮也經之以天地紀之以日月參
之以三光政教之本也
第貳場
論
忠恕違道不遠
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢封丙吉等爲列矦故人阿保賜物有
差詔〔元康三年〕
punctuated:
三月，取鄆〔昭公元年〕。叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公〕〔二十四年〕。有鸜鵒來巢。秋七月，上辛大雩，季辛又雩〔俱昭公二十五〕〔年〕。
禮記
凡君召，以三節；二節以走，一節以趨。
禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。
盡其道，端其義，而教生焉。是故君子之事君也，必身行之。
古之制禮也，經之以天地，紀之以日月，參之以三光，政教之本也。
第貳場
論
忠恕違道不遠。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢封丙吉等爲列矦、故人阿保賜物有差詔〔元康三年〕。
translation_en:
In the third month, Yun was taken. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕 Shusun She returned from Jin. 〔Duke Zhao,〕〔twenty-fourth year.〕 Mynahs came to nest. In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first xin day, the great rain sacrifice was performed; on the last xin day, another rain sacrifice was performed. 〔Both in Duke Zhao’s twenty-fifth〕〔year.〕
Record of Rites
Whenever the ruler summons someone, three tokens are used; with two tokens, one runs; with one token, one walks briskly.
Rites, music, punishments, and government have a single ultimate purpose: to unite the people’s hearts and bring forth the way of good governance.
Fully realizing the Way and setting right its principles gives rise to instruction. Thus, when a gentleman serves his ruler, he must personally put these into practice.
The ancients established rites with Heaven and Earth as their framework, the sun and moon as their ordering principles, and the three luminaries as their points of reference: these are the foundation of government and instruction.
Second Session
Discourse
Conscientiousness and reciprocity are not far from the Way.
Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from among these [?].〕
Draft an edict in the voice of the Han emperor enfeoffing Bing Ji and others as ranked marquises and bestowing gifts in varying amounts upon old acquaintances and nurses and guardians. 〔Third year of Yuankang.〕

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以褚遂良爲黃門侍郎參預朝政誥
貞觀十八年
擬宋以張詠知益州得便宜從事謝表淳
化五年
判語五條
磨勘卷宗
別籍異財
奏對失敘
申報軍務
帶造段疋
===
第叁場
策五道
問帝王之道莫先於學帝王之學務得其
要先儒之言是也迯求堯舜禹湯文武
之君罔不典學不識要何在歟厥後英
君世主稱制石渠臨決白虎甚者分夜
觀書更日侍讀與夫肆力於隆冬短晷
之際其學誠勤矣然治不隆古道非粹
punctuated:
擬唐以褚遂良爲黃門侍郎、參預朝政誥。貞觀十八年。
擬宋以張詠知益州、得便宜從事謝表。淳化五年。
判語五條：磨勘卷宗；別籍異財；奏對失敘；申報軍務；帶造段疋。
第叁場
策五道
問：帝王之道，莫先於學；帝王之學，務得其要。先儒之言是也。迯求堯舜禹湯文武之君，罔不典學，不識要何在歟？厥後英君世主，稱制石渠，臨決白虎，甚者分夜觀書，更日侍讀，與夫肆力於隆冬短晷之際，其學誠勤矣。然治不隆古，道非粹
translation_en:
Draft an enfeoffment proclamation in the voice of the Tang court appointing Chu Suiliang as Vice Director of the Chancellery, participating in the administration of government. Eighteenth year of Zhenguan [644].
Draft a memorial of thanks in the voice of Zhang Yong upon his appointment by the Song court as Prefect of Yizhou, with authority to act as circumstances require. Fifth year of Chunhua [994].
Five legal judgments: reviewing case files; establishing separate household registration and dividing family property; failure to observe proper order in replies to the throne; reporting military affairs; manufacturing additional bolts of silk fabric alongside an assigned production quota [?].
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: In the way of emperors and kings, nothing takes precedence over learning; in their learning, they must grasp its essentials. These words of earlier Confucian scholars are correct. Looking back [?] to such rulers as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, none failed to devote himself to learning. Yet wherein, we ask, did its essentials lie? Subsequently, illustrious sovereigns and rulers of successive ages pronounced imperial judgments at the Stone Canal Pavilion and personally settled discussions at the White Tiger Hall. Some even set aside portions of the night to read and had readers attend them on alternate days, while others exerted themselves during the short daylight hours of deepest winter. Their diligence in learning was indeed great. Yet their government did not attain the excellence of antiquity, and their way was not pure…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
白毋乃不得其要乎洪惟我
皇上以上聖之資撫中興之運朝御
經筵退臨書幄卓乎不可尚已頃復申
命侍臣次寫詩經周易中庸及舉歷代鑑書政
要編集直解講章以備日覽及取尚書
作爲文詞或詩賦以需燕玩允矣哉帝
王之盛節
祖宗之嘉謨也天下臣工罔不稽首颺言曰太
平之業可立待乎夫詩書周易中庸皆
聖賢之言無可去取然要自在焉歷代
鑑書上下古今數千餘年不得其要尤
不可也
===
天語丁寧
帝心經畫固惟要焉是求爾而非徒務博爲也
子多士幸昌言于時將繹而獻之以爲
聖學萬一之助
問天有七曜地有四瀆七曜緯天而左旋
其躔度有遲速順逆之殊而其變也動
punctuated:
白，毋乃不得其要乎？洪惟我皇上，以上聖之資，撫中興之運，朝御經筵，退臨書幄，卓乎不可尚已。頃復申命侍臣，次寫《詩經》《周易》《中庸》，及舉歷代鑑書、政要，編集直解講章，以備日覽；及取《尚書》，作爲文詞或詩賦，以需燕玩。允矣哉，帝王之盛節、祖宗之嘉謨也！天下臣工罔不稽首颺言曰：「太平之業，可立待乎！」夫《詩》《書》《周易》《中庸》，皆聖賢之言，無可去取，然要自在焉。歷代鑑書，上下古今數千餘年，不得其要，尤不可也。天語丁寧，帝心經畫，固惟要焉是求爾，而非徒務博爲也。子多士，幸昌言于時，將繹而獻之，以爲聖學萬一之助。

問：天有七曜，地有四瀆。七曜緯天而左旋，其躔度有遲速順逆之殊，而其變也，動
translation_en:
…pure—might this not be because they failed to grasp what was essential?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor, endowed with the qualities of supreme sagehood, presides over an age of dynastic resurgence. In the morning he attends the Classics Colloquium; upon withdrawing, he enters his reading chamber. His eminence cannot be surpassed. Recently he again commanded his attendant officials to transcribe in sequence the Classic of Poetry, the Changes of Zhou, and the Doctrine of the Mean, and to draw upon historical works offering admonitory examples and essentials of government, compiling plainly explained lecture texts for his daily reading. He also commanded them to take material from the Book of Documents and compose literary pieces, poems, or rhapsodies for his enjoyment at leisure. Truly these are the splendid practices of emperors and kings and the excellent counsels of his imperial ancestors! All officials throughout the realm bow their heads to the ground and proclaim: “The achievement of great peace may be awaited forthwith!”

The Poetry, the Documents, the Changes of Zhou, and the Doctrine of the Mean all contain the words of sages and worthies. Nothing in them may be selectively accepted or discarded, yet they have their essential points. Historical works offering admonitory examples span several thousand years, from antiquity to more recent times: it is especially unacceptable to fail to grasp their essentials. The Emperor’s words are earnest, and his mind carefully considers and plans. Surely he seeks only what is essential, rather than merely striving for breadth of learning. You assembled candidates are invited to speak fully on this occasion. Your words will be examined and presented to the throne, to offer even the slightest assistance to the Emperor’s learning.

Question: Heaven has the Seven Luminaries, and earth has the Four Watercourses. The Seven Luminaries traverse heaven and revolve to the left. Their courses differ in speed and in direct or retrograde motion; and their anomalies invariably …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
關人事之吉凶四瀆經地而東逝其源
委有曲折隱見之分而其變也每係公
私之利害史冊所載可得而考也夫變
沴之來固由數之適然矣或者以爲禍
福無門惟人所召人無釁焉妖不妄作
欲君恐懼脩省者果何見歟今
聖明御極憂勤惕勵凡所以脩德弭變者無乎
不至固宜天心順應而地道底寧矣然
而四方之以變沴告者且無虛歲其故
===
何歟豈
天心仁愛不忘儆動使
聖德日進於無疆歟抑其理淵默不可得而測
識也諸士子挾策而來不可謂無見矣
試舉其變沴之見於往古何者關人事
之吉凶何者係公私之利害代舉一二
用著于篇以觀博洽之學且陳今日應
變之方以徵用世之志
問岳牧相讓用熙庶績庶官乃和大猷
punctuated:
關人事之吉凶。四瀆經地而東逝，其源委有曲折隱見之分，而其變也，每係公私之利害，史冊所載，可得而考也。夫變沴之來，固由數之適然矣。或者以爲：「禍福無門，惟人所召；人無釁焉，妖不妄作。」欲君恐懼脩省者，果何見歟？今聖明御極，憂勤惕勵，凡所以脩德弭變者，無乎不至，固宜天心順應而地道底寧矣。然而四方之以變沴告者，且無虛歲，其故何歟？豈天心仁愛，不忘儆動，使聖德日進於無疆歟？抑其理淵默，不可得而測識也？諸士子挾策而來，不可謂無見矣。試舉其變沴之見於往古，何者關人事之吉凶，何者係公私之利害，代舉一二，用著于篇，以觀博洽之學；且陳今日應變之方，以徵用世之志。

問：「岳牧相讓，用熙庶績。」「庶官乃和，大猷
translation_en:
…bear upon good and ill fortune in human affairs. The Four Watercourses traverse the earth and flow eastward. Their courses, from source to outlet, differ in their windings and turns, concealment and emergence; their anomalous changes frequently affect the welfare of both the public and private individuals. What the historical records contain can be examined. The occurrence of anomalies and calamities surely results from the contingencies of cosmic cycles. Yet some say: “Disaster and blessing have no fixed gate; people alone summon them. When people have committed no fault, baleful signs do not arise without cause.” What understanding, indeed, underlies their wish that the ruler should respond with fear, cultivate himself, and examine his conduct? Now our sage and enlightened sovereign occupies the throne, anxious and diligent, vigilant and assiduous. He leaves nothing undone in cultivating virtue and averting anomalies. Surely Heaven should respond favorably, and the workings of the earth should attain tranquility. Nevertheless, scarcely a year passes without reports of anomalies and calamities from the four quarters. Why is this? Is Heaven, in its benevolence, ever mindful of warning and stirring him, so that his sagely virtue may advance daily without limit? Or is the underlying principle so profound and silent that it cannot be fathomed? You candidates have come bearing your writings and surely have insights of your own. Cite anomalies and calamities that appeared in antiquity: which bore upon good and ill fortune in human affairs, and which affected public and private welfare? Give one or two examples from successive eras and set them down in your essays, so that we may assess the breadth and depth of your learning. Also explain how anomalies should be met today, thereby demonstrating your determination to serve the world.

Question: “The regional overseers and governors yielded precedence to one another, thereby bringing all undertakings to fruition.” “The various officials were then in harmony, and the great plan…”

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
政臣道貴于和固也自夫非怨之風既
興傾危之俗又作延蔓以迄于黨人虞
周之盛邈哉微矣若夫引車以避者志
先國家之急並坐而歡者亦以天下之
未定則僅見焉至於公言廷諍私居乃
相稱美之不暇伏閤直攻而又戮力於
平賊之舉甚者反覆相非至語人則以
兄弟呼之其或庶幾乎夫衆臣和于朝
萬物和于野固所深望于今日者然而
===
世道升降之幾亦于此乎在也茲欲上
而公卿下而百辟濟濟然師師然以復
乎虞周之盛如之何則可務詳言之毋
曰位卑而言高固不敢也
問非兵無以衛民非食無以養兵故兵制
財用二者凡有天下國家之責不可以
不講也三代之法兵農合一卓乎不可
尚已然其法至周而始備降及春秋以
至於秦其法大壞禁戍之卒俱自爲行
punctuated:
政。臣道貴于和，固也。自夫非怨之風既興，傾危之俗又作，延蔓以迄于黨人，虞周之盛邈哉微矣。若夫引車以避者，志先國家之急；並坐而歡者，亦以天下之未定，則僅見焉。至於公言廷諍，私居乃相稱美之不暇；伏閤直攻，而又戮力於平賊之舉；甚者反覆相非，至語人則以兄弟呼之，其或庶幾乎？夫衆臣和于朝，萬物和于野，固所深望于今日者。然而世道升降之幾，亦于此乎在也。茲欲上而公卿，下而百辟，濟濟然，師師然，以復乎虞周之盛，如之何則可？務詳言之，毋曰位卑而言高，固不敢也。
問：非兵無以衛民，非食無以養兵。故兵制、財用二者，凡有天下國家之責，不可以不講也。三代之法，兵農合一，卓乎不可尚已。然其法至周而始備，降及春秋，以至於秦，其法大壞，禁戍之卒俱自爲行
translation_en:
…government [?]. That harmony is prized in the conduct of ministers is surely true. Once a spirit of recrimination and resentment arose, practices of intrigue and subversion followed, spreading down to the men of the factions. How remote and faint the flourishing age of Yu and Zhou had become! Such men as the one who turned his carriage aside to avoid another, intent on putting the urgent needs of the state first, or those who sat together in amity because the realm was not yet settled, were only rarely seen. As for those who disputed openly at court yet in private could not praise one another enough; those who prostrated themselves at the palace gate to make a direct attack on another, yet joined forces with him to suppress rebels; or even those who repeatedly condemned one another yet called each other brothers when speaking to others—did they perhaps approach this ideal? Harmony among ministers at court and harmony among all things beyond it are certainly what we earnestly hope for today. Yet here, too, lies the crucial point upon which the fortunes of the age rise or fall. If we now wish all officials, from the dukes and ministers above to the multitude of officers below, to comport themselves with dignity and mutual deference, restoring the flourishing age of Yu and Zhou, how can this be achieved? Explain in detail. Do not say, “My station is low, and I would certainly not dare speak of lofty matters.”
Question: Without soldiers there is no means to defend the people; without food there is no means to sustain soldiers. Thus military organization and public finance are two matters that anyone responsible for the realm and the state must study. Under the institutions of the Three Dynasties, soldiers and farmers were one: an outstanding system that could not be surpassed. Yet this system became fully developed only under the Zhou. By the Spring and Autumn period, and subsequently the Qin, it had fallen into grave disorder. Palace guards and garrison troops alike formed their own ranks…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
伍供給之需多挽於漕運由漢而唐而
宋皆遠不及古其始也或因前代之舊
或從一時之宜規度經畫未甞不善及
其終也傳世既遠或涉於意見之偏或
沮於時勢之戹而其法之善者遂淪沒
而不存矣故所行之失雖有不同而卒
同歸於敗焉其詳可得言歟我
祖宗創制立法於兵食二者盡善盡美
聖子神孫世守之以爲法程夫何近之言兵者
===
有行伍空虛兵威不振之患言食者有
倉庾缺乏軍需不足之憂是必有其說
也今欲隨事而立法因時而救弊以復
祖宗之舊然抑豈無其道歟諸士子抱藝而來
必嘗窮其得失之源究其成敗之迹試
條陳之以觀有用之學
問朔方河西之地自漢唐以來爲中國之
版籍舊矣我
國家混一區宇以河套廣野不復戍兵而朔
punctuated:
伍，供給之需多挽於漕運。由漢而唐而宋，皆遠不及古。其始也，或因前代之舊，或從一時之宜，規度經畫未甞不善。及其終也，傳世既遠，或涉於意見之偏，或沮於時勢之戹，而其法之善者遂淪沒而不存矣。故所行之失雖有不同，而卒同歸於敗焉。其詳可得言歟？我祖宗創制立法，於兵食二者盡善盡美，聖子神孫世守之以爲法程。夫何近之言兵者，有行伍空虛、兵威不振之患；言食者，有倉庾缺乏、軍需不足之憂？是必有其說也。今欲隨事而立法，因時而救弊，以復祖宗之舊，然抑豈無其道歟？諸士子抱藝而來，必嘗窮其得失之源，究其成敗之迹。試條陳之，以觀有用之學。

問：朔方河西之地，自漢唐以來，爲中國之版籍舊矣。我國家混一區宇，以河套廣野不復戍兵，而朔
translation_en:
…ranks, while the supplies they required were largely conveyed by the grain-transport system. From the Han through the Tang to the Song, all fell far short of antiquity. At the outset, they either followed precedents inherited from the preceding dynasty or adopted measures suited to the circumstances of the time; their planning and arrangements were by no means unsound. Ultimately, however, after many generations, their sound institutions disappeared and ceased to survive, whether through biased judgments or the constraints of the times and circumstances. Thus, although their errors in implementation differed, all finally ended in failure. Can you explain the details?

Our imperial ancestors established institutions and laws that were perfect in every respect concerning both troops and provisions. Their sagely sons and divine grandsons preserved these generation after generation as authoritative standards. Why, then, do those who discuss military affairs today worry about depleted ranks and diminished military strength, while those who discuss provisions worry about empty granaries and insufficient military supplies? There must surely be an explanation. If we now wish to establish regulations suited to particular affairs and remedy abuses according to present circumstances, thereby restoring the old institutions of our imperial ancestors, surely there must be a way? You candidates have come bearing your scholarly attainments and must have investigated the sources of these successes and failures and examined the course of their achievements and defeats. Set these out point by point, so that we may assess your learning in matters of practical use.

Question: The lands of Shuofang and Hexi have long been included in China's territorial registers, ever since the Han and Tang. Our dynasty unified the realm, but because the Hetao region was a vast wilderness, it no longer stationed troops there, and Shuo…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
方遂墟酒泉以東悉改衛所而燉煌不
守是固
王者務廣德而不務廣地之意也然戎虜盤
據窺伺爲奸南牧之馬莫禁於頻馳西
征之師徒勤於大舉有志之士恒竊痛
心我思古人經營玆土開創之功保障
之績邈乎其不可及矣試舉漢唐之盛
者言之如長平之奮身奴僕七征而收
薄伐之功驃騎之勇冠諸軍六舉而奏
===
封山之捷築受降城而斥地窮荒佩四
將印而控制萬里是皆功著北鄙折衝
之虎臣也其人可歷數歟又如屯田制
勝而振金城之旅投筆勵志而揚玉關
之威洪源克敵大築京觀瓜州出守計
擢虜衆是皆名顯西方奠邦之良帥也
其人又可歷數歟宋人不競二方郡縣
相繼淪於拓跋無足言者玆欲恢朔野
之封疆因黃河爲塞以絶北虜復河右
punctuated: 方遂墟，酒泉以東悉改衛所，而燉煌不守。是固王者務廣德而不務廣地之意也。然戎虜盤據，窺伺爲奸，南牧之馬莫禁於頻馳，西征之師徒勤於大舉，有志之士恒竊痛心。我思古人經營玆土，開創之功、保障之績，邈乎其不可及矣！試舉漢唐之盛者言之：如長平之奮身奴僕，七征而收薄伐之功；驃騎之勇冠諸軍，六舉而奏封山之捷；築受降城而斥地窮荒，佩四將印而控制萬里，是皆功著北鄙、折衝之虎臣也。其人可歷數歟？又如屯田制勝而振金城之旅，投筆勵志而揚玉關之威，洪源克敵，大築京觀，瓜州出守，計擢虜衆，是皆名顯西方、奠邦之良帥也。其人又可歷數歟？宋人不競，二方郡縣相繼淪於拓跋，無足言者。玆欲恢朔野之封疆，因黃河爲塞，以絶北虜，復河右
translation_en:
…Shuofang consequently became a wasteland. East of Jiuquan, all the territory was reorganized into guards and battalions, while Dunhuang was left undefended. This surely expressed the intention of a true king, who strives to extend his virtue rather than his territory. Yet the Rong barbarians occupy these lands, watching for opportunities to cause trouble. No one can prevent their horses from repeatedly racing south to pasture, while our armies campaigning west merely exhaust themselves in large expeditions. Men of resolve constantly grieve over this in private. When I consider how the ancients developed these lands—their achievements in opening them up and securing their defenses—their accomplishments seem far beyond our reach!

Let us take outstanding examples from the Han and Tang. The Marquis of Changping rose from servitude and, in seven campaigns, won distinction in punitive expeditions. The General of Agile Cavalry surpassed all the armies in courage and, in six expeditions, achieved the victory celebrated by sacrificial rites on a mountain. One built Shouxiang Cheng, the Fortress for Receiving Surrender, and extended the territory into the remotest wilderness; another bore the seals of four generalships and exercised control over ten thousand li. These were all valiant ministers whose achievements on the northern frontier were renowned and who repelled enemy assaults. Can you enumerate these men individually?

Again, one secured victory through military agricultural colonies and brought renown to the army at Jincheng; another cast aside his writing brush, steeled his resolve, and spread his military might beyond the Jade Gate. One defeated the enemy at Hongyuan and erected great mounds of enemy corpses; another took up a defensive command at Guazhou and, through stratagem, ‘selected the enemy host’ [?]. These were all fine commanders, renowned in the west, who secured the realm. Can you enumerate these men individually as well?

The men of the Song lacked strength, and the prefectures and counties of both regions fell successively to the Tuoba. There is nothing there worth discussing. Now we wish to restore the frontiers of the northern plains, use the Yellow River as a defensive barrier to cut off the northern barbarians, and recover the lands west of the river…
