title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
回也非助我者也於吾言無所不說
張三畏
同考試官教諭方　批〔論語難言子言之　婉如當時語良工之心苦矣〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔語多出人意表說　亦深矣〕
考試官學正范　批〔自然之文可誦〕
===
考試官教授林　批〔明暢〕
聖人言大賢無所益於已以其深有契乎已也
蓋助我由於疑問顏子默契之深而無疑問矣
宜夫子致無助我之嘆也歟昔夫子之意蓋謂
天下之理有疑則有問有問則有益若顏回殆
不可以是望之乎故夫強意質疑者或得于言
論之表用力辨難者時出諸志意之先夫助我
誠多矣回也雖從游有年但見其坐忘而已未
嘗窮詰問以開有助之益于是乎補吾聰明之
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「回也非助我者也，於吾言無所不說。」
張三畏
同考試官教諭方，批〔論語難言，子言之，婉如當時語，良工之心苦矣。〕
同考試官教諭陳，批〔語多出人意表，說亦深矣。〕
考試官學正范，批〔自然之文，可誦。〕
考試官教授林，批〔明暢。〕
聖人言大賢無所益於已，以其深有契乎已也。蓋助我由於疑問，顏子默契之深而無疑問矣，宜夫子致無助我之嘆也歟！昔夫子之意，蓋謂天下之理，有疑則有問，有問則有益。若顏回，殆不可以是望之乎？故夫強意質疑者，或得于言論之表；用力辨難者，時出諸志意之先。夫助我誠多矣！回也，雖從游有年，但見其坐忘而已，未嘗窮詰問以開有助之益，于是乎補吾聰明之
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Hui is no help to me: there is nothing I say that does not delight him.”
Zhang Sanwei

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: 〔The Analects is difficult to expound. You have expressed it with a subtlety that recalls the words spoken at the time. How painstaking is the master craftsman’s care!〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The phrasing often goes beyond what one would expect, and the exposition is also profound.〕
Examiner Fan, Director of Studies, comments: 〔Natural writing, worthy of recitation.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕

The Sage said that the great worthy brought him no benefit because that worthy understood him so deeply. For helping me comes through doubts and questions; Master Yan’s tacit understanding was so profound that he had neither doubts nor questions. Was it not fitting, then, that the Master should sigh that Hui gave him no help?

The Master’s meaning on that occasion was presumably this: concerning the principles of all things under Heaven, doubts lead to questions, and questions bring benefit. Yet in Yan Hui’s case, perhaps one cannot expect this of him? Those who apply their minds intently to raising doubts [?] may reach beyond what has been said; those who strive to debate difficult points sometimes anticipate what is in my mind. Such people indeed give me much help! Hui, however, though he has studied with me for years, appears only to sit in self-forgetfulness. He has never pursued questions exhaustively so as to afford me the benefit of his assistance, thereby making up for what my perceptiveness …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所未逮俾因乎此遂悟乎彼也雖與言終日但
見其如愚而已未甞極辨說以發相長之端于
是乎廣吾智慮之所未至俾因乎往遂知乎來
也夫回豈真無知者哉蓋以其深潛具至黙之
體明睿極旁照之用凡教之所施卽懽然于不
違之際由本以之末觸處皆通無有拒而不入
者焉凡語之所及卽怡然于不惰之中由始以
之終萬境俱徹無有窒而不化者焉我以言傳
彼以心悟舉隅之論有以觸其類長之機雖口
===
之者谻拳不足以喻悅之至也我以口授彼以
意逆成德之言有以達其通微之智雖物之遇
時雨不足以喻悅之深也夫悅既深則疑自泯
疑既泯則問自忘又何助我之有哉夫子言若
有憾于回而喜之之意殆不可掩矣抑助之者
其效淺說之者其功深是故顏子誠無助于夫
子矣至於傳道之責卒歸之其諸起予之商知
來之賜皆不預焉故君子曰發聖人之蘊者顏
子也然則顏子助夫子者又豈諸弟子之所能
punctuated: 所未逮，俾因乎此遂悟乎彼也。雖與言終日，但見其如愚而已，未甞極辨說以發相長之端，于是乎廣吾智慮之所未至，俾因乎往遂知乎來也。夫回豈真無知者哉？蓋以其深潛，具至黙之體；明睿，極旁照之用。凡教之所施，卽懽然于不違之際，由本以之末，觸處皆通，無有拒而不入者焉。凡語之所及，卽怡然于不惰之中，由始以之終，萬境俱徹，無有窒而不化者焉。我以言傳，彼以心悟，舉隅之論有以觸其類長之機，雖口之者谻拳，不足以喻悅之至也。我以口授，彼以意逆，成德之言有以達其通微之智，雖物之遇時雨，不足以喻悅之深也。夫悅既深，則疑自泯；疑既泯，則問自忘，又何助我之有哉？夫子言若有憾于回，而喜之之意殆不可掩矣。抑助之者，其效淺；說之者，其功深。是故顏子誠無助于夫子矣，至於傳道之責，卒歸之。其諸起予之商、知來之賜，皆不預焉。故君子曰：「發聖人之蘊者，顏子也。」然則顏子助夫子者，又豈諸弟子之所能
translation_en:
…where my understanding falls short, enabling me, through this, to grasp that. Though I speak with him all day, I see only that he seems foolish. Never does he pursue an argument to its utmost to initiate mutual advancement, thereby extending my thought into territory it has not yet reached and enabling me, through what has gone before, to understand what is to come.

But is Hui really without understanding? In his inward depth he possesses the substance of perfect stillness; in his luminous discernment he fully exercises the capacity to illuminate all sides. Whatever instruction is imparted, he receives joyfully, without opposition. Proceeding from root to branch, he understands everything he encounters; nothing is resisted or left unassimilated. Whatever is spoken of, he receives contentedly, without flagging. Proceeding from beginning to end, he penetrates every realm; nothing remains obstructed or untransformed. I convey it in words; he grasps it in his heart. Discussion that presents one corner sets in motion his capacity to extend his understanding by analogy. Even the mouth’s delight in fine food [?] cannot convey the utmost degree of his joy. I impart it orally; he anticipates its meaning in his mind. Words concerning the perfection of virtue activate his wisdom in penetrating subtleties. Even living things receiving timely rain cannot convey the depth of his joy.

Once his joy is deep, doubts naturally vanish; once doubts vanish, questions are naturally forgotten. How, then, could he give me any help? The Master’s words seem to express disappointment in Hui, yet his delight in him can scarcely be concealed. Moreover, the effect of helping the teacher is shallow, whereas the achievement of delighting in his teaching is profound. Thus Master Yan indeed gave the Master no help; yet responsibility for transmitting the Way ultimately fell to him. Neither Shang, who ‘stimulates me,’ nor Ci, who ‘knows what is to come,’ had a share in this. Thus the gentleman says: ‘It was Master Yan who brought forth what lay within the sage.’ If so, how could the help Master Yan gave the Master have been within the capacity of the other disciples…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
及歟
徵則悠遠悠遠則博厚博厚則高明
劉儒
同考試官教諭龔　批〔德到徵字已在功業上說了作者體認不眞往往於博厚高明處將巍乎其有成功等語入講重復可厭此作只就字意上形容不假襯貼而其旨自見是用録出〕
考試官學正范　批〔文具而意足〕
===
考試官教授林　批〔疏剔字義務見本旨與槃龔陳言者異矣〕
中庸論至誠之德著於外者自馴致其盛焉蓋
德實於中自著於外而爲事業也以誠之著不
有以馴致其盛者哉中庸發明天道而有及於
至誠之功用如此且天下之理未有誠而不著
亦未有著而不盛者也聖人之誠既極其至故
其徵諸事功內之所存有以裕其外之所發漸
漬舒□而不渝於拘迫顯設于一時者足以加
punctuated:
及歟？

徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。
劉儒
同考試官教諭龔　批〔德到徵字，已在功業上說了。作者體認不眞，往往於博厚高明處，將巍乎其有成功等語入講，重復可厭。此作只就字意上形容，不假襯貼，而其旨自見，是用録出。〕
考試官學正范　批〔文具而意足。〕
考試官教授林　批〔疏剔字義，務見本旨，與槃龔陳言者異矣。〕

中庸論至誠之德，著於外者自馴致其盛焉。蓋德實於中，自著於外而爲事業也。以誠之著，不有以馴致其盛者哉？中庸發明天道，而有及於至誠之功用如此。且天下之理，未有誠而不著，亦未有著而不盛者也。聖人之誠既極其至，故其徵諸事功，內之所存有以裕其外之所發，漸漬舒□而不渝於拘迫，顯設于一時者足以加
translation_en:
…match him?

“Manifestation leads to enduring reach; enduring reach leads to breadth and depth; breadth and depth lead to loftiness and illumination.”
Liu Ru

Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor: 〔When the discussion of virtue reaches the word “manifestation,” it is already speaking of achievements. Writers who do not truly grasp this often bring phrases such as “How majestic were his accomplishments!” into their exposition of “breadth and depth” and “loftiness and illumination,” producing tiresome repetition. This composition describes only the meanings of the words themselves. Without supplementary embellishment, its purport emerges of itself; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔The composition is complete, and its meaning fully expressed.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔It elucidates and distinguishes the meanings of the words, striving to reveal their essential purport. It differs from those who recycle stale expressions [?].〕

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the virtue of utmost sincerity, once manifested outwardly, naturally develops by degrees to its fullness. For virtue, being substantial within, naturally manifests itself outwardly as undertakings and achievements. Once sincerity manifests itself, does it not have the means to develop gradually to its fullness? In elucidating the Way of Heaven, the Doctrine of the Mean thus also addresses the efficacy of utmost sincerity. Moreover, among the principles governing all under Heaven, there is no sincerity that does not manifest itself, nor any manifestation that does not attain fullness. Since the sage’s sincerity has reached its utmost perfection, when it finds expression in undertakings and achievements, what is preserved within amply sustains what issues outwardly. Gradually permeating and unfolding □, and not changing under constraint [?], what is visibly established at one time is sufficient to confer…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
惠於百世而悠遠無窮矣中之所蓄有以符其
外之所章優游暇裕而不狃於急促昭示於一
旦者足以垂休乎千載而悠遠無旣矣惟其徵
之悠遠故其積也日引月長浩浩乎廣博而不
可涯涘窺淵淵乎混淪而不可底止測旣博而
且厚也豈褊淺其局量者擬倫耶惟其積之廣
博故其發也時異歲新巍峩擻揭而壯體勢於
莫攀宣朗昭融而燦光輝於莫掩旣高而且明
也豈卑汙其氣象者彷彿耶是則見於旣足之
===
時者有不容已之機故流於旣溢之餘者有不
容掩之妙聖人之德之盛如此此其所以載物
覆物而與天地同其體用也歟大抵誠者無妄
真實之體不貳之名物之所以成始而成終者
也使天地而非此不足以爲天地聖人而非此
則無以爲聖人矣何功用之足云子思作中庸
論聖人之德而必有及於天地亦以常物之
大情惟此相爲表裏合之則無可名狀乎嗚呼
君子思者可以語誠矣
punctuated: 惠於百世，而悠遠無窮矣。中之所蓄，有以符其外之所章，優游暇裕而不狃於急促，昭示於一旦者，足以垂休乎千載，而悠遠無旣矣。惟其徵之悠遠，故其積也日引月長，浩浩乎廣博而不可涯涘窺，淵淵乎混淪而不可底止測，旣博而且厚也，豈褊淺其局量者擬倫耶？惟其積之廣博，故其發也時異歲新，巍峩擻揭而壯體勢於莫攀，宣朗昭融而燦光輝於莫掩，旣高而且明也，豈卑汙其氣象者彷彿耶？是則見於旣足之時者，有不容已之機；故流於旣溢之餘者，有不容掩之妙。聖人之德之盛如此，此其所以載物、覆物，而與天地同其體用也歟？大抵誠者，無妄真實之體，不貳之名，物之所以成始而成終者也。使天地而非此，不足以爲天地；聖人而非此，則無以爲聖人矣，何功用之足云？子思作《中庸》，論聖人之德，而必有及於天地，亦以常物之大情，惟此相爲表裏，合之則無可名狀乎？嗚呼！君子思者，可以語誠矣。
translation_en:
…bestow blessings upon a hundred generations, enduring far into the future without limit. What is stored within accords with what is manifested without: unhurried and ample, it is not constrained by haste. What is revealed in a single day suffices to bequeath blessings for a thousand years, enduring far into the future without end. Precisely because its manifestations endure, its accumulation increases day by day and month by month. Vast in its breadth, its bounds cannot be discerned; profound in its undivided wholeness, its depths cannot be fathomed. Being both broad and substantial, how could those of narrow and shallow capacity compare with it? Precisely because its accumulation is extensive, its expression changes with the seasons and is renewed with the years. Lofty and towering [?], its imposing stature rises beyond reach; radiant and luminous, its brilliance cannot be concealed. Being both lofty and bright, how could those whose bearing is low and base resemble it? Thus, what appears when fullness has been attained possesses an impulse that cannot be arrested; what flows forth once it overflows possesses a wondrous quality that cannot be concealed. Such is the flourishing virtue of the sage. Is this not why he sustains and shelters all things, sharing with Heaven and Earth their substance and function?

In general, sincerity is the substance of truth and reality, free from falsity, and the name for undivided constancy. It is that through which things achieve their beginning and their completion. Without it, Heaven and Earth would not suffice to be Heaven and Earth; without it, the sage would have no means of being a sage. What efficacy could then be spoken of? When Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean and discussed the virtue of the sage, he invariably extended his discussion to Heaven and Earth. Was this also because, in the fundamental nature of ordinary things [?], these alone form the outward and inward aspects of one another, and, united, cannot be named or described? Ah! One may speak of sincerity with the gentleman who reflects [?].

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
老吾老以及人之老幼吾幼以及人之幼
天下可運於掌詩云刑于寡妻至于兄
弟以御于家邦言舉斯心加諸彼而已
故推恩足以保四海
喬甍
同考試官教諭許　批〔此題本是心足以王說來運掌正應王字意與保四海同作者不知但指易說謬矣子獨有見且道出反本之意明白足破羣疑錄之〕
考試官學正范　批〔不事雕琢而文采自見天下之至文也〕
===
考試官教授林　批〔簡潔〕
大賢既言推恩有序者易於王天下因明推恩
有序者足以王天下甚矣推恩之有序也于是
而不失焉豈不足以王天下而且易乎孟子因
齊王之問此則以是心足以王者而告之蓋謂
致王以推恩爲大推恩以親親爲始彼是心也
何心也卽不忍之心也盡自其及物者推之親
punctuated:
老吾老，以及人之老；幼吾幼，以及人之幼。天下可運於掌。《詩》云：「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦。」言舉斯心加諸彼而已。故推恩足以保四海。
喬甍
同考試官教諭許　批〔此題本是心足以王，說來運掌正應王字，意與保四海同。作者不知，但指易說，謬矣。子獨有見，且道出反本之意，明白足破羣疑，錄之。〕
考試官學正范　批〔不事雕琢，而文采自見，天下之至文也。〕
考試官教授林　批〔簡潔。〕
大賢既言推恩有序者易於王天下，因明推恩有序者足以王天下。甚矣，推恩之有序也！于是而不失焉，豈不足以王天下而且易乎？孟子因齊王之問此，則以是心足以王者而告之。蓋謂致王以推恩爲大，推恩以親親爲始。彼是心也，何心也？卽不忍之心也。盡自其及物者推之親
translation_en:
“Treat your own elders as elders, and extend this treatment to the elders of others; cherish your own young, and extend this treatment to the young of others. The realm can then be turned in your palm. The Book of Odes says: ‘Set an example for your wife, extend it to your brothers, and thereby govern the family and the state.’ This means simply taking this heart and applying it to others. Thus, extending benevolence is sufficient to bring security to all within the Four Seas.”

Qiao Meng 喬甍

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔This topic is fundamentally about the proposition that ‘this heart is sufficient to attain true kingship.’ The expression ‘turned in your palm’ directly answers to the word ‘kingship’; its meaning is the same as ‘bring security to all within the Four Seas.’ Writers fail to understand this and explain it only in terms of ease, which is mistaken. You alone have discerned this, and have also brought out the meaning of returning to the root. Your clarity is sufficient to dispel the doubts of the many. I select this essay for inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Fan, School Instructor: 〔Without laboring over ornament, its literary brilliance emerges of itself. This is writing of the highest order.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔Concise and clear.〕

Having already said that extending benevolence in its proper order makes it easy to rule the realm as a true king, the great worthy then explains that extending benevolence in its proper order is sufficient to rule the realm as a true king. How consequential is the proper order of extending benevolence! If one does not go astray in this, would it not be both sufficient and easy to rule the realm as a true king? In response to the King of Qi’s question about this, Mencius told him that this heart was sufficient to attain true kingship. His meaning was that extending benevolence is paramount in attaining true kingship, and that extending benevolence begins with affection for one’s own kin. What is this heart? It is precisely the heart that cannot bear the suffering of others. Taking its concern for other beings and tracing it back to one’s kin [?] …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
□以仁民乎故吾有父兄必先推是心而以老
□之然後推之以及乎人之老俾人之父兄無
于不安也吾有子弟必先推是心而以幼畜之
然後推之以及乎人之幼俾人之子弟無乎不
懷也以是王天下則由近以及遠而遠者自隨
自易以及難而難者自舉不猶運於掌之易易
乎故詩有云風化之本出於閨門而儀刑之道
始於寡妻以之至兄弟則兄弟睦焉以之御家
邦則家邦治焉夫豈有他哉蓋舉乎不忍之心
而加諸寡妻兄弟家邦之間特寡妻兄弟親而
在所先也家邦踈而在所後也于是善治者誠
能推此加彼各老其老而親踈之道洽以巳及
人各幼其幼而内外之分周吾見親親仁民不
失其序老安少懷各遂其生四海尚有不保者
乎四海既保則其王也誠運掌而巳矣夫臣之
言豈誣也哉其惟反而求之斯可矣抑恩自親
親則無不易而齊王先諸愛物始有所難固也
使能因孟子之言而得反本之道吾見不忍之
punctuated: □以仁民乎？故吾有父兄，必先推是心而以老□之，然後推之以及乎人之老，俾人之父兄無于不安也。吾有子弟，必先推是心而以幼畜之，然後推之以及乎人之幼，俾人之子弟無乎不懷也。以是王天下，則由近以及遠，而遠者自隨；自易以及難，而難者自舉。不猶運於掌之易易乎？故詩有云，風化之本出於閨門，而儀刑之道始於寡妻。以之至兄弟，則兄弟睦焉；以之御家邦，則家邦治焉。夫豈有他哉？蓋舉乎不忍之心，而加諸寡妻、兄弟、家邦之間，特寡妻、兄弟親而在所先也，家邦踈而在所後也。于是善治者誠能推此加彼，各老其老，而親踈之道洽；以巳及人，各幼其幼，而内外之分周。吾見親親仁民，不失其序；老安少懷，各遂其生。四海尚有不保者乎？四海既保，則其王也誠運掌而巳矣。夫臣之言豈誣也哉？其惟反而求之，斯可矣。抑恩自親親，則無不易，而齊王先諸愛物，始有所難，固也。使能因孟子之言而得反本之道，吾見不忍之
translation_en:
…[?] and thereby act benevolently toward the people? Thus, having fathers and elder brothers, we must first extend this heart to them, treating them with the respect due to elders [?], and then extend it to the elders of others, so that no one’s fathers or elder brothers lack security. Having sons and younger brothers, we must first extend this heart to them and nurture them as the young, and then extend it to the young of others, so that no one’s sons or younger brothers lack loving care. To become king over all under Heaven through this means is to proceed from those nearby to those far away, and those far away will follow of themselves; to proceed from what is easy to what is difficult, and the difficult will be accomplished of itself. Would this not be as easy as turning something in the palm of one’s hand?

Thus, as the Book of Odes says, moral transformation originates within the household, and the practice of setting an example begins with one’s wife. Extend it to brothers, and the brothers will live in harmony; apply it to governing the household and the state, and the household and the state will be well governed. How could there be any other means? It is simply a matter of taking the heart that cannot bear others’ suffering and applying it to one’s wife, brothers, household, and state. Only, wife and brothers are close kin and therefore come first; household and state are more distant and therefore come afterward. If one skilled in governing can truly extend this feeling here and apply it there, honoring one’s own elders, the proper relations between close kin and those more distant will be harmonious. By extending care from oneself to others and cherishing one’s own young, the duties toward those within and outside the family will be fully met. I see that affection for kin and benevolence toward the people will retain their proper order; the old will enjoy security and the young loving care, each enabled to live out their lives. Could anyone within the Four Seas still fail to be protected? Once all within the Four Seas are protected, becoming king will indeed be no more than turning something in one’s palm. Could the words of your servant be false? You need only turn inward and seek this within yourself.

Moreover, when kindness begins with affection for kin, nothing is difficult. Yet the king of Qi began with care for creatures, and thus encountered difficulty: this was only to be expected. If he could follow the words of Mengzi and grasp the way of returning to the root, I see that the heart that cannot bear others’ suffering…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
心始於一物終於百姓發於齊國達於天下
其三代矣乎桼之何一切倒行而逆施之無怪
乎靦然而爲五覇之罪人也噫
易
初筮告以剛中也
沈麒
同考試官教諭方　批〔講剛中處錯綜有〕
〔體文之至也〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔融會經語宛然天〕
===
〔成得精微之體〕
考試官學正范　批〔結本爻辭說來寓〕
〔忠愛意〕
考試官教授林　批〔易義如此至矣〕
論辭得發蒙之宜以爻備發蒙之德蓋告者固
難告而有節斯益難矣非九二有剛中之德而
能然乎昔文王繫蒙之辭曰初筮告夫子以卦
體釋之以爲學非誠則不至教非中則不倫故
明者之告與不告顧蒙者之誠與不誠何如耳
punctuated:
心始於一物，終於百姓，發於齊國，達於天下，其三代矣乎！桼之何一切倒行而逆施之？無怪乎靦然而爲五覇之罪人也。噫！

易
初筮告，以剛中也。
沈麒
同考試官教諭方批〔講剛中處錯綜有〕〔體文之至也〕
同考試官教諭陳批〔融會經語宛然天〕〔成得精微之體〕
考試官學正范批〔結本爻辭說來寓〕〔忠愛意〕
考試官教授林批〔易義如此至矣〕

論辭得發蒙之宜，以爻備發蒙之德。蓋告者固難，告而有節斯益難矣。非九二有剛中之德而能然乎？昔文王繫蒙之辭曰：「初筮告。」夫子以卦體釋之，以爲學非誠則不至，教非中則不倫。故明者之告與不告，顧蒙者之誠與不誠何如耳。
translation_en:
…the heart begins with a single creature and ultimately extends to the common people; it manifests itself in Qi and reaches throughout the realm. Would this not match the Three Dynasties? Why, then, act perversely and contrary to the proper way in everything [?]? No wonder he shamelessly becomes an offender even by the standards of the Five Hegemons. Alas!

Book of Changes
“At the first divination, I give instruction, because of firmness and centrality.”
Shen Qi

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of firmness and centrality interweaves its themes with structure: the height of literary composition.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The language of the classic is integrated as though naturally formed, capturing its subtle essence.”
Examiner Fan, School Instructor, comments: “The conclusion develops its explanation from the line statement, conveying sentiments of loyalty and loving concern.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “An interpretation of the Changes such as this has reached perfection.”

The statement is discussed as expressing the proper way to enlighten the ignorant, for the line possesses fully the virtues needed to enlighten them. Giving instruction is certainly difficult; giving instruction with due restraint is still more difficult. Is it not because the Nine in the Second Place possesses the virtues of firmness and centrality that it can accomplish this? In former times, King Wen appended to the hexagram Meng, ‘Youthful Ignorance,’ the statement: ‘At the first divination, I give instruction.’ The Master explained this through the structure of the hexagram, holding that learning without sincerity cannot attain its goal, and teaching without centrality cannot follow its proper order. Thus, whether the enlightened person gives instruction depends simply on whether the ignorant person is sincere.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
飾僞飾非拒諫之心則剛中之賢終亦必去
而已乎是不可也故曰蒙有君臣之道也
爻有等故曰物物相雜故曰文
王乾元
同考試官教諭方　批〔文物處體認獨真〕
〔蓋留心於理學者錄之〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔曰物曰文亦見易〕
〔書廣大悉備處此作良是結以聖人用易立〕
〔說尤出人意表〕
考試官學正范　批〔說理文字匪詞辭〕
〔達而已〕
考試官教授林　批〔能發傳易者之旨〕
===
大傳論易有卽畫之殊而爲言者有卽畫之間
而爲言者夫畫殊而物自分畫間而文自著也
何莫而非道之所寓乎宜大傳言之以示人也
其意蓋謂三才之道變動於六爻而六爻之變
則各有所適卽其畫之殊者而言之三五同功
若無可區別矣然而一貴一賤凜然尊卑之攸
punctuated:
飾僞飾非，拒諫之心，則剛中之賢終亦必去而已乎？是不可也。故曰：「蒙有君臣之道也。」

「爻有等，故曰物；物相雜，故曰文。」
王乾元
同考試官教諭方，批〔文物處體認獨真，〕〔蓋留心於理學者，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭陳，批〔曰物曰文，亦見易〕〔書廣大悉備處。此作良是，結以聖人用易立〕〔說，尤出人意表。〕
考試官學正范，批〔說理文字，匪詞辭〕〔達而已。〕
考試官教授林，批〔能發傳易者之旨。〕

大傳論易，有卽畫之殊而爲言者，有卽畫之間而爲言者。夫畫殊而物自分，畫間而文自著也，何莫而非道之所寓乎？宜大傳言之以示人也。其意蓋謂三才之道變動於六爻，而六爻之變則各有所適。卽其畫之殊者而言之，三五同功，若無可區別矣。然而一貴一賤，凜然尊卑之攸
translation_en:
…to cloak falsehood and cloak wrongdoing, with a heart that rejects remonstrance—must the worthy man of firmness and centrality ultimately do nothing but leave? This is unacceptable. Thus it is said: “The hexagram Meng contains the Way of ruler and minister.”

“The lines have grades; hence they are called ‘things.’ Things intermingle; hence they are called ‘patterns.’”
By Wang Qianyuan.

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of ‘patterns’ and ‘things’ is exceptionally true. He is evidently someone who applies himself to the Learning of Principle; select this essay.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The expressions ‘things’ and ‘patterns’ also reveal the breadth and comprehensiveness of the Book of Changes. This essay is very sound. Its conclusion, which grounds the argument in the sages’ use of the Changes, is especially unexpected.”
Examiner Fan, School Director, comments: “This writing expounds principle; it does more than merely convey its meaning in words [?].”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “It succeeds in bringing out the intent of those who transmitted the Changes.”

In discussing the Changes, the Great Commentary sometimes speaks in terms of distinctions among the lines, and sometimes in terms of the relations between them. Through distinctions among the lines, things naturally become differentiated; through the relations between the lines, patterns naturally become manifest. In what instance is the Way not embodied? Fittingly, the Great Commentary speaks of these matters to instruct people.

Its meaning is, presumably, that the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—changes and moves within the six lines, while the transformations of the six lines each have their own direction. Speaking in terms of distinctions among the lines, the third and fifth perform the same function, seemingly without anything to distinguish them. Yet one is noble and the other lowly, and there is an awe-inspiring distinction of superior and inferior …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
彼人之初筮盥而顒若精神則方聚也問焉以
言誠意則未散也方童蒙求我至純無雜竭齋
戒於洗心之時儼如蓍龜之在前焉至一無二
充有孚於盈缶之際宛如神明之在上焉是不
有初筮之誠者乎由是扣之則鳴啓以果行育
德之方受之如嚮亦以正法禦寇之道夫告之
如此而豈徒哉蓋君子之德以剛爲明剛之不
足則無告之之本以中爲節中之不至則失告
之之宜卦之二得乎九蓋有剛之德焉剛乃明
===
之所由生也九居二蓋有中之德焉中乃節
之所由出也吾見因材而篤待問之資必加於
積誠之士固未嘗不惓惓然而妄告者綜寡矣擇
可而施不拒之教必授於篤信之人固未嘗吝
教然而輕教者亦無矣夫學者以誠則學得其
道教者以中則教得其道發蒙之道於斯至矣
雖然蒙有君臣之道也是故幼冲之君迪知有
德者勿疑勿貳盡誠以順聽之庶彼得以盡輔
相之道翼之而爲百代之令主殆不難矣苟詘
punctuated:
彼人之初筮，盥而顒若，精神則方聚也；問焉以言，誠意則未散也。方童蒙求我，至純無雜，竭齋戒於洗心之時，儼如蓍龜之在前焉；至一無二，充有孚於盈缶之際，宛如神明之在上焉。是不有初筮之誠者乎？由是扣之則鳴，啓以果行育德之方；受之如嚮，亦以正法禦寇之道。夫告之如此，而豈徒哉？蓋君子之德，以剛爲明，剛之不足，則無告之之本；以中爲節，中之不至，則失告之之宜。卦之二得乎九，蓋有剛之德焉，剛乃明之所由生也；九居二，蓋有中之德焉，中乃節之所由出也。吾見因材而篤，待問之資必加於積誠之士，固未嘗不惓惓，然而妄告者綜寡矣；擇可而施，不拒之教必授於篤信之人，固未嘗吝教，然而輕教者亦無矣。夫學者以誠，則學得其道；教者以中，則教得其道。發蒙之道，於斯至矣。
雖然，蒙有君臣之道也。是故幼冲之君，迪知有德者，勿疑勿貳，盡誠以順聽之，庶彼得以盡輔相之道，翼之而爲百代之令主，殆不難矣。苟詘
translation_en:
When that person first consults the oracle, he washes his hands and assumes a reverent bearing: his spiritual energies are just then concentrated. When he puts his question into words, his sincere intent has not yet dispersed. Just as the youthful and unenlightened pupil seeks me out, he is utterly pure and unmixed. He observes purification and abstinence to the utmost as he cleanses his heart, solemnly acting as though the milfoil stalks and tortoise shell were before him. Utterly single-minded, without divided intent, he fills himself with sincerity as one fills an earthenware vessel, as though divine spirits were above him. Does he not possess the sincerity of the first consultation? Thus, when tapped, one sounds in response, enlightening him with methods for making his conduct resolute and nurturing virtue. He receives this like an echo, also through the way of setting standards right and warding off marauders. Can instruction given in this manner be without foundation?
The gentleman’s virtue takes firmness as the basis of clarity. If firmness is insufficient, he lacks the foundation for giving instruction. It takes centrality as its measure. If centrality is not attained, his instruction loses its appropriateness. The hexagram’s second place has a nine and therefore possesses the virtue of firmness: firmness is what gives rise to clarity. The nine occupies the second place and therefore possesses the virtue of centrality: centrality is what gives rise to proper measure. I see that, in nurturing people according to their capacities, the resources held ready for their questions will surely be bestowed upon scholars who have accumulated sincerity. There is certainly never any lack of earnest concern, yet instances of indiscriminate instruction are few [?]. In selecting suitable recipients and imparting instruction, teaching that turns no one away will surely be given to those of steadfast faith. There is certainly never any withholding of instruction, yet neither is there any careless teaching. If learners proceed with sincerity, their learning follows its proper way; if teachers proceed with centrality, their teaching follows its proper way. The way of enlightening the ignorant reaches its fullest expression here.
Nevertheless, the hexagram Meng, Youthful Ignorance, also contains the way governing ruler and minister. Thus, when a young ruler comes to recognize those who possess virtue, he should neither doubt them nor waver, but listen to them obediently with complete sincerity. They may then fully exercise their role of assistance and guidance. Helping him become an excellent ruler for a hundred generations should scarcely be difficult. If he bends …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
分二四同德若無所差等矣然而一遠一近截
然内外之頻異爻之有等如此是盖以不易之
位而寓夫不齊之情一物各具一理焉因所變
之名而隱乎至賾之象一物各取一義焉謂之
曰物則理寓乎器而有可名器乘乎理而有可
執是非道之散殊者乎即其畫之間者而言之
三陰三陽雜布於六虛之間序不紊而體則殊
一剛一柔錯陳於一卦之内位不出而質自異
物之相雜如此殆見經之以陽而緯之以陰參
===
伍以散其章錯之以奇而綜之以偶彌綸以合
其變謂之曰文則無色之賁固非苟合闇然之
章不假外飾是非道之昭著者乎吁文之等物
之雜而爲物爲文道之變動於六爻著如此易
之廣大悉備不於是而益可見哉抑論天地之
間陰陽而已爻之等陰陽不易之分也爻之文
陰陽不秘之精也聖人因其等而辨上下定民
志因其文而察時變化天下則易書與天地準
聖人又與易書準也易其聖人彌綸天地之道
punctuated: 分。二四同德，若無所差等矣；然而一遠一近，截然内外之頻異，爻之有等如此。是盖以不易之位而寓夫不齊之情，一物各具一理焉；因所變之名而隱乎至賾之象，一物各取一義焉。謂之曰物，則理寓乎器而有可名，器乘乎理而有可執，是非道之散殊者乎？即其畫之間者而言之，三陰三陽，雜布於六虛之間，序不紊而體則殊；一剛一柔，錯陳於一卦之内，位不出而質自異。物之相雜如此，殆見經之以陽而緯之以陰，參伍以散其章，錯之以奇而綜之以偶，彌綸以合其變。謂之曰文，則無色之賁固非苟合，闇然之章不假外飾，是非道之昭著者乎？吁！文之等、物之雜，而爲物爲文，道之變動於六爻著如此，《易》之廣大悉備，不於是而益可見哉？抑論天地之間，陰陽而已。爻之等，陰陽不易之分也；爻之文，陰陽不秘之精也。聖人因其等而辨上下，定民志；因其文而察時變，化天下。則《易》書與天地準，聖人又與《易》書準也。《易》其聖人彌綸天地之道
translation_en:
… distinctions of rank. The second and fourth lines share the same virtue, seemingly without any difference in standing. Yet one is distant and the other near, distinctly different as inner and outer [?]: such are the gradations among the lines. Thus, unchanging positions embody unequal circumstances, and each thing possesses its own principle. The names arising from change conceal profoundly intricate images, and each thing takes on its own significance. When these are called “things,” principle inheres in concrete forms and can be named, while concrete forms rest upon principle and can be apprehended. Is this not the Way dispersed in its diverse manifestations?

Speaking of what lies among the strokes, three yin and three yang lines are interspersed among the six positions: their sequence is orderly, but their forms differ. Hard and soft lines are intermingled within a single hexagram: they remain within their positions, yet their qualities differ of themselves. Such is the intermingling of things. We may discern yang as the warp and yin as the weft, combined in threes and fives to display their patterns; odd numbers interlaced and even numbers drawn together, comprehensively interwoven to unite their transformations. When this is called “pattern,” its colorless adornment is certainly no haphazard conjunction, and its unobtrusive pattern requires no external embellishment. Is this not the Way made manifest?

Ah! The gradations of pattern and the intermingling of things, constituting things and patterns—the Way’s changes and movements are thus manifest in the six lines. Does this not make the vastness and completeness of the Book of Changes still more apparent? Indeed, all that lies between Heaven and Earth is simply yin and yang. The gradations among the lines are the unchanging distinctions of yin and yang; the patterns of the lines are the essence of yin and yang openly revealed. Following these gradations, the sage distinguishes above from below and settles the people’s aspirations; following these patterns, he observes changes in the times and transforms all under Heaven. Thus the Book of Changes accords with Heaven and Earth, and the sage in turn accords with the Book of Changes. Surely the Book of Changes is that through which the sage comprehensively orders the Way of Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者乎
書
若虞機張往省括于度則釋
喬世寧
同考試官教諭許　批〔儉德永圖必奠而後發子能就虞人寫出讀之不覺躍然〕
考試官學正范　批〔假虞人之意寓告戒之私使伊尹自言不過如此〕
考試官教授林　批〔整潔〕
===
大臣告君謹德永圖之功必慮之善而動之時
也蓋慮之能善則動之斯時也大臣啓告於君
必譬諸射焉得非欲其易曉歟伊尹告太甲之
意謂夫王之欲縱蓋奢侈失之而無長遠之慮
者儉德永圖固當知所務矣然豈無所事事哉
譬之虞人然弦木爲弩其弩有機剡木爲矢其
矢有括時乎有事於田也弩機既張矢可發矣
然猶以爲奏功雖在於舉發之後經營謀則始於
捨決之初使括乖于度不致審焉能無空發乎
punctuated:
者乎？

書
「若虞機張，往省括于度，則釋。」
喬世寧
同考試官教諭許　批〔儉德永圖，必奠而後發。子能就虞人寫出，讀之不覺躍然。〕
考試官學正范　批〔假虞人之意，寓告戒之私，使伊尹自言，不過如此。〕
考試官教授林　批〔整潔。〕

大臣告君謹德永圖之功，必慮之善而動之時也。蓋慮之能善，則動之斯時也。大臣啓告於君，必譬諸射焉，得非欲其易曉歟？伊尹告太甲之意，謂夫王之欲縱，蓋奢侈失之，而無長遠之慮者。儉德永圖，固當知所務矣，然豈無所事事哉？譬之虞人然，弦木爲弩，其弩有機；剡木爲矢，其矢有括。時乎有事於田也，弩機既張，矢可發矣。然猶以爲奏功雖在於舉發之後，經營謀則始於捨決之初。使括乖于度，不致審，焉能無空發乎？
translation_en:
…is it not?

Book of Documents
“If, like a forester, you have cocked the crossbow, first examine whether the arrow’s notch accords with the proper measure; only then release it.”
Qiao Shining

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “In cultivating frugality and planning for the long term, one must establish a firm basis before letting fly. You have brought this out through the forester’s example; reading it, one cannot help feeling it spring to life.”
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “He draws upon the forester’s example to convey the heartfelt concern behind the admonition. Were Yi Yin to speak for himself, he could do no better.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Orderly and clean.”

A great minister tells his ruler that success in attending carefully to virtue and planning for the long term requires sound deliberation and timely action. For if deliberation is sound, action will be timely. When a great minister instructs his ruler, he necessarily draws an analogy with shooting: surely this is to make his meaning readily understood? Yi Yin’s intention in admonishing Tai Jia was to say that the king had given free rein to his desires, going astray through extravagance and lacking any consideration for the distant future. In cultivating frugality and planning for the long term, he certainly ought to know what to strive for. Yet could this mean there was nothing he needed to do?

Take the forester as an analogy. Wood is strung to make a crossbow, and the crossbow has a trigger mechanism; wood is sharpened to make an arrow, and the arrow has a notch. When it is time to hunt, once the crossbow is cocked, the arrow can be shot. Yet the forester still considers that, although success comes only after the shot, planning and deliberation begin at the outset, before release. If the notch deviates from the proper measure and he does not examine it thoroughly, how can he avoid shooting in vain?

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時乎有事於彍也弩機既撤矢可舍矣然猶以
爲擇全雖在於盈庖之後用巧實眆於釋掤之
先使括違于度不加察焉能無虛舍乎故當其
機之張也必殫厥心思于以審其括之合于度
歟否歟謀出萬全務使低昂之勢不乖乎準望
之宜然後發焉則中必應弦發斯不空矣當其
機之既撤也必竭乃目力于以察其括之適于
度歟否歟慮無遺巧務使疾徐之妙不違乎發
動之由然後舍焉則中必飲羽舍斯不虛矣是
===
則王之儉德永圖在於欽止率祖省括于度則
厥止可欽乃祖可率矣其所事事尚有餘蘊哉
大抵事必有法舍法則無可行省括于度射之
法也欽止率祖謹德永圖之法也使德非欽止
雖有賢聖無所庸其力射非省括雖有良工無
以施其巧矣伊尹欲太甲脩德悔過而必譬諸
射豈非假粗明精俾其言得而易入歟厥後太
甲果能克終允德爲商令王謂非伊尹告教之
功下可
punctuated:
時乎有事於彍也，弩機既撤，矢可舍矣。然猶以爲擇全雖在於盈庖之後，用巧實眆於釋掤之先。使括違于度，不加察，焉能無虛舍乎？故當其機之張也，必殫厥心思，于以審其括之合于度歟否歟，謀出萬全，務使低昂之勢不乖乎準望之宜，然後發焉，則中必應弦，發斯不空矣。當其機之既撤也，必竭乃目力，于以察其括之適于度歟否歟，慮無遺巧，務使疾徐之妙不違乎發動之由，然後舍焉，則中必飲羽，舍斯不虛矣。是則王之儉德永圖，在於欽止率祖；省括于度，則厥止可欽，乃祖可率矣。其所事事，尚有餘蘊哉？
大抵事必有法，舍法則無可行。省括于度，射之法也；欽止率祖，謹德永圖之法也。使德非欽止，雖有賢聖，無所庸其力；射非省括，雖有良工，無以施其巧矣。伊尹欲太甲脩德悔過，而必譬諸射，豈非假粗明精，俾其言得而易入歟？厥後太甲果能克終允德，爲商令王，謂非伊尹告教之功，下可。
translation_en:
When the time comes to draw the bow, the crossbow’s trigger mechanism has been disengaged and the arrow can be released. Yet one still considers that, although selecting whole game [?] takes place after the kitchen has been filled, the exercise of skill actually begins [?] before the quiver cover is removed. If the arrow’s nock departs from the prescribed measure and one fails to inspect it, how can one avoid releasing the arrow in vain? Thus, when the mechanism is cocked, one must exhaust one’s powers of thought to examine whether the nock conforms to the prescribed measure. One must plan with complete assurance, taking care that the angle, whether lowered or raised, accords with proper aim. Only then should one shoot: the hit will follow the sounding of the string, and the shot will not be wasted. Once the mechanism has been disengaged, one must exert one’s vision fully to inspect whether the nock fits the prescribed measure. In deliberation, no point of skill may be overlooked; one must ensure that the delicate adjustment of speed accords with the principles governing release. Only then should one let fly: the arrow will strike and bury itself up to its feathers, and its release will not be in vain. Accordingly, the king’s cultivation of frugal virtue and planning for the long term depend on reverently attending to his conduct and following his ancestors. By examining the nock against the prescribed measure, he can make his conduct reverent and follow his ancestors. Is there any further implication left unexplored in what he must do?
In general, every undertaking must have a standard; abandon that standard, and there is no way to proceed. Examining the nock against the prescribed measure is the standard for archery. Reverently attending to one’s conduct and following one’s ancestors are the standards for being heedful of virtue and planning for the long term. If the cultivation of virtue does not involve reverent attention to conduct, even sages and worthies have nowhere to apply their efforts. If archery does not involve inspecting the nock, even a skilled craftsman has no means of exercising his ingenuity. Yi Yin wished Taijia to cultivate virtue and repent his faults, and therefore insisted on drawing an analogy with archery. Was this not to use something simple to illuminate something subtle, so that his words could be understood and readily taken to heart? Thereafter, Taijia indeed succeeded in remaining truly virtuous to the end and became an excellent king of Shang. To say that this was not the achievement of Yi Yin’s admonition and instruction would be impossible [?].

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
萬年厭于乃德殷乃引考王伻殷乃承敘
萬年
桑蓁
同考試官教諭許　批〔道出周公忠愛之意宛然可掬短晷之下有是哉子亦奇矣〕
考試官學正范　批〔冲澹中能道出人所不到底意可錄〕
考試官教授林　批〔文有則而意亦完如子之言周公之心慰矣〕
===
大臣祝願於君福之所及者遠責難於君化之
所及者遠甚矣人臣之事君動以遠大相期也
況周公之輔成王其所以責願之者不以是爲
心哉昔周公因成王行命寧之禮而祝告於先
王及此意謂王既不忘乎我我其敢忘乎王是
故福之止於一人者不若及於家國之爲遠也
我之祝福於王豈徒惠篤敘於今日而已哉殆
必使繼王之後而爲之子孫者皆厭乎祖德之
厥瓜瓞綿綿麗以億計也而篤不忘以永孝思
punctuated:
萬年厭于乃德，殷乃引考。王伻殷乃承敘萬年。

桑蓁

同考試官教諭許，批〔道出周公忠愛之意，宛然可掬。短晷之下有是哉！子亦奇矣！〕
考試官學正范，批〔冲澹中能道出人所不到底意，可錄。〕
考試官教授林，批〔文有則而意亦完。如子之言，周公之心慰矣。〕

大臣祝願於君，福之所及者遠；責難於君，化之所及者遠。甚矣，人臣之事君，動以遠大相期也！況周公之輔成王，其所以責願之者，不以是爲心哉？昔周公因成王行命寧之禮，而祝告於先王，及此意謂：王既不忘乎我，我其敢忘乎王？是故福之止於一人者，不若及於家國之爲遠也。我之祝福於王，豈徒惠篤敘於今日而已哉？殆必使繼王之後而爲之子孫者，皆厭乎祖德之厥，瓜瓞綿綿，麗以億計也，而篤不忘以永孝思
translation_en:
“For ten thousand years they shall be satisfied with your virtue, and the people of Yin shall enjoy prolonged longevity. Let the king cause the people of Yin to continue in orderly succession for ten thousand years.”

Sang Zhen

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔The Duke of Zhou’s loyal affection is expressed so vividly that one can almost grasp it. To produce this in so little time! You are indeed remarkable!〕
Examiner Fan, School Instructor, comments: 〔With quiet simplicity, this conveys meanings others have not reached. Worth selecting.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔The composition has sound form, and its meaning is fully developed. Were things as you describe them, the Duke of Zhou’s heart would be comforted.〕

When a great minister offers good wishes for his ruler, the blessings extend far; when he demands difficult accomplishments of his ruler, the transforming influence extends far. How profoundly a minister, in serving his ruler, sets far-reaching and lofty expectations for him in everything! How much more so in the Duke of Zhou’s assistance to King Cheng: could his demands and wishes for the king have had any other purpose?

Formerly, when King Cheng performed the rite of issuing commands for pacification [?], the Duke of Zhou offered prayers to the former kings and touched upon this meaning, as if to say: “Since the king has not forgotten me, how could I dare forget the king?” Thus blessings confined to one person do not reach as far as those extending to the royal house and the state. In praying for blessings upon the king, would I seek merely that he graciously establish a firm order of succession today? Surely I must ensure that the descendants who succeed the king all receive their fill of their ancestor’s virtue [?], their lineage continuing like an unbroken succession of great and small melons, their numbers reckoned in hundreds of millions, and that, steadfast and never forgetting, they perpetuate their filial devotion …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者非一世夤斯蟄蟄年以萬言也而引弗替以
繩令武者如一時抑豈徒無邁疾於一身而已
哉殆必使從王於周而爲夫殷庶者皆享夫壽
考之休荷化國之日舒而祿貞茹醇恒見其康
彊感和氣之時至而登耆耇躋耋耄罔罹乎短折若
然則福之所及者遠矣然猶以治殷之責雖在
於我而化殷之本實係於王故當介使之歸効
責難之意以爲化之行於一時者不若垂之世
代之爲久也彼比臣之義起殷民之節性邁矣
===
而不能必其不遷王其懷可久之圖以躬行之
實數而爲條教之詳于以使之敬受而不違則
節性庶乎其日邁而奕世如一時也謹毖之命
申殷民之放心收矣而不能保其不變王其思
善導之術以心得之微形而爲訓典之懿于以
使之傾聽而不忽則放心庶乎其永收而萬年
同一日也若然則化之所及者遠矣吁視顧之
誠方切而責難之意遂繼老成之輔幼主其忠
愛有如是夫大抵人臣之事君貴忠愛之兩盡
punctuated: 者非一世。夤斯蟄蟄，年以萬言也，而引弗替以繩令武者如一時。抑豈徒無邁疾於一身而已哉？殆必使從王於周而爲夫殷庶者，皆享夫壽考之休，荷化國之日舒，而祿貞茹醇，恒見其康彊；感和氣之時至，而登耆耇，躋耋耄，罔罹乎短折。若然，則福之所及者遠矣。然猶以治殷之責雖在於我，而化殷之本實係於王，故當介使之歸，効責難之意，以爲化之行於一時者，不若垂之世代之爲久也。彼比臣之義起，殷民之節性邁矣，而不能必其不遷。王其懷可久之圖，以躬行之實，數而爲條教之詳，于以使之敬受而不違，則節性庶乎其日邁，而奕世如一時也。謹毖之命申，殷民之放心收矣，而不能保其不變。王其思善導之術，以心得之微，形而爲訓典之懿，于以使之傾聽而不忽，則放心庶乎其永收，而萬年同一日也。若然，則化之所及者遠矣。吁！視顧之誠方切，而責難之意遂繼。老成之輔幼主，其忠愛有如是夫！大抵人臣之事君，貴忠愛之兩盡。
translation_en:
…those who steadfastly remember and perpetuate their filial devotion will extend beyond a single generation. Reverently flourishing in multitudes [?], they will number their years in tens of thousands; yet those who continue without interruption to follow their ancestor’s worthy footsteps will act as though they belonged to a single age. Moreover, could the wish be merely that the king himself should suffer no affliction [?]? Surely it must also ensure that all the common people of Yin who follow the king under Zhou enjoy the blessings of longevity. Benefiting from the leisurely days of a realm transformed by moral influence, receiving blessings and imbibing its wholesome goodness [?], they will continually enjoy health and strength. Responding to the timely arrival of harmonious influences, they will attain venerable old age, reaching their seventies, eighties, and nineties, without suffering premature death. If so, the reach of these blessings will indeed be far.

Yet the Duke of Zhou still considered that, although responsibility for governing Yin rested with himself, the foundation for transforming Yin truly depended on the king. Therefore, when the emissary returned, he expressed his intention of holding the king to demanding standards: moral transformation carried out in a single age could not equal in duration that transmitted through successive generations. When the principle of aligning oneself as a minister was set forth [?], the people of Yin advanced in restraining their dispositions; yet there was no certainty that they would not waver. Let the king therefore cherish a plan that can endure, and articulate the substance of his own conduct in detailed provisions for instruction [?], so that they will receive these reverently and not disobey. Then their restraint of their dispositions may advance daily, and successive generations may act as though they belonged to a single age.

When the command to exercise vigilance and caution was reiterated, the wandering hearts of the people of Yin were brought back; yet there was no assurance that they would not change. Let the king therefore consider effective means of guidance, giving the subtle insights gained in his own heart expression in excellent written instructions, so that they will listen attentively and not disregard them. Then their wandering hearts may remain gathered in forever, and ten thousand years may be as a single day. If so, the reach of moral transformation will indeed be far.

Ah! Just as his sincere solicitude became most earnest, his intention of holding the ruler to demanding standards followed upon it. Such were the loyalty and affection with which this seasoned elder assisted his young sovereign! In general, what matters in a minister’s service to his ruler is that both loyalty and affection be fully realized.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
使徒知愛而不責難則爲婦寺之忠徒知忠而
不愛則無惻怛之實名爲忠而實非忠也周公
因成王之毖殷既爲之祝福而猶不忘責難之
恭則忠本於愛此其忠所以爲至而非夫人之
所能及也後之爲人臣者盍亦知所監哉
詩
伴奐爾游矣優游爾休矣豈弟君子俾爾
彌爾性似先公酋矣爾土宇昄章亦孔
之厚矣豈弟君子俾爾彌爾性百神爾
主矣爾受命長矣茀祿爾康矣豈弟君
子俾爾彌爾性純嘏爾常矣
===
糟壽
同考試官教諭龔　批　雅義塲中類能言
之語意鮮整而不失齋莊之體僅見此篇録
之以範作者
考試官學正范　批　寫出召公卷阿上
歆動成王之意讀之灑然噫吾子他日向用
必知所從事者矣
punctuated:
使徒知愛而不責難，則爲婦寺之忠；徒知忠而不愛，則無惻怛之實，名爲忠而實非忠也。周公因成王之毖殷，既爲之祝福，而猶不忘責難之恭，則忠本於愛。此其忠所以爲至，而非夫人之所能及也。後之爲人臣者，盍亦知所監哉！

詩
伴奐爾游矣，優游爾休矣。豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性，似先公酋矣。爾土宇昄章，亦孔之厚矣。豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性，百神爾主矣。爾受命長矣，茀祿爾康矣。豈弟君子，俾爾彌爾性，純嘏爾常矣。

糟壽

同考試官教諭龔　批：雅義，塲中類能言之；語意鮮整而不失齋莊之體，僅見此篇。録之以範作者。

考試官學正范　批：寫出召公《卷阿》上歆動成王之意，讀之灑然。噫！吾子他日向用，必知所從事者矣。
translation_en:
…If one knows only affection and does not demand difficult achievements of the ruler, one’s loyalty is that of palace women and eunuchs. If one knows only loyalty without affection, one lacks the substance of heartfelt concern: this is loyalty in name but not in reality. When the Duke of Zhou responded to King Cheng’s cautious handling of the people of Yin, he not only pronounced blessings upon him but still remembered the reverence expressed in demanding difficult achievements of him. His loyalty was thus rooted in affection. This is why his loyalty reached the highest degree, beyond what ordinary people could attain. Should not those who serve as ministers in later ages also recognize the example they ought to follow?

Book of Poetry
At ease you roam; leisurely you rest. Gracious and amiable lord, may you fulfill your allotted span and carry on the work of your former dukes to completion. Your territory is broad and distinguished; its extent is indeed great. Gracious and amiable lord, may you fulfill your allotted span and preside over the sacrifices to the hundred spirits. Long may you hold the mandate; abundant emoluments bring you peace. Gracious and amiable lord, may you fulfill your allotted span and constantly enjoy great blessings.

Zao Shou 糟壽

Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor: Candidates in the examination generally can expound the meaning of the Greater Odes. Yet this is the only essay I have seen whose language and ideas are fresh and well ordered while retaining a solemn, dignified manner. It is included as a model for writers.

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: This brings out the Duke of Shao’s intention in “Winding Hills” (Juan a) to inspire and stir King Cheng. Reading it leaves one refreshed. Ah! When you, young sir, are entrusted with office in the future, you will surely know where to direct your efforts.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批　〔師保進戒之體正〕
〔如此〕
大臣之戒君必極言福壽之盛以歆動其心焉
夫人君至願莫過於壽考福祿之盛也大臣極
言以歆動之責望之意有在矣想昔召康公戒
成王之意以爲吾王當國祚亨嘉之日爲游歌
卷阿之舉是雖以舒暢其襟懷亦因以覘知其
福履斯時也四方無事於經營而累世之熈洽
於爾乎是承其游也伴奐其游矣萬幾罔有乎
===
曠廢而前人之燕翼於爾乎是及其休也優游
其休矣然必俾爾豈弟之君子終其壽命無貽
於先公善始善終之美而伴奐優游之樂得享
之於無窮焉吾王統馭華夷而尺地莫非其有
土宇何大明也撫綏萬邦而一民莫非其臣興
圖何孔厚也然必俾爾豈弟之君子終其壽考
常爲天地山川鬼神之主而土宇昄章之大得
承之於悠久焉吾王年方鼎盛而貴爲天子之
尊受命不旣長乎運際盈成而富有四海之廣
punctuated:
考試官教授林批：〔師保進戒之體正〕〔如此〕

大臣之戒君，必極言福壽之盛，以歆動其心焉。夫人君至願，莫過於壽考福祿之盛也。大臣極言以歆動之，責望之意有在矣。想昔召康公戒成王之意，以爲吾王當國祚亨嘉之日，爲游歌卷阿之舉，是雖以舒暢其襟懷，亦因以覘知其福履。斯時也，四方無事於經營，而累世之熈洽，於爾乎是承；其游也，伴奐其游矣。萬幾罔有乎曠廢，而前人之燕翼，於爾乎是及；其休也，優游其休矣。然必俾爾豈弟之君子終其壽命，無貽於先公善始善終之美，而伴奐優游之樂，得享之於無窮焉。吾王統馭華夷，而尺地莫非其有，土宇何大明也！撫綏萬邦，而一民莫非其臣，興圖何孔厚也！然必俾爾豈弟之君子終其壽考，常爲天地山川鬼神之主，而土宇昄章之大，得承之於悠久焉。吾王年方鼎盛，而貴爲天子之尊，受命不旣長乎？運際盈成，而富有四海之廣
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔Precisely such is the proper manner in which a Grand Preceptor or Grand Guardian offers admonition.〕

When a great minister admonishes his ruler, he must speak fully of abundant blessings and longevity, thereby stirring his heart to aspire to them. For a ruler’s deepest wishes extend no further than long life and abundant blessings and emoluments. When a great minister speaks fully of these to stir him, he has particular expectations in mind. Consider the intention with which Duke Kang of Shao once admonished King Cheng. He thought: Our king, at a time when the fortunes of the dynasty flourish, goes forth to roam and sing on the winding hill. Though this serves to ease and gladden his heart, it also affords an occasion to observe his blessed circumstances. At this time, the four quarters require no exertion to bring them into order, and the peace and harmony accumulated over successive generations pass to you. Your roaming is indeed free and unhurried. None of the myriad affairs of government is neglected, and your predecessors’ provision for their descendants reaches you. Your repose is indeed leisurely and at ease. Yet you, a gracious and kindly lord, must be enabled to complete your allotted lifespan, falling short in nothing of the former dukes’ excellence in beginning and ending well [?], so that you may enjoy forever the pleasures of unhurried roaming and leisurely repose. Our king rules both the Hua and the Yi, and not a foot of land lies outside his possession: how vast and illustrious is his domain! He nurtures and pacifies the myriad states, and not a single person is other than his subject: how exceedingly substantial is his imperial undertaking [?]! Yet you, a gracious and kindly lord, must be enabled to reach the full term of your longevity, remaining always the lord who presides over sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, mountains and rivers, and ghosts and spirits, so that you may long retain this vast and magnificent domain. Our king is in the prime of life and occupies the exalted dignity of the Son of Heaven: is not the mandate he has received enduring indeed? His reign falls in a time of plenitude and accomplishment, and his wealth encompasses the breadth of all within the Four Seas …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
弟祿不既康乎然必俾爾豈弟之君子終天年
於有永享純嘏於無間命之長者而愈長福之
康者而愈康焉是則今日福祿之盛固吾王之
所深願然致之必有其由也是烏可不知所務
哉考之因事納忠固人臣之事納約自牖亦進
言之法周公欲成王知稼穡之艱難不激以危
言之峻惟陳后稷公劉風化以諷之康公從遊
卷阿將戒以用賢脩德之事必先壽考福祿廣
其心而歆動之皆所謂善引其君以當道視後
===
世立談慟哭者異矣噫成王卒成中興之令主
謂非二公之力而誰歸
駿發爾私終三十里亦服爾耕十千維耦
劉景玉
同考試官教諭龔　批　〔頌題不過勸耕一事下筆便覺窘然此作只本朱傳組織成文〕
理亦自足必老於葩義者錄之
考試官學正范　批　〔周王戒農官之意〕
模寫殆盡讀之自不能釋手
punctuated:
弟祿不既康乎？然必俾爾豈弟之君子終天年於有永，享純嘏於無間，命之長者而愈長，福之康者而愈康焉。是則今日福祿之盛，固吾王之所深願，然致之必有其由也，是烏可不知所務哉？考之，因事納忠，固人臣之事；納約自牖，亦進言之法。周公欲成王知稼穡之艱難，不激以危言之峻，惟陳后稷、公劉風化以諷之。康公從遊卷阿，將戒以用賢脩德之事，必先壽考福祿，廣其心而歆動之，皆所謂善引其君以當道，視後世立談慟哭者異矣。噫！成王卒成中興之令主，謂非二公之力而誰歸？

「駿發爾私，終三十里。亦服爾耕，十千維耦。」
劉景玉

同考試官教諭龔批：〔頌題不過勸耕一事，下筆便覺窘然。此作只本朱傳組織成文〕理亦自足，必老於葩義者，錄之。

考試官學正范批：〔周王戒農官之意〕模寫殆盡，讀之自不能釋手。
translation_en:
…Are your blessings not already abundant [?]? Yet you, our gracious and amiable lord, must be enabled to complete your natural lifespan in enduring longevity and enjoy unalloyed blessings without interruption, so that your long life grows still longer and your abundant blessings still more abundant. Such flourishing blessings and emoluments are indeed what our king profoundly desires today. Yet there must be a means of attaining them: how could he fail to know where to direct his efforts?

On examination, offering loyal counsel as occasions arise is certainly a minister’s duty; presenting restrained counsel as though through a window is also a method of remonstrance. The Duke of Zhou wished King Cheng to understand the hardships of sowing and harvesting. He did not provoke him with the severity of stern admonitions, but set forth the transforming influence of Hou Ji and Gong Liu to counsel him indirectly. When Duke Kang accompanied the king on an excursion to Juan’e, he intended to admonish him about employing worthy men and cultivating virtue. He necessarily began with longevity, blessings, and emoluments, broadening the king’s mind and stirring his aspirations. Both exemplify what is called skillfully guiding one’s ruler onto the proper Way. They differed from those of later ages who burst into bitter weeping as soon as they began to speak. Ah! King Cheng ultimately became an excellent ruler who renewed his dynasty’s fortunes. If this was not the achievement of these two dukes, to whom should the credit go?

“Vigorously break up your private fields, throughout the full thirty li. Attend also to your ploughing: ten thousand men work in pairs.”
Liu Jingyu

Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor: 〔A topic from the Hymns concerns no more than the single matter of encouraging cultivation; as soon as one takes up the brush, one feels constrained. This composition simply draws on Zhu Xi’s commentary to weave its text.〕 Its reasoning is nevertheless sufficient in itself. Its author must be thoroughly practiced in interpreting the Odes. Selected.

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔The Zhou king’s intention in admonishing the agricultural officials〕 is rendered almost completely. Once one begins reading, one cannot put it down.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批　理到之言家數自
別
王者戒農官之治田盡所耕之地無不耕之人
蓋治田貴乎地利盡而人力協也否則廢厥事
而曠厥官矣奚可哉此戒農官之詞其意謂夫
國家以農爲重農事以耕爲先彼鄉遂之地皆
私田也私田不耕則西成失望農斯廢矣爾當
命彼甸徒于以大發其私田可焉溝洫之間皆
爾私也爾私弗治則士女何穀民斯病矣爾當
===
率彼農人于以駿發乎爾私可焉載芟載柞必
盡夫萬夫之所受此疆爾界可使有荒蕪者乎
啓之辟之必徧乎一川之所有上原下隰可使
有汙莱者乎然人力有未齊則務廣地者失之
荒廢時事者失之怠故必主伯耕也亞旅耕也
凡百畆所受者無非服事之人勸課之下無惰
農焉比閭耕也族黨耕也凡爾職所司者罔非
力農之輩巡省之餘無遊氓焉田以一川則人
以萬計櫛風雨而畟畟良耜者固非一耦也然
punctuated:
考試官教授林　批：理到之言，家數自別。
王者戒農官之治田，盡所耕之地，無不耕之人。蓋治田貴乎地利盡而人力協也，否則廢厥事而曠厥官矣，奚可哉？此戒農官之詞，其意謂夫國家以農爲重，農事以耕爲先。彼鄉遂之地，皆私田也。私田不耕，則西成失望，農斯廢矣。爾當命彼甸徒，于以大發其私田可焉。溝洫之間，皆爾私也。爾私弗治，則士女何穀，民斯病矣。爾當率彼農人，于以駿發乎爾私可焉。載芟載柞，必盡夫萬夫之所受；此疆爾界，可使有荒蕪者乎？啓之辟之，必徧乎一川之所有；上原下隰，可使有汙莱者乎？然人力有未齊，則務廣地者失之荒，廢時事者失之怠。故必主伯耕也，亞旅耕也，凡百畆所受者，無非服事之人，勸課之下無惰農焉；比閭耕也，族黨耕也，凡爾職所司者，罔非力農之輩，巡省之餘無遊氓焉。田以一川，則人以萬計，櫛風雨而畟畟良耜者，固非一耦也，然
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, an instructor, comments: “These words get to the heart of the principle; their manner of composition is distinctive.”
The king admonished the agricultural officials about tending the fields: all cultivable land was to be fully worked, and no one was to remain without work at the plough. For in tending fields, what matters is that the land’s productive capacity be fully used and human effort coordinated. Otherwise, the work would be neglected and the duties of office left unfulfilled. How could that be acceptable?
These words admonishing the agricultural officials mean this: the state regards agriculture as fundamental, and in agricultural work ploughing comes first. The lands of the inner and outer townships are all privately cultivated fields. If these fields are not ploughed, hopes for the autumn harvest will fail, and agriculture will fall into neglect. You should therefore command the field workers to break up their private fields extensively. All the land between the ditches and channels consists of your private fields. If your private fields are not tended, how will men and women obtain grain? The people will suffer. You should therefore lead those farmers in vigorously breaking up your private fields.
Clear the grasses and fell the trees: the work must extend throughout the allotments received by ten thousand cultivators. Within these boundaries and your field divisions, can any land be allowed to remain overgrown? Open it up and bring it under cultivation: the work must reach everything within the river plain. On the high ground and in the low, damp fields, can any land be allowed to remain waterlogged or fallow? Yet if human effort is not coordinated, those intent on extending cultivation will err by leaving land untended, while those who neglect seasonal tasks will err through indolence. Thus the heads and overseers must plough, and their deputies and subordinates must plough. All who receive an allotment of a hundred mu must perform their work; under encouragement and supervision, there will be no idle farmers. The neighborhood groups and wards must plough, and the clan groups and districts must plough. All within your official jurisdiction must devote themselves to agriculture; after your inspection rounds, there will be no people wandering idly about.
When the fields encompass an entire river plain, the workers number in the tens of thousands. Those who brave wind and rain, working with their keen, fine ploughshares, certainly constitute more than a single pair of ploughmen. Yet …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
拜力齊心之勤有如一耦而並耕也里方三十
則夫以十千耒耜而澤澤其耕者固非二人
也然通力合作之勞有如二人而並治也是則
舉耕事而盡其地則地無遺利矣服耕事而盡
其人則人無遺力矣如是而後豐年可必則成
王之昭假於爾者不負爾農官之職亦庶乎其
少盡矣是可以不知所勉哉大抵周家以農事
開國故自后稷至於成康重農之意著於無逸
之書歌於雅頌之什不一而盡誠以生民命脉
之所係舍此而欲言治皆末也周之所以久安
長治以至歷年八百者未必不肇基於此後世
人主不此之務遊心異術以求安天下之策甚
至有不辨菽麥而來人譏誚者宜乎治莫古若
也
===
春秋
九月考仲子之宮〔隱公五年〕
廉傑
同考試官教諭路　批〔題本易知作者類〕
punctuated:
拜力齊心之勤，有如一耦而並耕也。里方三十，則夫以十千，耒耜而澤澤其耕者，固非二人也。然通力合作之勞，有如二人而並治也。是則舉耕事而盡其地，則地無遺利矣；服耕事而盡其人，則人無遺力矣。如是而後豐年可必，則成王之昭假於爾者不負，爾農官之職亦庶乎其少盡矣。是可以不知所勉哉？大抵周家以農事開國，故自后稷至於成康，重農之意著於《無逸》之書，歌於雅頌之什，不一而盡。誠以生民命脉之所係，舍此而欲言治，皆末也。周之所以久安長治，以至歷年八百者，未必不肇基於此。後世人主不此之務，遊心異術，以求安天下之策，甚至有不辨菽麥而來人譏誚者。宜乎治莫古若也。

春秋
九月，考仲子之宮。〔隱公五年〕
廉傑
同考試官教諭路批〔題本易知，作者類〕
translation_en:
…yet in their diligent exertions, joining strength [?] and uniting their resolve, they are like a single pair plowing side by side. In a tract thirty li square, the husbandmen number ten thousand: those wielding plows and plowshares, turning up the soil, are certainly more than two men. Yet in their shared exertions and cooperative labor, they are like two men cultivating together. Thus, when the work of plowing extends over all the land, none of the land’s benefits is left unrealized; when all the people take part in cultivation, none of their strength is left unused. Only then can a plentiful harvest be assured. You will thereby fulfill King Cheng’s manifest exhortation to you, and you agricultural officials may hope to have discharged at least some portion of your duties. Can you then fail to know what you must strive to do?

Broadly speaking, the house of Zhou founded its state upon agriculture. Thus, from Hou Ji down to Kings Cheng and Kang, its concern for agriculture was expressed in the chapter “Against Ease” and sung in the Major and Minor Odes and the Hymns, in more instances than can be exhaustively recounted. Indeed, agriculture is what sustains the lifeblood of the people; any discussion of governance that sets it aside concerns mere incidentals. Zhou’s enduring peace and good government, lasting as long as eight hundred years, may well have had their foundation here. Rulers of later ages neglected this task and let their minds wander among strange doctrines, seeking strategies to bring peace to the realm. Some could not even distinguish beans from wheat and thus invited ridicule. Little wonder that their governance never equaled that of antiquity.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In the ninth month, the temple of Zhongzi was inaugurated.” 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin〕
By Lian Jie 廉傑.
