title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
能言之但傳意錯綜難於分析此篇體認真
切議論明當而詞又足以發之是用錄出
考試官學正范　批　謹嚴文字
考試官教授林　批　析傳合經明整可
誦
春秋紀望國祀事之失不惟譏夫禮而又正其
名此考宮一舉而魯之典禮紊矣宜春秋特書
以譏之也歟且仲子者惠公之妾桓公之母也
我隱嗣封適追先志既爲之立祭享之宮又爲
===
之舉告成之祀宜若愛親而友弟矣君子以爲
非禮者何歟蓋宗廟之制典禮所嚴魯在當時
奉周公之祀祔羣公之主者吾聞其有閟宮也
仲子何人乃令堂寢極規制之宏土木耀輪奐
之美果昭耶穆耶而宮以奉之耶借曰禮緣情
制斯舉可謂義起者矣殊不知諸侯之廟五一
定之制也今五廟之外而復有仲子之宮是魯
有六廟矣成先君之邪心也壞望國之家法也
苟不謹之則奸典悖禮豈可以爲訓哉故經於
punctuated:
能言之，但傳意錯綜，難於分析。此篇體認真切，議論明當，而詞又足以發之，是用錄出。
考試官學正范，批：謹嚴文字。
考試官教授林，批：析傳合經，明整可誦。
《春秋》紀望國祀事之失，不惟譏夫禮，而又正其名。此考宮一舉，而魯之典禮紊矣，宜《春秋》特書以譏之也歟！且仲子者，惠公之妾、桓公之母也。我隱嗣封，適追先志，既爲之立祭享之宮，又爲之舉告成之祀，宜若愛親而友弟矣。君子以爲非禮者何歟？蓋宗廟之制，典禮所嚴。魯在當時，奉周公之祀、祔羣公之主者，吾聞其有閟宮也。仲子何人，乃令堂寢極規制之宏，土木耀輪奐之美？果昭耶、穆耶，而宮以奉之耶？借曰禮緣情制，斯舉可謂義起者矣。殊不知諸侯之廟五，一定之制也。今五廟之外，而復有仲子之宮，是魯有六廟矣。成先君之邪心也，壞望國之家法也。苟不謹之，則奸典悖禮，豈可以爲訓哉？故經於
translation_en:
…can discuss it, but the meaning of the commentary is intricately interwoven and difficult to disentangle. This essay shows a genuine and precise understanding; its arguments are clear and sound, and its language adequately expresses them. It has therefore been selected for inclusion.
Examiner Fan, School Instructor, comments: “A carefully composed and rigorous piece.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “It analyzes the commentary in accord with the Classic; clear and orderly, it merits recitation.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records errors in the sacrificial affairs of a leading state, not merely to criticize its ritual practice but also to rectify its designations. This single act of consecrating the temple threw Lu’s ritual institutions into disorder. Was it not fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should specifically record it as a criticism? Zhongzi was Duke Hui’s concubine and Duke Huan’s mother. Our Duke Yin succeeded to the fief and undertook to fulfill his predecessor’s intentions: he erected a temple for sacrifices to her and held a sacrifice to announce its completion. This might seem to show love for a parent and affection for a younger brother. Why, then, did the gentleman consider it contrary to ritual?
The arrangements of ancestral temples are strictly governed by ritual institutions. In Lu at that time, I understand, there was the Secluded Temple, where sacrifices were offered to the Duke of Zhou and the spirit tablets of the successive dukes were enshrined. Who was Zhongzi, that the halls and inner chambers of her temple should be built on so magnificent a scale, their timber and earthen construction displaying such architectural splendor? Did she belong to the zhao rank or the mu rank of ancestors, that a temple should be provided to serve her? Granted, one might say that ritual is fashioned according to human feelings, and that this act could be called an innovation founded on righteousness. Yet this entirely overlooks the fixed rule that a feudal lord has five temples. Now, with Zhongzi’s temple in addition to the five, Lu had six temples! This fulfilled the former ruler’s misguided wishes and undermined the ancestral rules of a leading state. If such matters are not carefully guarded, the established institutions will be violated and ritual contravened. How could this serve as a model? Thus, in the Classic, with regard to…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宮廟之作合禮者則不書此而書考宮者以其
爲仲子之宮不當立也非禮之罪不於是而見
乎然又謂之正名者何歟蓋嫡妾之分人倫所
重魯在當時配惠公之食享小君之祀者吾聞
其有孟子也仲子何人乃今俎豆陳備物之豐
祼獻肅如在之敬果嫡耶繼耶而祀以尊之耶
借曰母以子貴此心可謂善推者矣殊不知諸
侯不再娶三代之禮也今孟子之外復有仲子
之祀是惠有二嫡矣啓桓公之逆志也悖天敘
===
之大倫也苟不正之則亂名犯分其何以示法
哉故經於夫人之稱必姓謚號之兼舉此而單
舉姓字者著其爲惠公之妾非夫人也正名之
義不於是而見乎噫考宮書而後宗廟之禮嚴
仲子書而後嫡妾之名正聖筆之精有如是哉
大抵有國家者不可不謹於禮也惠公滅禮而
徇於愛隱公越禮而成其惡卒致羽父之謀桓
公之弑其禍有不可勝言者故聖人嚴於嫡妾
長幼之禮以垂戒於後世可謂深切著明矣猶
punctuated:
宮廟之作，合禮者則不書。此而書考宮者，以其爲仲子之宮，不當立也。非禮之罪，不於是而見乎？然又謂之正名者，何歟？蓋嫡妾之分，人倫所重。魯在當時，配惠公之食、享小君之祀者，吾聞其有孟子也。仲子何人，乃今俎豆陳備物之豐，祼獻肅如在之敬，果嫡耶？繼耶？而祀以尊之耶？借曰母以子貴，此心可謂善推者矣。殊不知諸侯不再娶，三代之禮也。今孟子之外，復有仲子之祀，是惠有二嫡矣，啓桓公之逆志也，悖天敘之大倫也。苟不正之，則亂名犯分，其何以示法哉？故經於夫人之稱，必姓謚號之兼舉。此而單舉姓字者，著其爲惠公之妾，非夫人也。正名之義，不於是而見乎？

噫！考宮書而後宗廟之禮嚴，仲子書而後嫡妾之名正。聖筆之精，有如是哉！大抵有國家者，不可不謹於禮也。惠公滅禮而徇於愛，隱公越禮而成其惡，卒致羽父之謀、桓公之弑，其禍有不可勝言者。故聖人嚴於嫡妾長幼之禮，以垂戒於後世，可謂深切著明矣。猶
translation_en:
…when palaces and ancestral temples are built in accordance with ritual, the Classic does not record them. Here it records the inauguration of the temple because this was a temple for Zhongzi, which ought not to have been established. Is not the offense against ritual thereby revealed? Yet why is this also called rectifying names? The distinction between principal wife and concubine is of great importance in human relationships. In Lu at that time, I understand that Mengzi was the one who shared Duke Hui’s sacrificial offerings and received sacrifices as his consort. Who was Zhongzi, that sacrificial stands and vessels should now display abundant offerings of every kind, and that libations and presentations should be performed with solemn reverence, as though she were present? Was she truly the principal wife? Was she a successor wife? Why honor her with sacrifices? Suppose one says that a mother becomes honored through her son: such a sentiment might be called a commendable extension of affection. Yet this overlooks the ritual rule of the Three Dynasties that a feudal lord does not marry a principal wife a second time. Now, with sacrifices to Zhongzi in addition to those for Mengzi, Duke Hui has two principal wives. This encourages Duke Huan’s rebellious ambitions and violates the fundamental human relationships ordained by Heaven. Unless this is corrected, titles will be confused and distinctions transgressed: how could it furnish a standard? Thus, when the Classic refers to a ruler’s wife, it invariably gives her clan name, posthumous name, and title together. Here it gives only her clan name and personal designation, making clear that she was Duke Hui’s concubine, not his principal wife. Is not the principle of rectifying names thereby revealed?

Ah! By recording the temple’s inauguration, the ritual rules governing ancestral temples are upheld; by writing “Zhongzi,” the designations of principal wife and concubine are set right. Such is the precision of the sage’s brush! In general, those who govern states and great households must be scrupulous about ritual. Duke Hui cast aside ritual to indulge his affection; Duke Yin transgressed ritual and brought Hui’s wrongdoing to completion. In the end this led to Yufu’s plot and Duke Huan’s murder of his ruler, with calamities beyond recounting. Thus the sage strictly upheld the ritual distinctions between principal wife and concubine, elder and younger, to leave a warning for later generations. This may indeed be called profoundly earnest and lucidly expressed. Yet…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有溺愛不悟如晉獻公者亦獨何心歟
楚子伐鄭〔宣公四年〕楚子伐鄭〔宣公九年〕
賈正已
同考試官教諭路　批〔傳意甚明作者罔〕
〔知歸着牽引別傳冗雜可厭晚得此篇簡嚴〕
〔整潔讀之使人悚然可敬可敬〕
考試官學正范　批〔論楚事美惡詞正〕
〔而嚴作手也〕
考試官教授林　批〔善發傳意〕
===
外夷討貳國春秋予之外夷䝉貳國春秋貶之
此聖人於楚再伐鄭詞同而予奪異者討罪謹
辨之義其嚴矣哉在昔春秋中葉我宣當國晉
覇寖微於諸夏楚莊崛起於南荆戎馬交横干
戈迭逞蓋無日不以爭鄭爲事也乃今楚也憤
鄭人之未服率師徒而往問虔劉其人民震蕩
其郊保與後此之伐鄭志固同矣何春秋書爵
而以爲予之耶彼歸生者犯無將之戒負不道
之罪中外環視未聞有討罪之舉也而楚子乃
punctuated:
有溺愛不悟如晉獻公者，亦獨何心歟？

楚子伐鄭〔宣公四年〕。楚子伐鄭〔宣公九年〕。
賈正已
同考試官教諭路，批〔傳意甚明，作者罔〕〔知歸着，牽引別傳，冗雜可厭。晚得此篇，簡嚴〕〔整潔，讀之使人悚然。可敬，可敬！〕
考試官學正范，批〔論楚事美惡，詞正〕〔而嚴，作手也。〕
考試官教授林，批〔善發傳意。〕

外夷討貳國，《春秋》予之；外夷䝉貳國，《春秋》貶之。此聖人於楚再伐鄭，詞同而予奪異者，討罪謹辨之義，其嚴矣哉！在昔春秋中葉，我宣當國，晉覇寖微於諸夏，楚莊崛起於南荆，戎馬交横，干戈迭逞，蓋無日不以爭鄭爲事也。乃今楚也，憤鄭人之未服，率師徒而往問，虔劉其人民，震蕩其郊保，與後此之伐鄭，志固同矣。何《春秋》書爵而以爲予之耶？彼歸生者，犯無將之戒，負不道之罪，中外環視，未聞有討罪之舉也，而楚子乃
translation_en:
…Yet there were still men such as Duke Xian of Jin, blinded by indulgent affection and failing to awaken to their error. What could have been in their hearts?

“The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Xuan.〕 “The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan.〕
Jia Zhengyi 賈正已

Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔The commentary’s meaning is perfectly clear, yet writers fail〕〔to grasp its point, dragging in other commentaries in a wearisome jumble. At last I obtained this essay: concise, rigorous,〕〔orderly, and clean. Reading it inspires awe. Admirable, admirable!〕
Examiner Fan, School Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing the good and bad in Chu’s actions, the language is correct〕〔and stern. An accomplished writer!〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Skillfully brings out the commentary’s meaning.〕

When an outer barbarian state chastises a state of divided allegiance, the Spring and Autumn Annals approves it; when an outer barbarian state shields such a state [?], the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns it. Thus, in recording Chu’s two attacks on Zheng, the Sage uses identical wording but differs in his approval and disapproval. How exacting is his principle of carefully distinguishing the grounds for punishing wrongdoing!

Formerly, midway through the Spring and Autumn period, when our Duke Xuan governed the state, Jin’s hegemony among the states of the central lands was gradually weakening, while King Zhuang of Chu rose to power in southern Jing. Warhorses ranged to and fro, and weapons were wielded in successive campaigns. Scarcely a day passed without a struggle for Zheng.

On this occasion, Chu, angered that the people of Zheng had not submitted, led its troops to demand an accounting, slaughtering its people and throwing its outlying settlements and fortifications into turmoil. Its intention was surely the same as in its subsequent attack on Zheng. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals record the ruler’s noble rank as a sign of approval? That man Guisheng had violated the injunction against even contemplating regicide and incurred the guilt of a heinous crime. Looking all around, within and beyond the central states, one heard of no action to punish his offense. Yet the Viscount of Chu then…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
能投袂而奮其威援枹而聲其罪文告播於溱
洧三綱之重賴以復明義聲揚於江漢九伐之
典由茲不墜戡亂鋤宄師何壯耶苟不予之則
人將以弑逆者爲常情而君臣之彛泯矣經故
稱爵者取其仗義也誅亂討賊之善不於是而
見乎傳所謂治亂賊之黨者此也既而楚也追
懷干厲之憾復舉駕鄭之兵國君親將大衆偕
行與前此之伐鄭事若等矣何春秋書爵而又
以爲貶之耶彼鄭人者居晉楚之衝負懿親之
===
望上下安輯未聞有可聲之罪也而楚莊無故
驅犬羊之羣張崩沸之勢三軍悉力播虐熖於
中原兩廣揚威鼓妖氛於上國恃强憑弱師何
悖耶苟不貶之則人將以猾夏者爲常事而内
外之防決矣經故稱爵者見其自將也重兵陵
暴之惡不於是而著乎傳所謂謹華夷之辨者
此也噫同一楚子也同一伐鄭也而善惡之不
可掩如此者此春秋所以非聖人莫能脩也歟
抑又論之楚以僭竊之夷頻年内擾無足較者
punctuated: 能投袂而奮其威，援枹而聲其罪。文告播於溱洧，三綱之重賴以復明；義聲揚於江漢，九伐之典由茲不墜。戡亂鋤宄，師何壯耶！苟不予之，則人將以弑逆者爲常情，而君臣之彛泯矣。經故稱爵者，取其仗義也。誅亂討賊之善，不於是而見乎？傳所謂治亂賊之黨者，此也。既而楚也，追懷干厲之憾，復舉駕鄭之兵，國君親將，大衆偕行，與前此之伐鄭事若等矣。何《春秋》書爵，而又以爲貶之耶？彼鄭人者，居晉楚之衝，負懿親之望，上下安輯，未聞有可聲之罪也。而楚莊無故驅犬羊之羣，張崩沸之勢，三軍悉力，播虐熖於中原；兩廣揚威，鼓妖氛於上國。恃强憑弱，師何悖耶！苟不貶之，則人將以猾夏者爲常事，而内外之防決矣。經故稱爵者，見其自將也。重兵陵暴之惡，不於是而著乎？傳所謂謹華夷之辨者，此也。噫！同一楚子也，同一伐鄭也，而善惡之不可掩如此者，此《春秋》所以非聖人莫能脩也歟！抑又論之，楚以僭竊之夷，頻年内擾，無足較者。
translation_en:
…was able to shake out his sleeves and rise in might, take up the drumstick, and proclaim the offender’s crimes. His proclamation spread through the lands of the Zhen and Wei rivers, restoring clarity to the weighty Three Bonds; his call to righteousness resounded along the Jiang and Han rivers, preserving the institutions governing the nine grounds for punitive campaigns. Quelling disorder and rooting out malefactors—how splendid his army was! Had he not been commended, people would have come to regard regicide and rebellion as ordinary human conduct, and the enduring norms between ruler and subject would have vanished. Thus, when the Classic names him by his rank, it approves his championing of righteousness. Is not the goodness of suppressing rebellion and punishing traitors revealed here? This is what the commentary means by bringing the faction of rebels and traitors to justice.

Later, Chu, brooding over the grievance at Ganli [?], again raised troops to overrun Zheng. The ruler commanded in person, and a great host marched with him. The affair seemed equivalent to the earlier attack on Zheng. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals record his rank yet thereby censure him? The people of Zheng occupied the strategic crossroads between Jin and Chu and bore the expectations attached to their close kinship with the royal house. Those above and below lived in peace and concord; no crime warranting public denunciation had been heard of. Yet King Zhuang of Chu, without cause, drove forward his packs of dogs and sheep, unleashing a force like a collapse and a boiling torrent. His three armies exerted their full strength, spreading the flames of cruelty through the Central Plain; his two chariot divisions displayed their might, stirring up a baleful atmosphere in the central states. Relying on strength to oppress the weak—how perverse his army was! Had he not been censured, people would have come to regard the disruption of the Xia states as an ordinary affair, and the barrier separating those within from those without would have broken down. Thus, when the Classic names him by his rank, it shows that he commanded in person. Is not the evil of using a powerful army for oppression and violence made manifest here? This is what the commentary means by carefully maintaining the distinction between the Hua and the Yi.

Alas! It is the same Viscount of Chu and the same act of attacking Zheng, yet good and evil cannot be concealed in this way. Is this why none but a sage could have compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals? To pursue the argument further: Chu, a Yi state that usurped royal standing, disturbed the central states year after year; its conduct scarcely merits further reckoning.

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
獨惜晉景奕世之覇始則不能討鄭繼而不能
討陳使楚人得以假義號召諸侯於辰陵縣陳
入鄭大敗晉師伐宋滅蕭雷動諸夏於是盟主
之權屬之楚矣獨不深可咎乎先儒謂景公無
制中夏之畧於此益信
禮記
凡君召以三節二節以走一節以趨
王朝
同考試官教諭周　批〔三節以一節二節互講得旨且淵然之光蒼然之色奪諸人目〕
===
考試官學正范　批〔組織經語炳炳有文且能道出敬君之意可誦〕
擊節於子深矣
考試官教授林　批〔深得禮家之旨〕
君傳命節以時用臣赴命儀以節施夫節有疎
密赴有疾徐皆敬君命故也古之人臣事君有
禮哉記玉藻者謂夫君臣固有尊卑之分亦有
往來之禮是故王事勞乎咨詢而綸音布於在
punctuated:
獨惜晉景奕世之覇，始則不能討鄭，繼而不能討陳，使楚人得以假義號召諸侯於辰陵，縣陳入鄭，大敗晉師，伐宋滅蕭，雷動諸夏。於是盟主之權屬之楚矣，獨不深可咎乎？先儒謂景公無制中夏之畧，於此益信。

《禮記》
凡君召，以三節：二節以走，一節以趨。
王朝
同考試官教諭周批〔三節以一節、二節互講，得旨。且淵然之光、蒼然之色，奪諸人目。〕
考試官學正范批〔組織經語，炳炳有文，且能道出敬君之意，可誦。〕
擊節於子深矣！
考試官教授林批〔深得禮家之旨。〕

君傳命，節以時用；臣赴命，儀以節施。夫節有疎密，赴有疾徐，皆敬君命故也。古之人臣，事君有禮哉！記《玉藻》者謂：夫君臣固有尊卑之分，亦有往來之禮。是故王事勞乎咨詢，而綸音布於在
translation_en:
… Yet it is especially regrettable that Duke Jing of Jin, heir to a hegemony maintained over successive generations, first failed to punish Zheng and then failed to punish Chen. This allowed the men of Chu to invoke righteousness as a pretext for summoning the feudal lords to Chenling, to annex Chen as a county and enter Zheng, to inflict a great defeat on Jin’s army, to attack Song and destroy Xiao, and to shake the Chinese states like thunder. Thus the authority of the leader of the covenants passed to Chu. Was this not profoundly blameworthy? Earlier Confucian scholars said that Duke Jing lacked a strategy for controlling the central Chinese states; these events further confirm their judgment.

Book of Rites
“Whenever the ruler summons someone, three kinds of tally are used: with two tallies, one runs; with one tally, one hastens.”
Wang Chao
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔The ‘three kinds of tally’ are explained through the mutually illuminating treatment of ‘one tally’ and ‘two tallies,’ capturing the meaning. Moreover, its deep radiance and venerable hue dazzle the eye.〕
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔The language of the classics is woven into a brilliantly accomplished composition. It also succeeds in expressing the meaning of reverence for the ruler and deserves to be recited.〕
I applaud you most heartily!
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔It thoroughly grasps the purport of the ritual scholars.〕

When the ruler transmits a command, tallies are used as the occasion requires; when a minister responds to the command, his manner of proceeding accords with the tallies. The tallies may be fewer or more numerous, and the response swifter or slower: all this is for the sake of reverencing the ruler’s command. How well the ministers of antiquity observed ritual in serving their rulers! The author of the “Jade Pendants” chapter means that ruler and minister certainly have their respective superior and subordinate stations, but there are also rites governing their exchanges. Thus, when royal affairs require the labor of consultation, the sovereign’s words are proclaimed to those serving …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
官在外之日于是乎有二節之時焉合二於一
正遇三而齊矣國政俟其揆序而渙命布於在
府在朝之地于是乎有一節之時焉加一於二
亦以三而止矣不可多也不可寡也等威明於
惟緌之間不可損也不可益也度數秩於有文
之際人臣于此何如其爲容耶必也二節之至
則曰事固急乎不然何其節之密也于是乎不
以走不幾於以急緩爲心者耶故靡及之慮已
形而欲發之端即𨒪濟濟于官者而今惕惕于
===
道接武繼武不暇拘矣是若有失容之誚殊不
知當急而承之以急實所以敬君也一節之臨
則曰是固緩乎不然何其節之疎也于是乎不
以趨不幾於以奔走爲事者耶是故將事之敬
雖形而失措之儀不設刻刻于室者而今翔翔
于朝如矢如流不必務矣是若有脩容之嫌殊
不知當緩而承之以緩亦所以敬君也夫一節
二節命雖異而以走以趨敬則同當時君臣諤
然可想見矣雖然二節以走一節以趨以緩急
punctuated: 官在外之日，於是乎有二節之時焉。合二於一，正遇三而齊矣。國政俟其揆序，而渙命布於在府在朝之地，於是乎有一節之時焉。加一於二，亦以三而止矣。不可多也，不可寡也，等威明於惟緌之間；不可損也，不可益也，度數秩於有文之際。人臣于此何如其爲容耶？必也二節之至，則曰：「事固急乎！不然，何其節之密也？」於是乎不以走，不幾於以急緩爲心者耶？故靡及之慮已形，而欲發之端即𨒪。濟濟于官者，而今惕惕于道，接武繼武，不暇拘矣。是若有失容之誚，殊不知當急而承之以急，實所以敬君也。一節之臨，則曰：「是固緩乎！不然，何其節之疎也？」於是乎不以趨，不幾於以奔走爲事者耶？是故將事之敬雖形，而失措之儀不設。刻刻于室者，而今翔翔于朝，如矢如流，不必務矣。是若有脩容之嫌，殊不知當緩而承之以緩，亦所以敬君也。夫一節二節，命雖異，而以走以趨，敬則同。當時君臣諤然可想見矣。雖然，二節以走，一節以趨，以緩急
translation_en:
…when officials are away on duty, there are occasions for using two tokens of summons. Combining these two with the one makes exactly three. When affairs of state await deliberation and ordering, and the sovereign’s commands are proclaimed to those in government offices and at court, there are occasions for using one token. Adding this one to the two likewise stops at three. There can be neither more nor fewer: distinctions of rank and authority are made clear through the pendant cords [?]. Nothing may be subtracted or added: prescribed measures are duly ordered through their ornamentation [?]. How, then, should a minister conduct himself?

When two tokens arrive, he must say: “The business must surely be urgent! Otherwise, why should the tokens be so closely spaced?” If he does not then run, would he not come close to treating urgent business as something that may be delayed [?]? Thus, as soon as concern about failing to arrive in time arises, the impulse to set out immediately takes effect [?]. He who was composed and dignified in office is now anxious and alert on the road; step follows step, with no leisure to observe restraints upon his gait. This might seem to invite criticism for a loss of decorum. Yet such criticism entirely misses the point: responding urgently to what requires urgency is precisely how one shows reverence for one’s ruler.

When one token arrives, he says: “This must surely be less urgent! Otherwise, why should the tokens be so widely spaced?” If he does not then advance at a measured quick step, would he not come close to making mere running about his business? Thus, although his reverence in undertaking the task is apparent, he displays no flustered deportment. He who was ever painstaking in his chamber now moves with easy dignity at court; he need not strive to move like an arrow or a flowing stream. This might seem open to the suspicion that he is cultivating his appearance. Yet such suspicion entirely misses the point: responding deliberately to what allows deliberation is also how one shows reverence for one’s ruler.

Whether there is one token or two, the summons differs, but the reverence expressed in running or advancing at a measured quick step is the same. One can imagine the forthright bearing [?] of ruler and ministers in those days. Nevertheless, running at two tokens and advancing at a measured quick step at one token, according to the urgency or otherwise of the business…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
爲敬者也一命而傴再命三命而傴而俯而循
牆而走以多寡爲敬者也君子事君敬固無所
不在至於趨走疾徐之間傴僂隆殺之際尤有
節焉斯不僕僕矣夫爲國何貴乎臣之僕僕哉
是故禮之所以作也
古之制禮也經之以天地紀之以日月參
之以三光政教之本也
萬天衢
同考試官教諭周　批〔曰經曰紀曰參就〕
〔從上文象天地日月三光說來殊有源委尚〕
===
〔謂不深於禮經者乎〕
考試官學正范　批〔從有經有紀有參〕
〔講政教之本深得旨讀之聳然〕
考試官教授林　批〔結云鄉飲與王制〕
〔相表裏道人所未道〕
聖人制禮備造化而出治道也夫鄉飲之禮大
矣天地日月三光無不象而備之則政教豈不
由是出乎記鄉飲者至此其意蓋謂禮制由造
punctuated:
爲敬者也。一命而傴，再命三命而傴而俯而循牆而走，以多寡爲敬者也。君子事君，敬固無所不在；至於趨走疾徐之間、傴僂隆殺之際，尤有節焉，斯不僕僕矣。夫爲國，何貴乎臣之僕僕哉？是故禮之所以作也。
古之制禮也，經之以天地，紀之以日月，參之以三光，政教之本也。
萬天衢
同考試官教諭周，批〔曰經、曰紀、曰參，就〕〔從上文象天地日月三光說來，殊有源委，尚〕〔謂不深於禮經者乎？〕
考試官學正范，批〔從有經、有紀、有參〕〔講政教之本，深得旨，讀之聳然。〕
考試官教授林，批〔結云鄉飲與王制〕〔相表裏，道人所未道。〕
聖人制禮，備造化而出治道也。夫鄉飲之禮大矣！天地日月三光，無不象而備之，則政教豈不由是出乎？記鄉飲者至此，其意蓋謂禮制由造
translation_en:
…express reverence through the appropriate degrees of haste and deliberation. At the first appointment one bows; at the second and third appointments one bows, bends low, and hurries along beside the wall: this expresses reverence according to the number of appointments received. When a gentleman serves his ruler, reverence is indeed present in everything. Yet particularly in the pace of his steps, whether swift or slow, and in the depth of his bows, whether greater or lesser, there are proper measures. Thus he does not merely bustle about. For governing a state, what value is there in ministers merely bustling about? This is why ritual was established.
“When the ancients instituted ritual, they took Heaven and Earth as its framework, the sun and moon as its ordering pattern, and the three luminaries as its correlates. It is the foundation of government and moral instruction.”
Wan Tianqu
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The expressions ‘framework,’ ‘ordering pattern,’ and ‘correlates’ follow directly from the preceding discussion of emulating Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, and the three luminaries. The argument has a clear source and development. Can one still say that this writer lacks a profound understanding of the ritual classic?”
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “By discussing the foundation of government and moral instruction in terms of a framework, an ordering pattern, and correlates, the writer grasps the meaning profoundly. Reading it stirs one deeply.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “The conclusion states that ‘The Village Drinking Ceremony’ and ‘Royal Regulations’ complement one another as inner and outer aspects. This says what others have not said.”
When the sages instituted ritual, they incorporated the workings of creation in their entirety and brought forth the Way of governance. Great indeed is the ritual of village drinking! It embodies and takes as its models Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, and the three luminaries, leaving nothing out. How, then, could government and moral instruction fail to arise from it? At this point, the author recording the village drinking ceremony presumably means that ritual institutions derive from the workings of creation…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
化而作政教本禮制而行古之聖人因會聚之
常以制飲食之節致尊讓之義以遠鬬辨之非
于是乎有鄉飲酒之禮焉夫非經則無本故立
賓主以象天地天地乃所以爲經也但見賓以
義主以仁一天地之綱維截然有本而不離焉
豈非經之以天地乎非紀則無文故設介僎以
象日月日月乃所以爲紀也但見介從賓僎從
主一日月之分次秩然有文而不雜焉豈非紀
之以日月乎非參則無輔于是乎立三賓以象
===
三光而三光非卽所以爲參參歟故三賓參居以
輔乎衆賓一三光參列以輔于天焉則又參之
以三光矣是若無預於治而何以謂之政教之
本也蓋曰政曰教有大綱焉經紀則大綱以立
有萬目焉紀布則萬目以張又有衆輔焉參備
則衆輔以具由是名分定於等威賓介交而貴
賤別祭飲行而隆殺辨不必家至之油油然而
治自出也風俗成於禮讓敦和樂弟長燕安之
儀極不流不遺不亂之美不必日見之勃勃然
punctuated: 化而作，政教本禮制而行。古之聖人因會聚之常，以制飲食之節，致尊讓之義，以遠鬬辨之非，于是乎有鄉飲酒之禮焉。夫非經則無本，故立賓主以象天地，天地乃所以爲經也。但見賓以義，主以仁，一天地之綱維，截然有本而不離焉，豈非經之以天地乎？非紀則無文，故設介僎以象日月，日月乃所以爲紀也。但見介從賓，僎從主，一日月之分次，秩然有文而不雜焉，豈非紀之以日月乎？非參則無輔，于是乎立三賓以象三光，而三光非卽所以爲參參歟？故三賓參居以輔乎衆賓，一三光參列以輔于天焉，則又參之以三光矣。是若無預於治，而何以謂之政教之本也？蓋曰政曰教，有大綱焉，經紀則大綱以立；有萬目焉，紀布則萬目以張；又有衆輔焉，參備則衆輔以具。由是名分定於等威，賓介交而貴賤別，祭飲行而隆殺辨，不必家至之，油油然而治自出也。風俗成於禮讓，敦和樂弟長燕安之儀，極不流不遺不亂之美，不必日見之，勃勃然
translation_en:
… transformation, while governance and moral instruction proceed on the basis of ritual institutions. The sages of antiquity took the ordinary practice of gathering together as the basis for regulating eating and drinking. They brought the principles of respect and deference to full expression, thereby keeping people from the wrongs of fighting and disputation. Thus arose the village wine-drinking ceremony. Without a guiding framework there can be no foundation. Accordingly, guest and host were established to symbolize Heaven and Earth: Heaven and Earth provide that framework. We see the guest acting through righteousness and the host through benevolence, conforming to the governing structure of Heaven and Earth, each distinctly grounded and never departing from it. Is this not to give the ceremony its framework through Heaven and Earth? Without an ordering system there can be no patterned arrangement. Accordingly, the assistant to the guest and the assistant to the host were appointed to symbolize the sun and moon: the sun and moon provide that ordering system. We see the guest’s assistant following the guest and the host’s assistant following the host, conforming to the respective stations of sun and moon, orderly in their patterned arrangement and without confusion. Is this not to order the ceremony through the sun and moon? Without supplementary participants there can be no assistance. Accordingly, three guests were established to symbolize the Three Luminaries—the sun, moon, and stars. Are not the Three Luminaries precisely what provide this supplementary support [?]? Thus the three guests take their places to assist the assembled guests, just as the Three Luminaries stand arrayed to assist Heaven. In this way the ceremony is further supplemented through the Three Luminaries.

This might seem to have no bearing on government; why, then, call it the foundation of governance and moral instruction? Governance and instruction have their main guiding principles: with a framework and an ordering system, those principles are established. They have their myriad particulars: when the ordering system is extended throughout, those particulars are all set forth. They also have their many forms of assistance: when supplementary arrangements are complete, all such assistance is provided. Thus status and allotted roles are fixed through distinctions of rank and dignity. As guest and assistant exchange courtesies, noble and humble are distinguished; as offerings and drinking proceed, the greater and lesser degrees of ceremony are made clear. There is no need to visit every household: smoothly and naturally, good order emerges of itself. Customs are formed through ritual and deference. The ceremonial forms of harmony, joy, respect for elders, and peaceful ease are strengthened, fully realizing the excellence of neither excess, neglect, nor disorder. There is no need to meet with people every day: vigorously …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而化自行也孰謂政教之本猶不在是乎故曰
觀于鄉而知王道之易易也益可見矣雖然是
禮也三年大比興賢者能者與夫諸侯之卿大
夫貢士於其君類如此有志於復古者果能舉
而行之則孝弟日興造士以告于王而升諸司
馬者固濟濟如也然則鄉飲與王制殆相爲表
裏者乎
第貳塲
論
===
忠恕違道不遠
糟士奇
同考試官教諭冀 批〔檃括中庸一篇之意殆盡又且句句不離道與忠恕間有道出〕
前人所未嘗道者於理深矣關西之學倡自
橫渠若子豈非勃然而興者耶筆力千鈞姑
未暇論
考試官學正范 批〔論題涉性理最難下筆此作滚滚千餘言開闔抑揚變化萬〕
punctuated:
而化自行也。孰謂政教之本猶不在是乎？故曰：「觀于鄉而知王道之易易也。」益可見矣。雖然，是禮也，三年大比，興賢者能者，與夫諸侯之卿大夫貢士於其君，類如此。有志於復古者，果能舉而行之，則孝弟日興，造士以告于王而升諸司馬者，固濟濟如也。然則鄉飲與王制殆相爲表裏者乎？
第貳塲
論
忠恕違道不遠
糟士奇
同考試官教諭冀批〔檃括中庸一篇之意殆盡，又且句句不離道與忠恕，間有道出〕前人所未嘗道者，於理深矣。關西之學倡自橫渠，若子豈非勃然而興者耶？筆力千鈞，姑未暇論。
考試官學正范批〔論題涉性理，最難下筆。此作滚滚千餘言，開闔抑揚，變化萬〕
translation_en:
…and moral transformation proceeds of itself. Who could say that the foundation of government and instruction does not lie in this? Thus it is said: “By observing the village ceremony, one comes to understand how very easy the kingly Way is.” This is now all the more apparent. Nevertheless, this rite—at the great assessment held every three years, when men of virtue and ability are advanced, and when the ministers and grandees of the regional lords present worthy men to their rulers—takes much the same form. If those intent on restoring antiquity can indeed put it into practice, filial piety and fraternal deference will flourish daily, and accomplished scholars reported to the king and advanced to the Minister of War will assuredly be numerous and distinguished. Thus, are the village drinking ceremony and the “Royal Regulations” not, perhaps, complementary aspects of one whole?
Second Session
Discourse
“Conscientiousness and Reciprocity Are Not Far from the Way”
Zao Shiqi
Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: 〔This encompasses virtually the entire meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean; moreover, every sentence stays close to the Way and to conscientiousness and reciprocity. At times it expresses〕 what earlier writers have never expressed: its understanding of principle is profound. Learning in Guanxi was first championed by Hengqu; are you not one of those who have risen vigorously in response? Your brush has the force of a thousand jun; for the moment, I have no leisure to discuss that.
Comment by Examiner Fan, School Director: 〔Discourse topics involving human nature and principle are the hardest to begin writing on. This composition flows on for more than a thousand words, opening and closing, restraining and elevating, varying in myriad …〕

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
狀讀之使人忘倦固以至文說至理耶噫
亦奇矣
味哉
考試官教授林　批　本動以天說來有
道者天而已乎君子脩其人以至之則幾
矣夫天人之勢至遠也而理尤至近也勢
固不可以遽合理亦不可以終離苟徒執
其勢而强諉之曰吾未幾于天斯求諸天
而已矣人何爲哉是欲一蹴而至道者耶
===
道可一蹴而至天下無愚人矣吾見其愈
不幾也君子則曰天之未幾惟人可至理
也人之大者孰有如忠恕乎于是充之乎
一心之間達之乎萬事之表則人至人至
則天至天至則道至何也道不遠人其理
固合而不離也吾以人求之則人亦不遠
道人不遠道而違道也又豈遠乎吾見其
幾矣忠恕違道不遠天人之謂也且道何
以謂之天也以其出於天故謂之天也天
punctuated:
狀，讀之使人忘倦，固以至文說至理耶？噫，亦奇矣！味哉！
考試官教授林，批：「本動以天說來有。」
道者，天而已乎？君子脩其人以至之，則幾矣。夫天人之勢至遠也，而理尤至近也。勢固不可以遽合，理亦不可以終離。苟徒執其勢而强諉之曰：「吾未幾于天，斯求諸天而已矣，人何爲哉？」是欲一蹴而至道者耶？道可一蹴而至，天下無愚人矣。吾見其愈不幾也。君子則曰：「天之未幾，惟人可至，理也。」人之大者，孰有如忠恕乎？于是充之乎一心之間，達之乎萬事之表，則人至；人至則天至，天至則道至。何也？道不遠人，其理固合而不離也。吾以人求之，則人亦不遠道。人不遠道，而違道也，又豈遠乎？吾見其幾矣。忠恕違道不遠，天人之謂也。且道何以謂之天也？以其出於天，故謂之天也。天
translation_en:
…forms: reading it makes one forget weariness. Is this not consummate writing expounding the highest principles? Ah, extraordinary indeed! How much there is to savor!
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “The opening develops its explanation in terms of Heaven [?].”
Is the Way simply Heaven? If the gentleman cultivates his human capacities to attain it, he will come close. Heaven and humanity are exceedingly distant in their respective positions, yet exceedingly close in principle. Though their positions cannot suddenly be brought together, neither can their principle remain forever divided. Suppose someone merely insists upon that distance and offers the forced excuse: “I have not come close to Heaven, so I shall seek only in Heaven. What can human effort accomplish?” Is this someone who wishes to reach the Way in a single leap? If the Way could be reached in a single leap, there would be no foolish people in the world. I see such a person coming ever less close to it. The gentleman, however, says: “Though Heaven has not yet been approached, it can be reached through human effort alone: this is the principle.” Among the great human virtues, what compares with doing one’s utmost and treating others as oneself—zhong and shu? Thus, when one brings these to fullness within one’s heart and extends them to the outward realm of all affairs, human fulfillment is attained. When human fulfillment is attained, Heaven is attained; when Heaven is attained, the Way is attained. Why? The Way is not far from people: their principle is inherently united and inseparable. If I seek it through humanity, then humanity, too, is not far from the Way. If people are not far from the Way, how could their distance from it be great? I see them coming close. The saying “Doing one’s utmost and treating others as oneself are not far from the Way” speaks of Heaven and humanity. Moreover, why is the Way called Heaven? Because it issues from Heaven, it is called Heaven. What Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
命之謂性率性之謂道性出於天道非出
於天而出於性是卽出於天矣則謂之天
罔宜是故子之孝臣之忠弟之敬朋友之
先施皆道也皆天命之所以不可已者也
夫道雖出於天尤自率性而得之性也者
我之所固有反而求之昭昭如焉固非奪
諸彼以與諸此取諸塗而强置于懷也則
豈遠于人乎故曰其理合而不離也聖人
不思不勉厥動以天與道一而已矣夫何
===
形生智發氣質雜揉有智者賢者愚者不
肖者愚不肖瞠乎不及于道賢智則又踰
而過之而道始遠矣天人之勢始出矣于
是乎不得不求諸人而况天亦有待于人
耶人者何忠恕之謂也忠者何盡已之謂
也恕者何推已之謂也忠恕者何盡已以
推已之謂也忠主於内以立其恕恕達於
外以行其忠人斯盡矣苟求道者但知道
者天也道失乃遽皇皇然于天焉求之忠
punctuated: 命之謂性，率性之謂道。性出於天，道非出於天而出於性，是卽出於天矣，則謂之天罔宜。是故子之孝、臣之忠、弟之敬、朋友之先施，皆道也，皆天命之所以不可已者也。夫道雖出於天，尤自率性而得之。性也者，我之所固有，反而求之，昭昭如焉，固非奪諸彼以與諸此，取諸塗而强置于懷也，則豈遠于人乎？故曰其理合而不離也。聖人不思不勉，厥動以天，與道一而已矣。夫何形生智發，氣質雜揉，有智者、賢者、愚者、不肖者。愚不肖瞠乎不及于道，賢智則又踰而過之，而道始遠矣，天人之勢始出矣。于是乎不得不求諸人，而况天亦有待于人耶？人者何？忠恕之謂也。忠者何？盡已之謂也。恕者何？推已之謂也。忠恕者何？盡已以推已之謂也。忠主於内以立其恕，恕達於外以行其忠，人斯盡矣。苟求道者但知道者天也，道失乃遽皇皇然于天焉求之，忠
translation_en:
…what [Heaven] commands is called human nature; following that nature is called the Way. Human nature comes from Heaven. The Way comes not directly from Heaven but from human nature, and thus it does indeed come from Heaven. To call it Heaven is therefore appropriate [?]. Thus a son's filial devotion, a minister's loyalty, a younger brother's respect, and taking the initiative in showing kindness to friends are all the Way. They are all expressions of Heaven's command that cannot cease. Although the Way comes from Heaven, it is attained especially through following one's nature. This nature is inherently ours: turn inward and seek it, and it is manifestly clear. It is certainly not something seized from there and given here, or picked up from the road and forcibly thrust into one's bosom. How, then, could it be far from human beings? Hence I say that their principles are united and inseparable. The sage acts without deliberation or effort; his every movement accords with Heaven, and he is simply one with the Way.
How is it, then, that when bodily form comes into being and intelligence emerges, differing endowments of vital energy mingle, producing the wise, the worthy, the foolish, and the unworthy? The foolish and unworthy stare helplessly, unable to reach the Way, while the worthy and wise overstep it. Only then does the Way become distant, and a separation between Heaven and humanity emerges. Thus one cannot but seek it in the human sphere—and does not Heaven itself also depend upon human effort? What is meant by the human sphere? Wholeheartedness and sympathetic understanding. What is wholeheartedness? Fully exerting oneself. What is sympathetic understanding? Extending one's understanding of oneself to others. What are wholeheartedness and sympathetic understanding together? Fully exerting oneself so as to extend that understanding to others. Wholeheartedness presides within, establishing sympathetic understanding; sympathetic understanding reaches outward, putting wholeheartedness into practice. In this way, human effort is fulfilled. If those who seek the Way know only that the Way is Heaven, then, upon losing the Way, they hastily and anxiously seek it in Heaven, while wholeheartedness…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
恕之在人者則曰卑矣近矣是不足以至
道殆猶望泰山之高輒揹其階超足而登
之吾見其幾者幾希君子于是惟盡已乎
爾惟推已乎爾又惟盡已以推已乎爾盡
已則忠立推已則恕行盡已以推已則忠
恕並至忠立天下之大本之所存也恕行
天下之達道之所發也忠恕並至則天命
之性率性之道亦無不幾焉曰違道不遠
至矣哉憂之遠而言之切也今夫吾之子
===
若臣若弟若朋友強施我以不欲吾艴然
矣則盡其心以推之吾父吾君吾兄與夫
朋友不欲猶夫吾也乃勿施諸父勿施諸
君勿施諸弟勿施諸朋友是卽忠恕之事
也由是而之焉孝不遠矣忠不遠矣敬不
遠矣先施不遠矣斯其明效也是則直求
天於天者始不可及勢離而理亦離也反
而求諸人則可以幾之理合而勢亦合也
然則君子豈棄天者哉正欲盡人以至乎
punctuated:
恕之在人者，則曰卑矣，近矣，是不足以至道。殆猶望泰山之高，輒揹其階，超足而登之，吾見其幾者幾希。君子于是惟盡已乎爾，惟推已乎爾，又惟盡已以推已乎爾。盡已則忠立，推已則恕行，盡已以推已則忠恕並至。忠立，天下之大本之所存也；恕行，天下之達道之所發也；忠恕並至，則天命之性、率性之道，亦無不幾焉。曰「違道不遠」，至矣哉！憂之遠而言之切也。
今夫吾之子，若臣，若弟，若朋友，強施我以不欲，吾艴然矣。則盡其心以推之，吾父、吾君、吾兄與夫朋友，不欲猶夫吾也。乃勿施諸父，勿施諸君，勿施諸弟，勿施諸朋友，是卽忠恕之事也。由是而之焉，孝不遠矣，忠不遠矣，敬不遠矣，先施不遠矣，斯其明效也。是則直求天於天者，始不可及，勢離而理亦離也；反而求諸人，則可以幾之，理合而勢亦合也。然則君子豈棄天者哉？正欲盡人以至乎
translation_en:
…as for reciprocity as it resides in human beings, they say: “It is lowly and close at hand; it is insufficient for attaining the Way.” This is much like gazing at the height of Mount Tai, then turning one’s back on its steps and trying to scale it in a leap. I see very few who come anywhere near success. The gentleman therefore simply does his utmost, extends consideration from himself to others, and, further, does his utmost in thus extending consideration. Doing his utmost establishes wholeheartedness; extending consideration puts reciprocity into practice. Doing his utmost in extending consideration brings both wholeheartedness and reciprocity to fulfillment. In the establishment of wholeheartedness resides the great foundation of all under Heaven; in the practice of reciprocity manifests the universally applicable Way of all under Heaven. When both reach fulfillment, one can approach both the nature conferred by Heaven’s mandate and the Way of following that nature. The saying “They are not far from the Way” is consummate indeed! Its concern is far-reaching and its words earnest.
Now, if my son, minister, younger brother, or friend forcibly imposes on me something I do not desire, I become angry. If I then fully apply my heart and extend this understanding to others, I recognize that my father, ruler, elder brother, and friends have things they do not desire, just as I do. Thus I do not impose these things on my father, my ruler, my younger brother [?], or my friends. This is precisely the work of wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Proceeding in this way, filial devotion is not far off, loyalty is not far off, respect is not far off, and taking the initiative in kindness toward friends is not far off. These are its manifest effects. Thus, when one seeks Heaven directly in Heaven, it proves beyond reach: circumstances are divorced, and principle is divorced as well. But if one turns back and seeks it in human beings, one can approach it: principle is united, and circumstances are united as well. Does the gentleman, then, abandon Heaven? He precisely wishes to fulfill what is human in order to reach…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天孳孳焉使天爲可以幾也他日子貢問
所以終身行之者亦曰其恕乎蓋終身行
之者道也忠恕違道不遠故特以是命之
即中庸之意也而不及忠者恕自忠出言
恕則忠在其中矣曾子又曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣此正動以天之謂也動以天則
己無待於盡且推矣君子誠能盡之又盡
至於無所不盡無所盡推之又推至於無
所不推無所推則至乎夫子之忠恕而渾
===
然與道爲一矣由是乎可以致中和之極
即天地無不位萬物無不育焉夫不遠者
殆又奚足論耶雖然惟忠恕可以至道惟
誠可以語忠恕何也蓋有誠而後有忠有
忠而後有恕一不誠則皆虛器矣是故純
亦不已聖人所以爲忠恕也惟夫曾子眞
積之久夫後能得之然則君子欲以至乎
忠恕者抑惟誠之爲貴乎
表
punctuated:
天，孳孳焉使天爲可以幾也。他日，子貢問所以終身行之者，亦曰：「其恕乎！」蓋終身行之者，道也。忠恕違道不遠，故特以是命之，即中庸之意也。而不及忠者，恕自忠出，言恕則忠在其中矣。曾子又曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」此正動以天之謂也。動以天，則己無待於盡且推矣。君子誠能盡之又盡，至於無所不盡、無所盡；推之又推，至於無所不推、無所推，則至乎夫子之忠恕，而渾然與道爲一矣。由是乎可以致中和之極，即天地無不位，萬物無不育焉。夫不遠者，殆又奚足論耶！雖然，惟忠恕可以至道，惟誠可以語忠恕。何也？蓋有誠而後有忠，有忠而後有恕，一不誠則皆虛器矣。是故「純亦不已」，聖人所以爲忠恕也。惟夫曾子眞積之久，夫後能得之。然則君子欲以至乎忠恕者，抑惟誠之爲貴乎！

表
translation_en:
…Heaven, diligently striving to make Heaven attainable. On another occasion, when Zigong asked what one could practice throughout one’s life, the Master likewise said, “Surely it is reciprocity!” What one practices throughout one’s life is the Way. Since wholeheartedness and reciprocity are not far from the Way, he specifically instructed him in these terms. This is precisely the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean. His failure to mention wholeheartedness was because reciprocity proceeds from wholeheartedness: when reciprocity is spoken of, wholeheartedness is already included. Zengzi also said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of wholeheartedness and reciprocity.” This is precisely what is meant by acting through Heaven. When one acts through Heaven, one no longer needs the effort of fully realizing oneself and extending this to others. If the gentleman can truly realize himself fully, again and again, until nothing is left unrealized and nothing remains to be realized, and extend this to others, again and again, until nothing is excluded and nothing remains to which it must be extended, he will attain the Master’s wholeheartedness and reciprocity and become wholly one with the Way. Through this he can bring equilibrium and harmony to their utmost realization: Heaven and Earth will each occupy their proper place, and all things will receive their nourishment. What need would there then be even to speak of being merely “not far” from the Way?

Nevertheless, only through wholeheartedness and reciprocity can one attain the Way, and only with sincerity can one speak of wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Why? Only with sincerity is there wholeheartedness, and only with wholeheartedness is there reciprocity. Once sincerity is absent, all become empty vessels. Thus, “purity likewise never ceases”: this is how the sage practices wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Only after Zengzi had long accumulated genuine effort could he grasp this. For the gentleman who wishes to attain wholeheartedness and reciprocity, then, must sincerity not be what is most prized?

Memorials

四六子固能之耶
考試官教授林　批　麗而有則是工於
四六者
臣詠言伏蒙
聖恩以臣知益州得便宜從事者寵溢韜鈐特
倍表方之任令優節鉞尤專制閫之權顯
服
寵光私憂奮負臣詠誠惶誠恐頓首頓首竊以

punctuated:
擬宋以張詠知益州得便宜從事謝表
化五年
喬世寧

同考試官教諭許批：通篇皆組織忠定及蜀郡事，煥若指掌。至便宜處，尤歸尊于朝廷。予固頃刻不忘君者耶？博學工文，抑餘事耳。

考試官學正范批：婉而有則，雅而有文，洋洋巨篇，皆出天然語。昔温公嘗謂不能四六，子固能之耶？

考試官教授林批：麗而有則，是工於四六者。

臣詠言：伏蒙聖恩，以臣知益州，得便宜從事者，寵溢韜鈐，特倍表方之任；令優節鉞，尤專制閫之權。顯服寵光，私憂奮負。臣詠誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首。竊以强立功名，偶占負俗之士；優當盤錯，終資
translation_en:
A memorial of thanks composed in the persona of Zhang Yong of the Song, upon his appointment as Prefect of Yizhou with authority to act at his discretion.
Fifth year of Hua [?].
Qiao Shining.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: The entire piece weaves together events concerning Zhongding [Zhang Yong’s posthumous title] and the Shu region, presenting them as clearly as the palm of one’s hand. In treating discretionary authority, it especially accords supremacy to the imperial court. Surely [he?] is one who never forgets his sovereign for an instant. Broad learning and literary skill are merely secondary accomplishments.

Comment by Examiner Fan, School Instructor: Graceful yet disciplined, elegant and accomplished: this expansive composition consists entirely of natural expressions. Lord Wen [Sima Guang] once said that he could not compose four-six parallel prose. You certainly can, can you not?

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: Beautiful yet disciplined: this is the work of someone skilled in four-six parallel prose.

Your servant Yong states: I have humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious favor, appointing me Prefect of Yizhou and authorizing me to act at my discretion. Your favor abundantly equips me with military authority, especially increasing the responsibility of serving as an exemplar for a region; your command grants generous authority through the credentials and battle-axe of command, particularly entrusting me with control over affairs beyond the threshold. Publicly I receive this glorious favor; privately I anxiously strive to bear its burden [?]. Your servant Yong, truly apprehensive and truly fearful, bows his head to the ground, bows his head to the ground.

I humbly consider that those who resolutely establish merit and reputation may sometimes be men who defy prevailing conventions; to deal with tangled roots and knotted wood with ease ultimately requires …

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
利器之賢官在惟人任求厥稱故賢主益
書屛之愼明王極推轂之嚴伏念臣詠斻
僻迂流乖崖拙品少甘學劒長略知書貧
賤客遊獨抱下人之恥剛方自許因成任
氣之爊初試乙科歷躋膴仕强幹誤聞
當宁朴忠偶薦同朝夢協三刀邊徼符於明
府地凌九折幸蟳節於忠臣雖猥貽不拘
小節之稱詎敢嬰自當一面之寄茲蓋伏
遇
===
沉謀淵默
英斷雷行北漢揚旗力遽剪其孤壘東遼
聲復震乎三關昭
文武之丕資恢
帝王之遠略睠彼靈關之地昔稱天險之區王
壘參儀咽喉諸郡銅梁重阻襟帶兩川竊
憤兇殘深憑險固肆脅民而爲盜敢鼓衆
以興訛亡命爭依堅城遂陷遊魂突釜覬
punctuated: 利器之賢。官在惟人，任求厥稱。故賢主益書屛之愼，明王極推轂之嚴。伏念臣詠，斻僻迂流，乖崖拙品；少甘學劒，長略知書。貧賤客遊，獨抱下人之恥；剛方自許，因成任氣之爊。初試乙科，歷躋膴仕。强幹誤聞當宁，朴忠偶薦同朝。夢協三刀，邊徼符於明府；地凌九折，幸蟳節於忠臣。雖猥貽不拘小節之稱，詎敢嬰自當一面之寄？茲蓋伏遇沉謀淵默，英斷雷行。北漢揚旗，力遽剪其孤壘；東遼聲復震乎三關。昭文武之丕資，恢帝王之遠略。睠彼靈關之地，昔稱天險之區。王壘參儀，咽喉諸郡；銅梁重阻，襟帶兩川。竊憤兇殘，深憑險固，肆脅民而爲盜，敢鼓衆以興訛。亡命爭依，堅城遂陷。遊魂突釜，覬
translation_en:
…worthy men whose abilities are like sharp instruments. Offices depend upon the men who hold them, and appointments must match their qualifications. Thus worthy rulers exercise still greater care in inscribing names upon their screens, and enlightened kings are most exacting when sending commanders forth.

I, your servant Yong, humbly reflect that I am eccentric and impractical [?], obstinate in disposition and clumsy in character. In youth I delighted in swordsmanship; as I grew older, I acquired a little knowledge of books. Poor and of humble station, I traveled as a sojourner, privately nursing the shame of being beneath others. Priding myself on firmness and uprightness, I thereby developed the fault of acting on impulse [?]. I first passed the examination in the second class and subsequently rose through well-remunerated offices. An undeserved reputation for strength and competence reached Your Majesty; my plain loyalty happened to win recommendations from colleagues at court. The dream of three knives proved auspicious: an appointment on the frontier fell to me as prefect. The terrain rises over the Nine Bends; fortunately, a loyal servant’s integrity was upheld [?]. Though I have undeservedly received praise for not being constrained by petty details, how could I dare shoulder the responsibility of independently commanding an entire region?

This has come about because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, profound and silent in deliberation, brilliant and thunderous in decisive action. When your banners were raised against Northern Han, your might swiftly destroyed its isolated stronghold; in eastern Liao, your renown again shook the Three Passes. You manifested your great gifts in civil and military affairs and extended the far-reaching strategy of an emperor.

Consider the land of Lingguan, long known as a region of natural defenses. Wanglei rises majestically [?], forming the throat of the various commanderies; Tongliang’s successive barriers bind together the two regions of Chuan. I am privately indignant that savage men, relying heavily upon these formidable defenses, brazenly coerced the people into banditry and dared to incite the multitude by spreading false rumors. Fugitives flocked to their support, and fortified cities consequently fell. These wandering spirits burst out of the cauldron [?], hoping to…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
公孫躍馬之長怒臂當車逞劉闢發兵之
計一方滋毒釁已積於踰年三帥屯軍機
每妨於愒日星書告急
旰食軫懷遂謂紓
朕之憂私計非卿不可尚謬六條之政乃承千
里之師尤以救變須出於常經謀大難膠
於小節毋拘文法襲遂安渤海之民外決
軍功李牧滅襜林之寇特委推心之信預
消掣肘之艱發許後聞動由中制畏布得
===
由四體精白天盡一心息民則文翁之遺
軌惟稽定亂則諸葛之前規是繹省文弛
禁計欲出於萬全赴會投機功必成於一
舉益盡寅恭而將事務期處置之得宜劒
閣馳驅畢枕戈之志華陽底定用成傳
檄之休尤念尊在
朝廷專惟
社稷一張一弛雖微臣之智無常作福作威終
明辟之公有在臣無任感
punctuated: 公孫躍馬之長，怒臂當車，逞劉闢發兵之計。一方滋毒，釁已積於踰年；三帥屯軍，機每妨於愒日。星書告急，旰食軫懷，遂謂：「紓朕之憂，私計非卿不可。」尚謬六條之政，乃承千里之師。尤以救變須出於常經，謀大難膠於小節。毋拘文法，襲遂安渤海之民；外決軍功，李牧滅襜林之寇。特委推心之信，預消掣肘之艱。發許後聞，動由中制。畏布得由四體，精白天盡一心。息民則文翁之遺軌惟稽，定亂則諸葛之前規是繹。省文弛禁，計欲出於萬全；赴會投機，功必成於一舉。益盡寅恭而將事，務期處置之得宜。劒閣馳驅，畢枕戈之志；華陽底定，用成傳檄之休。尤念尊在朝廷，專惟社稷。一張一弛，雖微臣之智無常；作福作威，終明辟之公有在。臣無任感
translation_en:
…the enduring ascendancy of Gongsun riding to power [?]; like a mantis raising its arms against a carriage, they pursued Liu Pi’s scheme of raising troops. Their poison spread throughout the region, and their offenses accumulated for more than a year. Three commanders encamped their armies, but opportunities were repeatedly lost through procrastination. Urgent dispatches reported the crisis; Your Majesty, delaying your meal until late in the day, was deeply concerned. You therefore declared: “To relieve my anxiety, I judge privately that no one but you will do.” Though I still unworthily administered the government under the Six Articles, I was now entrusted with an army operating a thousand li away.

Above all, responding to an emergency requires going beyond ordinary rules, and planning great undertakings cannot be constrained by minor details. Unfettered by legal formalities, Xi Sui [?] brought peace to the people of Bohai; deciding military affairs in the field, Li Mu destroyed the raiders of Chanlin. You especially entrusted me with your wholehearted confidence, forestalling the difficulties of interference. I was permitted to act first and report afterward, while my actions remained subject to direction from the center. Awe was to extend through all four limbs [?], and pure sincerity was to exhaust the devotion of a single heart [?]. To bring repose to the people, I would consult the precedents left by Wen Weng; to quell disorder, I would examine the earlier methods of Zhuge Liang. By reducing formalities and relaxing prohibitions, my plans sought complete security; by responding to circumstances and seizing opportunities, success must be achieved in a single undertaking.

With still greater reverence I would carry out my duties, striving to ensure that every measure was appropriate. Hastening to Jiange, I would fulfill my resolve to sleep with my weapon as my pillow; bringing Huayang to peace, I would achieve the glorious result of pacification through the circulation of a proclamation. Above all, I bear in mind that supreme authority rests with the imperial court, and that my delegated discretion serves only the altars of soil and grain. In tightening or relaxing measures, the judgment of your insignificant servant may vary with circumstances; but the power to bestow blessings and wield punishments ultimately remains vested in the impartial authority of the enlightened sovereign. Your servant cannot contain his gratitude…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄

punctuated:
□稱□，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場，策，第一問。沈麒。

同考試官教諭方批〔正心之論，先儒嘗言之，作者亦往往宗其旨。至以進君子、退小人爲輔，則未之及。夫君子不進，小人不退，心亦安能正耶？子可謂善告君者。得士如此，可以賀矣！〕

同考試官教諭陳批〔敷陳〕聖學，而拳拳於天理人欲之分、君子小人之辨，因事納忠，子誠得其道乎！

考試官學正范批〔結用主敬窮理，尤〕
translation_en:
…[opening formula partly illegible: ?], with the utmost fervor and trembling apprehension, I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks to Your Majesty.

Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question. Shen Qi.

Associate Examiner, Instructor Fang, comments: 〔Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed rectifying the mind, and writers frequently follow their purport. Yet they have not gone so far as to make advancing exemplary men and dismissing petty men its supporting measures. If exemplary men are not advanced and petty men are not dismissed, how can the mind be rectified? You may indeed be called one who knows how to counsel a ruler. Obtaining a scholar such as this is cause for congratulations!〕

Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen, comments: 〔You expound〕 the learning of the sage ruler, earnestly attending to the distinction between Heavenly principle and human desires, and to distinguishing exemplary men from petty men. Offering loyal counsel as the occasion presents itself, you have truly grasped the proper way!

Examiner, School Instructor Fan, comments: 〔The conclusion employs maintaining reverent attentiveness and investigating principle, especially…〕

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
為㖿𥈞子欲堯舜吾
君者耶
考試官教授林　批
流出
考試官教授林　批　忠愛之意自方寸
大哉人君之學乎正心術以植其本辨人
材以廣其助斯可以語要矣政不能以自
行于是乎有本德不可以孤立于是乎有
助無本則雜雜則靡無助則離離則陋學
至於雜且離而靡而陋焉經生學士猶或
===
恥之矣彼心術者事物之宗也故正心術
而謂之本也人材者君身之輔也故辨人
材而謂之助也人君之學誠能嚴理欲以
清治亂之源別忠邪以定取舍之極則本
立於上而下之翼而助之者衆矣猶曰非
要焉固不可也范氏曰人主學與不學係
天下治亂故道惟學而巳矣程子曰帝王
之學苟得其要無難也故學惟要而巳矣
西山眞氏又曰惟學可以養此心惟親近
punctuated:
為㖿𥈞，子欲堯舜吾君者耶？
考試官教授林，批：流出。
考試官教授林，批：忠愛之意自方寸。
大哉，人君之學乎！正心術以植其本，辨人材以廣其助，斯可以語要矣。政不能以自行，於是乎有本；德不可以孤立，於是乎有助。無本則雜，雜則靡；無助則離，離則陋。學至於雜且離，而靡而陋焉，經生學士猶或恥之矣。彼心術者，事物之宗也，故正心術而謂之本也；人材者，君身之輔也，故辨人材而謂之助也。人君之學，誠能嚴理欲以清治亂之源，別忠邪以定取舍之極，則本立於上，而下之翼而助之者衆矣。猶曰非要焉，固不可也。范氏曰：「人主學與不學，係天下治亂。」故道惟學而巳矣。程子曰：「帝王之學，苟得其要，無難也。」故學惟要而巳矣。西山眞氏又曰：「惟學可以養此心，惟親近
translation_en:
…[opening characters unclear: 為㖿𥈞]. Are you one who wishes to make our ruler a Yao or a Shun?
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Flows forth.” [?]
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “The feeling of loyalty and love comes from the heart.” [The two comment fragments appear disordered.]
Great indeed is the learning of a ruler! He rectifies the workings of his mind to establish its foundation and discriminates among men of talent to broaden its support: only then can we speak of grasping its essentials. Government cannot carry itself out; hence the need for a foundation. Virtue cannot stand alone; hence the need for support. Without a foundation, learning becomes confused, and confusion leads to dissipation; without support, it becomes isolated, and isolation leads to narrowness. When learning becomes confused and isolated, dissipated and narrow, even students of the classics and scholars may feel ashamed of it.
The workings of the mind are the source of affairs and things; thus, rectifying them is called the foundation. Men of talent are the ruler’s aids; thus, discriminating among them is called support. If, in his learning, a ruler can rigorously distinguish principle from desire, thereby purifying the source of order and disorder, and distinguish loyalty from wickedness, thereby establishing the ultimate standard for acceptance and rejection, then the foundation will be established above, and many below will sustain and assist him. To say that this is still not essential would surely be untenable.
Master Fan said: “Whether the ruler studies or not determines whether the realm is orderly or disordered.” Thus, the Way lies in learning alone. Master Cheng said: “In the learning of emperors and kings, if they grasp its essentials, there is no difficulty.” Thus, learning lies solely in grasping the essentials. Master Zhen of Xishan also said: “Only learning can nurture this mind; only drawing close to…”

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遠涪陵之禍其於心術何如也或縱許史
干政或寵馬竇專國或蔽宇文士及而殺
張蘊古或狎李林甫而疎張九齡或任盧
多遜而疑趙普其於人材何如也夫學之
要數君者皆罔罔然則玄宗得免於亡餘
免於亂幸矣而欲企隆古之治窺粹白之
道不亦難乎哉洪惟
皇上聰明齊聖躬上聖之資嘉靖興邦撫中興
之運茲者特降
===
睿旨爰命侍臣處分詩易類次中庸析尚書之
大旨以爲詩賦詞章之體輯通鑑之要語
以爲直解講章之文用進日
覽兼備燕覲典學之勤望道之切皇皇如也
夫衆目紛紜提綱則順羣言糾錯舉要則
精而其要若詩之毋貳爾心及夫青蠅刺
讒緇衣好賢易之直內方外與履霜剝廬
之戒鶴鳴鴻漸之休書之惟精惟一與簡
脩進良之法聖說殄行之事至於中庸戒
punctuated:
遠涪陵之禍，其於心術何如也？或縱許史干政，或寵馬竇專國，或蔽宇文士及而殺張蘊古，或狎李林甫而疎張九齡，或任盧多遜而疑趙普，其於人材何如也？夫學之要，數君者皆罔罔然，則玄宗得免於亡，餘免於亂，幸矣！而欲企隆古之治，窺粹白之道，不亦難乎哉？
洪惟皇上聰明齊聖，躬上聖之資，嘉靖興邦，撫中興之運。茲者特降睿旨，爰命侍臣處分《詩》《易》，類次《中庸》，析《尚書》之大旨，以爲詩賦詞章之體；輯《通鑑》之要語，以爲直解講章之文，用進日覽，兼備燕覲。典學之勤，望道之切，皇皇如也！夫衆目紛紜，提綱則順；羣言糾錯，舉要則精。而其要，若《詩》之「毋貳爾心」，及夫《青蠅》刺讒、《緇衣》好賢；《易》之直內方外，與履霜、剝廬之戒，鶴鳴、鴻漸之休；《書》之「惟精惟一」，與簡脩進良之法、聖說殄行之事；至於《中庸》戒
translation_en:
…to avert the calamity of Fuling: how did this reflect upon the disposition of his mind? Some allowed the Xu and Shi families to interfere in government; some favored the Ma and Dou families and let them monopolize state power; some were blinded by Yuwen Shiji and put Zhang Yungu to death; some were intimate with Li Linfu and estranged Zhang Jiuling; some entrusted affairs to Lu Duoxun and distrusted Zhao Pu. How did this reflect upon their judgment of men of talent? These several rulers were all utterly bewildered concerning the essentials of learning. That Xuanzong escaped destruction, and the others escaped disorder, was fortunate indeed! Yet if they wished to aspire to the government of high antiquity and glimpse the way of unalloyed purity, would that not have been difficult?
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty possesses intelligence and sagacity equal to the sages, personally endowed with the qualities of the highest sage. Bringing auspicious peace and revitalizing the realm, you preside over an age of restoration. Recently you specially issued an imperial instruction, commanding attendant officials to arrange the Book of Poetry and the Book of Changes, classify and order the Doctrine of the Mean, and analyze the principal meanings of the Book of Documents, presenting these in the forms of poetry, rhapsodies, and literary compositions; and to compile essential passages from the Comprehensive Mirror into plainly explained lecture texts. These were to be submitted for daily perusal and also made available for informal audiences [?]. How tireless is your diligence in pursuing learning, and how earnest your aspiration toward the Way!
When the many particulars are bewilderingly numerous, grasping their main thread puts them in order; when the many teachings are intertwined, bringing out their essentials makes them clear and precise. Such essentials include, in the Book of Poetry, “Do not be divided in your heart,” together with “Blue Flies,” which censures slander, and “Black Robes,” which expresses love for the worthy; in the Book of Changes, being upright within and square without, together with the warnings conveyed by treading on frost and stripping away a dwelling, and the auspicious images of a calling crane and a wild goose advancing gradually; in the Book of Documents, “Be discerning; be single-minded,” together with the methods of selecting the cultivated and advancing the good, and the matter of “sage words” [?] and conduct that brings ruin. As for the Doctrine of the Mean’s admonition…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君子可以維持此心故要惟正心術辨人
材而已矣何也葢心術之微天理人欲之
攸分也天理長則開清明之化人欲肆則
甚蔽固之私是以不可不正也人材之衆
君子小人之攸聚也君子用則廣忠諫之
益小人進則興蠱惑之端是以不可不辨
也昔堯舜禹湯文武之爲學也慎危微之
戒合義禮之防崇緝熈之功服敬怠之訓
孰不以正心術爲本乎陟明命德黜幽去
===
凶顯忠遂良刑懲覆暴用吉士屏憸人灼
俊心斥利口孰不以辨人材爲助乎其要
固各在也沿及漢宣帝臨石渠以决五經
之異同章帝登白虎以析諸儒之講議唐
太宗分夜觀書於槖鞬之餘玄宗更日侍
讀於閤門之内宋太宗日讀太平御覽三
卷隆冬短晷必足其數孰謂其學之不勤
也哉然或好刑名之術或湛宫闈之禍或
假仁盜名或窮欲致亂或渝金匱之盟以
punctuated:
君子可以維持此心，故要惟正心術、辨人材而已矣。何也？葢心術之微，天理人欲之攸分也。天理長，則開清明之化；人欲肆，則甚蔽固之私，是以不可不正也。人材之衆，君子小人之攸聚也。君子用，則廣忠諫之益；小人進，則興蠱惑之端，是以不可不辨也。昔堯舜禹湯文武之爲學也，慎危微之戒，合義禮之防，崇緝熈之功，服敬怠之訓，孰不以正心術爲本乎？陟明命德，黜幽去凶，顯忠遂良，刑懲覆暴，用吉士，屏憸人，灼俊心，斥利口，孰不以辨人材爲助乎？其要固各在也。
沿及漢宣帝臨石渠以决五經之異同，章帝登白虎以析諸儒之講議，唐太宗分夜觀書於槖鞬之餘，玄宗更日侍讀於閤門之内，宋太宗日讀太平御覽三卷，隆冬短晷，必足其數，孰謂其學之不勤也哉？然或好刑名之術，或湛宫闈之禍，或假仁盜名，或窮欲致亂，或渝金匱之盟以
translation_en:
…the gentleman can thereby sustain this mind. Thus the essentials are simply to rectify the dispositions of the mind and distinguish among men of talent. Why is this? The subtle workings of the mind are where heavenly principle and human desires diverge. When heavenly principle grows, it ushers in enlightened governance; when human desires run unchecked, they intensify the selfishness that clouds and confines the mind. Hence these dispositions must be rectified. Among the many men of talent, gentlemen and petty men gather together. When gentlemen are employed, the benefits of loyal remonstrance increase; when petty men advance, occasions for deception and confusion arise. Hence they must be distinguished.
When Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu pursued learning, they heeded the warning about the precarious human mind and the subtle moral mind, conformed to the restraints of righteousness and ritual propriety, cultivated the work of continuing enlightenment, and observed the injunctions concerning reverence and indolence. Which of them did not take rectifying the dispositions of the mind as his foundation? They promoted the discerning and appointed the virtuous, dismissed the benighted and removed the wicked, honored the loyal and advanced the good, imposed punishments and overthrew the violent, employed worthy men and banished the deceitful, discerned the hearts of the talented and rejected glib speakers. Which of them did not take distinguishing among men of talent as an aid? Each of these essentials was assuredly present.
Coming down to later times, Emperor Xuandi of the Han presided at Shiqu to settle differences in interpretations of the Five Classics, and Emperor Zhangdi convened at Baihu to examine the scholars’ discussions. Emperor Taizong of the Tang set aside part of the night to read after his military duties; Xuanzong had readers attend him on alternating days within the palace gates. Emperor Taizong of the Song read three juan of the Imperial Digest of the Taiping Era each day; even in the short days of deepest winter, he invariably completed that number. Who could say that they were not diligent in learning? Yet one favored the techniques of penal administration, another became engulfed in calamities within the palace, another feigned benevolence to steal a good name, another pursued his desires to the utmost and brought about disorder, and another violated the covenant of the golden coffer in order to…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
懼慎獨以入道去讒貴德以勸賢孰有大
於正心術辨人材者耶若夫通鑑所載大
者如董仲舒曰正心以正朝廷正朝廷以
正百官栁公權曰用筆在心心正則筆正
皆正心術之謂也孔明曰親賢臣遠小人
先漢所以興隆親小人遠賢臣後漢所以
傾頽李德裕曰致理之道在於辨羣臣之
邪正正人如松栢小人如藤蘿皆辨人材
之謂也斯固其要乎伏望
===
皇上九重之上萬機之餘於夫詩易尚書中庸
通鑑諸書師意以求端省躬以踐實正心
術以爲之本凡天理必行私欲必去而又
行之惟恐不至去之惟恐不盡也辨人材
而爲之助凡君子必進小人必退而又進
之惟恐不先退之惟恐復□也夫然則學
得其要而此心有正而無偏人臣有忠而
無枉行政有是而無瑕天下有理而無亂
可以出於唐虞三代之上漢唐諸君抑每
punctuated: 懼，慎獨以入道，去讒貴德以勸賢，孰有大於正心術、辨人材者耶？若夫《通鑑》所載，大者如董仲舒曰：「正心以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官。」栁公權曰：「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」皆正心術之謂也。孔明曰：「親賢臣，遠小人，先漢所以興隆；親小人，遠賢臣，後漢所以傾頽。」李德裕曰：「致理之道，在於辨羣臣之邪正。正人如松栢，小人如藤蘿。」皆辨人材之謂也。斯固其要乎？伏望皇上九重之上、萬機之餘，於夫《詩》《易》《尚書》《中庸》《通鑑》諸書，師意以求端，省躬以踐實，正心術以爲之本。凡天理必行，私欲必去，而又行之惟恐不至，去之惟恐不盡也。辨人材而爲之助，凡君子必進，小人必退，而又進之惟恐不先，退之惟恐復□也。夫然，則學得其要，而此心有正而無偏，人臣有忠而無枉，行政有是而無瑕，天下有理而無亂，可以出於唐虞三代之上，漢唐諸君抑每
translation_en:
…fear [?]; to enter the Way through vigilance over oneself when alone, and to encourage the worthy by rejecting slander and honoring virtue—what could be more important than rectifying the workings of the mind and discerning men's talents and character? Among the major teachings recorded in the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian), Dong Zhongshu said: “Rectify the mind in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify the hundred officials.” Liu Gongquan said: “The use of the brush lies in the mind: when the mind is upright, the brush is upright.” Both speak of rectifying the workings of the mind. Kongming said: “Drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men at a distance was how the Former Han flourished; drawing close to petty men and keeping worthy ministers at a distance was how the Later Han declined.” Li Deyu said: “The way to achieve good government lies in distinguishing the wicked from the upright among one's ministers. Upright men are like pines and cypresses; petty men are like climbing vines.” Both speak of discerning men's talents and character. Surely these are the essentials?

I humbly hope that Your Majesty, within the innermost palace and amid the intervals between your myriad affairs, will study such books as the Classic of Poetry, the Classic of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Comprehensive Mirror, taking their meaning as your teacher to seek out fundamental principles, examining yourself to put them into practice, and making the rectification of your mind the foundation. Every principle of Heaven must be enacted, and every selfish desire eliminated; moreover, in enacting them, fear only that you may fall short, and in eliminating such desires, fear only that some may remain. Support this by discerning men's talents and character: gentlemen must invariably be advanced and petty men dismissed. Moreover, in advancing the former, fear only that you may not do so soon enough; in dismissing the latter, fear only that they may again □ [?]. If you do this, your learning will grasp its essentials: your mind will be upright and free from bias; your ministers loyal and free from crookedness; your administration correct and free from fault; and the realm well governed and free from disorder. You may thereby surpass even the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, while the rulers of the Han and Tang would each…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
下矣舍是而言要吾見其雜而靡離而陋
皆非所知也雖然難御者心必居敬夫後
可以言正難知者人必窮理夫後可以言
辨不易之理也苟不居敬則濁源以求清
不窮理則反鑑以索照欲其正且辨焉毋
乃不可乎故大居敬貴窮理尤正心術辨
人材之要也執事儻與其進則
大廷之對執此以往矣
第二問
===
同考試官教諭許　批〔脩德弭變雖儒生之常談要之亦止此此爲是洪範庶徵豈欺我哉此策言多剴切足認忠愛謹録之以爲〕
當宁
獻
考試官學正范　批〔条常應變具見才識三秦之良屬之子矣〕
考試官教授林　批〔策警他日立〕
punctuated:
下矣。舍是而言要，吾見其雜而靡、離而陋，皆非所知也。雖然，難御者心，必居敬夫後可以言正；難知者人，必窮理夫後可以言辨，不易之理也。苟不居敬，則濁源以求清；不窮理，則反鑑以索照。欲其正且辨焉，毋乃不可乎？故大居敬貴窮理，尤正心術、辨人材之要也。執事儻與其進，則大廷之對，執此以往矣。
第二問
同考試官教諭許，批〔脩德弭變，雖儒生之常談，要之亦止此，此爲是。《洪範》庶徵，豈欺我哉？此策言多剴切，足認忠愛，謹録之以爲〕當宁獻。
考試官學正范，批〔条常應變，具見才識，三秦之良屬之子矣。〕
考試官教授林，批〔策警，他日立〕
translation_en:
…rank below them. To abandon this and speak of essentials would, in my view, produce only what is confused and insubstantial, disconnected and crude—none of which I can acknowledge as sound. Nevertheless, the mind is difficult to govern: only after maintaining reverence can one speak of rectifying it. People are difficult to know: only after investigating principle exhaustively can one speak of discerning them. These are unchanging principles. Without maintaining reverence, one muddies the source while seeking clear water; without investigating principle exhaustively, one turns a mirror backward while seeking a reflection. Would it not be impossible then to rectify the mind and discern people? Thus, placing great weight on maintaining reverence [?] and valuing the exhaustive investigation of principle are especially essential to rectifying the workings of the mind and discerning men of talent. If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I shall take these principles with me when answering before the imperial court.
Second Question
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Cultivating virtue to avert anomalies may be commonplace talk among Confucian scholars, yet ultimately it comes down to this, and this is correct. Could the ‘Various Verifications’ of the Great Plan deceive us? Much of this policy essay is incisive and pertinent, sufficiently demonstrating the writer’s loyalty and devotion. I respectfully record it as an offering to His Majesty.”
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “In setting out the regular order and responding to changes, he fully displays ability and discernment. This young man deserves to be counted among the outstanding men of the Three Qin region.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “This policy essay is incisive. When in future he takes his place …”

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷黙然而已乎得子可爲是舉慶矣
對天地之道其行也有常度而考之者當
因其已然之迹其變也有異徵而當之者
難諉之適然之數蓋天地之道隱而難究
也其安之而爲常變之而爲異誠有不可
得而忽焉者考其常而參其變使在我者
不迷其感通之故善計天下者可不素定
而豫講之乎請因明問所及而陳之粤自
太極肇分萬象流布爲文于天者有日月
五星之迭運所謂七曜也爲經于地者有
江淮河濟之交流所謂四瀆也然天浮陽
旋轉於外而日月五星逆天而左行故卽
其天體之運轉而其躔度之遲速順逆有
可得而言之者蓋三百六十五度有竒者
固天之數也天行健故日周其數而又過
之日月五星皆隨之以動而惟日之行健
次于天然視天退一度矣月之行又次於
日視天退十三度矣其餘五星之行則又
punctuated:
朝廷，黙然而已乎？得子，可爲是舉慶矣。

對：天地之道，其行也有常度，而考之者當因其已然之迹；其變也有異徵，而當之者難諉之適然之數。蓋天地之道隱而難究也，其安之而爲常，變之而爲異，誠有不可得而忽焉者。考其常而參其變，使在我者不迷其感通之故，善計天下者可不素定而豫講之乎？請因明問所及而陳之。粤自太極肇分，萬象流布，爲文于天者，有日月五星之迭運，所謂七曜也；爲經于地者，有江淮河濟之交流，所謂四瀆也。然天浮陽，旋轉於外，而日月五星逆天而左行，故卽其天體之運轉，而其躔度之遲速順逆，有可得而言之者。蓋三百六十五度有竒者，固天之數也。天行健，故日周其數而又過之。日月五星皆隨之以動，而惟日之行健次于天，然視天退一度矣。月之行又次於日，視天退十三度矣。其餘五星之行則又
translation_en:
…at court, could you merely remain silent? Having found you, we may congratulate ourselves on this examination.

Answer: The Way of Heaven and Earth follows regular measures in its operation, and those who investigate it should rely on the traces of what has already occurred. Its changes manifest unusual signs, and those who encounter them can hardly dismiss them as mere chance. For the Way of Heaven and Earth is hidden and difficult to fathom. Its settled condition constitutes regularity, and its changes constitute anomalies: these are indeed matters that cannot be disregarded. By examining its regularities and comparing its changes, we may avoid misunderstanding the reasons for the interaction and response between ourselves and Heaven and Earth. Can those who plan well for the realm fail to settle their understanding beforehand and discuss these matters in advance? Allow me to set forth my views on the matters raised in your illuminating question.

Ever since the Supreme Ultimate first divided and the myriad phenomena spread forth, the patterns in Heaven have included the successive movements of the sun, moon, and five planets—the so-called Seven Luminaries. The main watercourses on Earth include the interflowing Jiang, Huai, He, and Ji rivers—the so-called Four Waterways. Heaven, however, is buoyant yang, revolving on the outside, while the sun, moon, and five planets move leftward against Heaven [?]. Thus, by considering the revolution of the celestial sphere, one can explain the slowness and speed, and the direct and retrograde motion, of their courses. Three hundred and sixty-five degrees and a fraction are, indeed, Heaven’s allotted number. Heaven moves vigorously, and so each day completes that number and exceeds it. The sun, moon, and five planets all move along with it. Only the sun’s vigor of motion ranks next to Heaven’s; nevertheless, relative to Heaven, it falls behind by one degree. The moon’s motion ranks next to the sun’s, falling behind Heaven by thirteen degrees. As for the motions of the remaining five planets, they in turn…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
各有遲速焉進數順天而左退數逆天而
右而順逆實於此乎見矣地純陰凝聚於
内而江淮河濟就下而東逝故即其地勢
之所在而其源委之曲折隱見有可得而
言者蓋四海九州流派之異趨者水之勢
也江水發源於岷山而東至於澧淮水發
源於桐栢而東會于泗沂自積石至於龍
門東至於底柱以及於大陸者河也自沇
水流爲濟入于河溢爲滎東出於陶丘者
===
濟也其經流之地各有曲折焉伏流隱而
難尋見處顯而易見而隱見實於此乎分
矣夫七曜之在天其行固有常度矣然二
氣之錯行或不能無薄蝕飛流之慘天之
變徵雖微而人事之吉凶每由之大之關
於國家之興亡君臣之禍福次之關於民生
之休戚感應之理誠有不可得而誣者姑
舉其一二言之彗星見西方而商鞅入秦
五星聚東井而漢高興沛七國將變月出
punctuated:
各有遲速焉，進數順天而左，退數逆天而右，而順逆實於此乎見矣。地純陰，凝聚於内，而江淮河濟就下而東逝，故即其地勢之所在，而其源委之曲折隱見，有可得而言者。蓋四海九州流派之異趨者，水之勢也。江水發源於岷山，而東至於澧；淮水發源於桐栢，而東會于泗沂；自積石至於龍門，東至於底柱，以及於大陸者，河也；自沇水流爲濟，入于河，溢爲滎，東出於陶丘者，濟也。其經流之地，各有曲折焉。伏流隱而難尋，見處顯而易見，而隱見實於此乎分矣。
夫七曜之在天，其行固有常度矣。然二氣之錯行，或不能無薄蝕飛流之慘。天之變徵雖微，而人事之吉凶每由之。大之關於國家之興亡、君臣之禍福，次之關於民生之休戚，感應之理誠有不可得而誣者。姑舉其一二言之：彗星見西方，而商鞅入秦；五星聚東井，而漢高興沛；七國將變，月出
translation_en:
…each has its own speed. When their measured positions advance, they follow Heaven to the left; when they retreat, they move against Heaven to the right. Their direct and retrograde motions are thus manifested. Earth is pure yin, condensed within, and the Yangzi, Huai, Yellow, and Ji rivers descend and flow eastward. Thus, by considering the configuration of the land, one can discuss the winding courses of their headwaters and downstream reaches, and where they disappear and reappear. The divergent courses of streams throughout the Four Seas and Nine Provinces reflect water’s natural tendency. The Yangzi rises in Mount Min and reaches Li [?] to the east; the Huai rises in Tongbai and joins the Si and Yi to the east. The river that runs from Jishi to Longmen, eastward to Dizhu, and onward to Dalu is the Yellow River. The river that flows from the Yan River to become the Ji, enters the Yellow River, spills out to form the Xing marsh, and emerges eastward at Taoqiu is the Ji. Each winds through the lands it traverses. Underground streams are hidden and difficult to trace; where they emerge, they are exposed and readily seen. It is here that the distinction between hidden and visible courses becomes apparent.
The seven luminaries in Heaven certainly have regular measures governing their movements. Yet the intermingling movements of the two vital forces, yin and yang, may give rise to the alarming phenomena of occultations, eclipses, and shooting stars. Though the signs of celestial anomalies are subtle, good and ill fortune in human affairs often follow from them. At their greatest, they concern the rise and fall of states and the calamities and blessings of rulers and ministers; at the next level, they concern the well-being and suffering of the people. The principle of stimulus and response truly cannot be denied. Let us mention just one or two examples: a comet appeared in the west, and Shang Yang entered Qin; the five planets gathered in the Eastern Well constellation, and Gaozu of Han rose in Pei; when the Seven Kingdoms were about to rebel, the moon appeared…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
北辰矣大宗靖內太白經天矣他如流星
燭地而夷狄有竊發之虞星孛西方而衣
冠蒙禁錮之慘此其人事吉凶之應固也
四瀆之在地其流固有常道矣然世代之
相仍或不能無騰溢決齧之患地之變徵
雖微而公私之利害實因之上之係於國
家之盛衰君臣之勞逸下之係於民居之
蕩析利害之著誠有不可得而掩者姑舉
其一二言之耿圮於河而殷都遷岷山壅
===
江而西漢滅王莽竊命濟水竭澤矣武后
專制洛水溢河矣他如黃河決而天下爲
厲濟漕通而關中不給此其公私利害之
係固也則是七曜之運四瀆之流或安之
而爲常變之而爲異常者安之而不知變
者避之而不可參常應變恐懼脩省誠有
國者所當究心乎昔胤侯誓師有曰先王
克謹天戒臣人克有常憲而周公之詩亦
曰徹彼桑土綢繆牖戶儆戒相成自古然
punctuated:
北辰矣。大宗靖內，太白經天矣。他如流星燭地，而夷狄有竊發之虞；星孛西方，而衣冠蒙禁錮之慘：此其人事吉凶之應固也。
四瀆之在地，其流固有常道矣。然世代之相仍，或不能無騰溢決齧之患。地之變徵雖微，而公私之利害實因之。上之係於國家之盛衰、君臣之勞逸，下之係於民居之蕩析，利害之著，誠有不可得而掩者。姑舉其一二言之：耿圮於河，而殷都遷；岷山壅江，而西漢滅；王莽竊命，濟水竭澤矣；武后專制，洛水溢河矣。他如黃河決，而天下爲厲；濟漕通，而關中不給：此其公私利害之係固也。
則是七曜之運、四瀆之流，或安之而爲常，變之而爲異。常者安之而不知，變者避之而不可。參常應變，恐懼脩省，誠有國者所當究心乎！昔胤侯誓師有曰：「先王克謹天戒，臣人克有常憲。」而周公之詩亦曰：「徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。」儆戒相成，自古然
translation_en:
…at the Northern Pole. When Emperor Dazong [?] pacified internal disorder, Venus traversed the sky. Other examples include meteors illuminating the earth, portending the danger of sudden incursions by non-Chinese peoples, and a comet appearing in the west, when men of official standing suffered the calamity of exclusion from office. Such, indeed, are the correspondences between these phenomena and good or ill fortune in human affairs.
The Four Great Watercourses on earth ordinarily follow fixed channels. Yet as successive ages pass, they cannot always be free of surging floods, breached banks, and erosion. Although the portents of terrestrial change may be subtle, benefits and harms to public and private interests actually depend upon them. Above, they bear upon the flourishing or decline of the state and the toil or ease of ruler and ministers; below, upon the destruction of people’s homes and their dispersal. Their beneficial and harmful effects are so evident that they truly cannot be concealed. Let us cite one or two examples: Geng was destroyed by the Yellow River, and the Yin capital was moved; a blockage of the Yangzi at Mount Min preceded the fall of the Western Han. When Wang Mang usurped the mandate, the Ji River and its marshes dried up [?]; when Empress Wu exercised sole rule, the Luo River overflowed its channel [?]. Other examples include the Yellow River breaching its banks and bringing calamity upon the realm, and grain transport along the Ji flowing freely while Guanzhong lacked supplies [?]. Such, indeed, is their bearing upon public and private benefit and harm.
Thus the movements of the Seven Luminaries and the flow of the Four Great Watercourses are normal when they remain settled, and anomalous when they change. People take normal conditions for granted without understanding them; when changes occur, they try to evade them but cannot. To examine the normal and respond to change, to cultivate oneself and reflect upon one’s conduct in fear and apprehension—surely these are matters to which those who rule a state should devote their minds! In former times, the Marquis of Yin declared in his charge to the troops: “The former kings were scrupulously attentive to Heaven’s warnings; their ministers duly observed constant laws.” A poem by the Duke of Zhou likewise says: “Strip the bark from those mulberry roots, and bind fast the windows and doors.” Admonition and vigilance complement one another; this has been so since ancient times…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也我
皇上以至聖之德際中興之運
臨御以來憂勤惕厲不遑寧處凡所以脩德
弭變者無乎不至固宜七曜循軌而乾符
無反正之愆四瀆安流而坤輿無失馭之
或矣然而
天心仁愛每寓於譴告之中而天災地沴或關
人事或係公私守臣之所
奏報言官之所論列時有聞於中外若此者
===
豈非欲
聖德日進於無疆歟是知恐懼脩省在今日尤
所當究心而未可諉之適然之數也殆必
肅然於未變之前而竦然於遇變之日凡
其所以夙夜祇懼以感格天心者不徒崇
徹樂減膳之虛文而必孚之以實德如洪
範之五事能脩也雲漢之八章能舉也則
災者且將轉而爲祥矣否則將翫之以爲
常吾之瀆慢方深而彼之酷烈愈熾其如
punctuated: 也。我皇上以至聖之德，際中興之運，臨御以來，憂勤惕厲，不遑寧處。凡所以脩德弭變者，無乎不至。固宜七曜循軌，而乾符無反正之愆；四瀆安流，而坤輿無失馭之或矣。然而天心仁愛，每寓於譴告之中，而天災地沴，或關人事，或係公私，守臣之所奏報、言官之所論列，時有聞於中外。若此者，豈非欲聖德日進於無疆歟？是知恐懼脩省，在今日尤所當究心，而未可諉之適然之數也。殆必肅然於未變之前，而竦然於遇變之日。凡其所以夙夜祇懼，以感格天心者，不徒崇徹樂減膳之虛文，而必孚之以實德。如洪範之五事能脩也，雲漢之八章能舉也，則災者且將轉而爲祥矣。否則，將翫之以爲常，吾之瀆慢方深，而彼之酷烈愈熾，其如
translation_en:
…so it has been. Our August Emperor, possessing the virtue of supreme sagehood, has met with an age of dynastic resurgence. Since ascending the throne, he has labored anxiously and remained vigilant, allowing himself no time for repose. He has left nothing undone in cultivating virtue and averting portents of calamity. Surely, then, the Seven Luminaries should follow their courses, with no deviation from proper order in Heaven’s signs [?]; the Four Watercourses should flow peacefully, with no possibility of the earth slipping beyond control. Yet Heaven’s benevolent concern is often conveyed through reprimands and warnings. Heavenly disasters and earthly disturbances, sometimes connected with human affairs and sometimes involving public or private interests, are reported in memorials by territorial officials and discussed by remonstrance officials; accounts of them are heard from time to time at court and in the provinces. Is this not because Heaven wishes the Emperor’s sagely virtue to advance daily without limit?

Thus we know that fearful vigilance, self-cultivation, and self-examination especially demand earnest attention today. These events must not be dismissed as mere chance workings of fate. One must surely remain reverent before an abnormal event occurs and stand in awe when it arrives. In maintaining reverent fear morning and night to move Heaven’s heart, one must not merely esteem the empty formalities of suspending music and reducing meals, but must establish sincerity through genuine virtue. If the Five Activities set out in the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) can be cultivated, and the teachings of the eight stanzas of “The Milky Way” (Yunhan) put into practice, disasters will turn into auspicious blessings. Otherwise, if we treat them lightly as ordinary occurrences, our irreverence and negligence will deepen while their destructive force grows ever fiercer. How then shall we deal with…

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國患何哉寤寐隄防以綱維地道者不徒
爲鑿渠障流之近功而必行之以大計如
賈讓之三策能用也蘇子之水學能行也
則沴者且將反而爲福矣否則恃之以無
恐吾之怠弛方仍而彼之奔潰愈甚其如
民靑何哉唐魏徵因旱暵欲太宗脩省乃
曰禍福無門惟人所召人無釁焉妖不妄
作蓋以天人之交感應之理微妙莫測惟
反躬自咎庶乎可回爾是豈無所見而云
===
乎夫畏天者興習天者亡雖儒生之常談
而今日弭變之道端不外此幸進而教之
第三問
曹士奇
同考試官教諭冀　批〔洋洋正論至誠惻怛之意眞若可掬憂時愛國慨焉深矣子之言得行天下國家之福也〕
考試官學正范　批〔秦中山川雄奇閎壯故士生於中多負剛直之氣子固其人耶〕
punctuated:
國患何哉？寤寐隄防，以綱維地道者，不徒爲鑿渠障流之近功，而必行之以大計。如賈讓之三策能用也，蘇子之水學能行也，則沴者且將反而爲福矣。否則恃之以無恐，吾之怠弛方仍，而彼之奔潰愈甚，其如民靑何哉？唐魏徵因旱暵欲太宗脩省，乃曰：「禍福無門，惟人所召。人無釁焉，妖不妄作。」蓋以天人之交，感應之理微妙莫測，惟反躬自咎，庶乎可回爾。是豈無所見而云乎？夫畏天者興，習天者亡，雖儒生之常談，而今日弭變之道，端不外此。幸進而教之。
第三問
曹士奇
同考試官教諭冀批〔洋洋正論，至誠惻怛之意眞若可掬，憂時愛國，慨焉深矣！子之言得行，天下國家之福也。〕
考試官學正范批〔秦中山川雄奇閎壯，故士生於中，多負剛直之氣。子固其人耶？〕
translation_en:
…what, then, can be done about the calamities afflicting the state? To remain vigilant, waking and sleeping, and safeguard the workings of the earth requires more than the immediate achievements of digging channels and damming currents: comprehensive plans must be put into effect. If Jia Rang’s three strategies can be employed and Master Su’s teachings on water management implemented, destructive forces will turn into blessings. Otherwise, relying on a supposed absence of danger, we will persist in negligence while the waters rush and burst forth ever more violently. What, then, of the people [?; the transcription reads 民靑]?
During a drought in the Tang dynasty, Wei Zheng wished Emperor Taizong to cultivate himself and examine his conduct. He therefore said: “Calamity and good fortune have no fixed gate; people themselves summon them. When people are without fault, ominous phenomena do not arise without cause.” For in the intercourse between Heaven and humanity, the principles of stimulus and response are subtle and unfathomable. Only by examining oneself and acknowledging one’s faults may one hope to reverse the situation. Could he have spoken thus without insight? Those who fear Heaven flourish; those who grow accustomed to it perish. Although this is a commonplace among Confucian scholars, the means of averting calamities today lie precisely here. I hope you will come forward and instruct me.
Third Question
Cao Shiqi
Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: 〔An expansive and upright argument! Its utter sincerity and compassionate concern seem almost tangible. How profound your indignation, your concern for the times, and your love of country! If your words could be put into practice, it would be a blessing for all under Heaven and for the state.〕
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔The mountains and rivers of Qinzhong are imposing, extraordinary, vast, and magnificent. Thus scholars born there often possess a firm and upright spirit. Are you indeed such a man?〕

title: 嘉靖四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批　昔賢謂希文做秀
才時便理會天下事于子亦云
人臣果貴于和乎曰忠臣不和不貴于和
也抑貴于不和乎曰同寅和衷不貴于不
和也非不貴于和也不貴于和而同也非
不貴于不和也不貴于不和而爭也夫閧
辨難之端以定國是者是謂之不和持求
勝之心以快己私者亦爭爾非不和也不
和公也進而極辨退而交懽始而相非終
===
而相濟又何害其爲和而不同者耶爭私
也怒于室色于市訟于朝若讐若水火然
不至甘心不已也是故不和與爭公私之
間也君子于是乎存公天下國家之心是
非之公吾不和勝負之私吾不爭則和讓
之風蔚然興矣執事之意蓋以不和憂天
下國家者也愚生以爲不和不足憂也爭
斯憂之至大者歟自夫虞廷師師岳牧有
相讓之美周官董正庶官有乃和之風邈
punctuated:
考試官教授林批：昔賢謂希文做秀才時，便理會天下事，于子亦云。

人臣果貴于和乎？曰：「忠臣不和。」不貴于和也。抑貴于不和乎？曰：「同寅和衷。」不貴于不和也。非不貴于和也，不貴于和而同也；非不貴于不和也，不貴于不和而爭也。夫閧辨難之端以定國是者，是謂之不和；持求勝之心以快己私者，亦爭爾，非不和也。不和，公也。進而極辨，退而交懽；始而相非，終而相濟，又何害其爲和而不同者耶？爭，私也。怒于室，色于市，訟于朝，若讐，若水火然，不至甘心不已也。是故不和與爭，公私之間也。君子于是乎存公天下國家之心：是非之公，吾不和；勝負之私，吾不爭。則和讓之風蔚然興矣。執事之意，蓋以不和憂天下國家者也。愚生以爲不和不足憂也，爭斯憂之至大者歟！自夫虞廷師師，岳牧有相讓之美；周官董正，庶官有乃和之風，邈
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “A worthy of former times said that Xiwen, while still a student, already concerned himself with the affairs of the realm. The same may be said of you.”

Is harmony truly what should be prized in a minister? It is said, “Loyal ministers do not harmonize.” Thus harmony is not what is prized. Or is disharmony what should be prized? It is said, “Be united in reverence and harmonious in purpose.” Thus disharmony is not what is prized either. It is not that harmony is unworthy of esteem; what is unworthy is harmony that amounts to mere conformity. It is not that disharmony is unworthy of esteem; what is unworthy is disharmony that becomes contention. To open up matters for disputation and challenge [?] in order to settle the proper course of state policy is what is called disharmony. To harbor a desire to prevail so as to gratify one’s private interests is merely contention, not disharmony.

Disharmony serves the public good. At court, men debate to the utmost; away from court, they enjoy friendly relations. At first they criticize one another; in the end they assist one another. How does this prevent them from being harmonious without merely conforming? Contention serves private interests. Men rage in their chambers, display their anger in the marketplace, and dispute at court, treating one another as enemies, as incompatible as fire and water. They will not stop until their resentment is satisfied. Thus the distinction between disharmony and contention lies between public and private interests. Here the gentleman preserves a heart devoted to the common good of the realm and the state: where the public question of right and wrong is concerned, I will disagree; where the private matter of winning and losing is concerned, I will not contend. Then a spirit of harmony and deference will flourish abundantly.

Your intent, honored examiner, is presumably to express concern for the realm and the state on account of disharmony.
